  227| 
  228| /// Complete backing-store scale after the global governor/override and the
  229| /// selected renderer's own bounded workload factor are composed.
  230| fn effective_resolution_scale(renderer: &DriverRenderer, governor_scale: f32) -> f64 {
  231|     let forced =
  232|         f32::from_bits(crate::RENDER_SCALE_BITS.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed));
  233|     let global_scale = if forced > 0.0 {
  234|         forced as f64
  235|     } else {
  236|         governor_scale as f64
  237|     };
  238|     global_scale * renderer.resolution_factor()
  239| }
  240| 
  241| /// Engine owns its renderer behind the port; the driver also needs to call
  242| /// `resize` on the concrete type. This thin adapter shares one renderer
  243| /// between both without widening the port.
  244| struct SharedRenderer(Rc<RefCell<DriverRenderer>>);
  245| 
  246| impl RendererPort for SharedRenderer {
  247|     fn artifact_needs(&self) -> RenderArtifactNeeds {
  248|         self.0.borrow().artifact_needs()
  249|     }
  250| 
  251|     fn uses_surface_meshes(&self) -> bool {
  252|         self.0.borrow().uses_surface_meshes()
  253|     }
  254|     fn upload_surfaces(&mut self, chunks: &[SurfaceChunk<'_>]) {
  255|         self.0.borrow_mut().upload_surfaces(chunks);
  256|     }
  257|     fn remove_surfaces(&mut self, keys: &[SurfaceChunkKey]) {
  258|         self.0.borrow_mut().remove_surfaces(keys);
  259|     }
  260|     fn clear_surfaces(&mut self) {
  261|         self.0.borrow_mut().clear_surfaces();
  262|     }
  263|     fn cpu_telemetry_string(&self) -> Option<String> {
  264|         self.0.borrow().cpu_telemetry_string()
  265|     }
  266|     fn upload_atlas(&mut self, texels: &[u32]) {
  267|         self.0.borrow_mut().upload_atlas(texels);
  268|     }
  269|     fn upload_atlas_rows(&mut self, first_row: u32, texels: &[u32]) -> bool {
  270|         self.0.borrow_mut().upload_atlas_rows(first_row, texels)
  271|     }
  272|     fn draw(&mut self, frame: &FrameParams, chunks: &[ChunkDraw]) {
  273|         self.0.borrow_mut().draw(frame, chunks);
  274|     }
  275|     fn upload_label_atlas(&mut self, rgba: &[u8], width: u32, height: u32) {
  276|         self.0.borrow_mut().upload_label_atlas(rgba, width, height);
  277|     }
  278| }
  279| 
  280| /// The embedded product-label atlas: row 0 almond water, row 1 rations.
  281| /// The rations row stays transparent until a rations logo lands in
  282| /// `wasm_frontend/assets/` and gets blitted here.
  283| fn build_label_atlas() -> Option<(Vec<u8>, u32, u32)> {
  284|     const ALMOND_LABEL_PNG: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../../assets/almond_water_label.png");
  285|     let label = image::load_from_memory(ALMOND_LABEL_PNG).ok()?.to_rgba8();
  286|     let (width, row_height) = label.dimensions();
  287|     let mut atlas = vec![0u8; (width * row_height * 2 * 4) as usize];
  288|     atlas[..(width * row_height * 4) as usize].copy_from_slice(label.as_raw());
  289|     Some((atlas, width, row_height * 2))
  290| }
  291| 
  292| /// Saved backend preference, written by the Settings menu. Query params
  293| /// always win so shared links stay exact reproductions.
  294| fn stored_backend_pref(window: &Window) -> Option<String> {
  295|     window
  296|         .local_storage()
  297|         .ok()
  298|         .flatten()
  299|         .and_then(|storage| storage.get_item("vackrooms_backend").ok())
  300|         .flatten()
  301| }
  302| 
  303| /// Backend, then renderer, selection.
  304| ///
  305| /// Backend: `?backend=auto|webgl|webgpu` > saved preference > automatic.
  306| /// Automatic mode uses standards-based WebGPU when a secure browser context
  307| /// exposes a usable adapter, otherwise it retains WebGL2 as the compatibility
  308| /// floor. Renderer within the backend follows `?renderer=`.
  309| async fn create_renderer(
  310|     window: &Window,
  311|     canvas: &HtmlCanvasElement,
  312|     status_msg: &HtmlElement,
  313|     query: &str,
  314|     quality: GpuQualityProfile,
  315| ) -> Result<DriverRenderer, JsValue> {
  316|     let backend = query_param(query, "backend")
  317|         .map(str::to_owned)
  318|         .or_else(|| stored_backend_pref(window))
  319|         .unwrap_or_else(|| "auto".to_owned());
  320|     // Surfels are a WebGL2-only renderer for now: the WebGPU `SurfelPipeline`
  321|     // exists but nothing selects it. This is decided before the preflight
  322|     // rather than after, for two reasons. `?renderer=surfel` would otherwise
  323|     // parse to `None` on a WebGPU-capable browser and quietly render
  324|     // *surfaces* — the worst outcome, because the wrong renderer looks like
  325|     // the right one having a bad day. And `?backend=webgpu` propagates a
  326|     // preflight failure as a hard error, which would be an odd way for a
  327|     // renderer that never touches WebGPU to fail.
  328|     let wants_surfel = query_param(query, "renderer") == Some("surfel");
  329|     if wants_surfel && backend != "webgl" {
  330|         web_sys::console::warn_1(&JsValue::from_str(
  331|             "the surfel renderer is WebGL2-only; ignoring the requested backend",
  332|         ));
  333|     }
  334|     let use_webgpu = if wants_surfel {
  335|         false
  336|     } else if backend == "webgpu" {
  337|         webgpu_preflight(window, status_msg).await?;
  338|         true
  339|     } else if backend == "auto" {
  340|         match webgpu_preflight(window, status_msg).await {
  341|             Ok(()) => true,
  342|             Err(_) => {
  343|                 status_msg.set_text_content(Some("Generating world in WebAssembly…"));
  344|                 false
  345|             }
  346|         }
  347|     } else {
  348|         false
  349|     };
  350|     if use_webgpu {
  351|         let requested = query_param(query, "renderer").and_then(RendererKind::parse);
  352|         return WebGpuRenderer::new_auto(canvas, requested, quality)
  353|             .await
  354|             .map(DriverRenderer::WebGpu);
  355|     }
  356| 
  357|     let renderer_choice = query_param(query, "renderer");
  358|     if renderer_choice == Some("cpu") {
  359|         return Ok(DriverRenderer::Cpu(CpuCanvasRenderer::new(canvas)?));
  360|     }
  361|     if renderer_choice == Some("raymarch") {
  362|         // Default on; `?bricks=0` selects the plain SVDAG encoding instead.
  363|         let bricks = query_param(query, "bricks") != Some("0");
  364|         return WebGl2Renderer::with_bricks(canvas, bricks).map(DriverRenderer::Raymarch);
  365|     }
  366|     if renderer_choice == Some("surfel") {
  367|         let profile = if quality == GpuQualityProfile::High {
  368|             SurfelProfile::high()
  369|         } else {
  370|             SurfelProfile::low()
  371|         };
  372|         match SurfelRenderer::new(canvas, profile) {
  373|             Ok(gpu) => return Ok(DriverRenderer::Surfel(gpu)),
  374|             Err(err) => {
  375|                 web_sys::console::warn_2(
  376|                     &JsValue::from_str(
  377|                         "surfel renderer unavailable, falling back to surface meshes:",
  378|                     ),
  379|                     &err,
  380|                 );
  381|             }
  382|         }
  383|     }
  384|     if renderer_choice == Some("splat") {
  385|         let profile = if quality == GpuQualityProfile::High {
  386|             SplatProfile::high()
  387|         } else {
  388|             SplatProfile::low()
  389|         };
  390|         match SplatRenderer::new(canvas, profile) {
  391|             Ok(gpu) => return Ok(DriverRenderer::Splat(gpu)),
  392|             Err(err) => {
  393|                 web_sys::console::warn_2(
  394|                     &JsValue::from_str(
  395|                         "splat renderer unavailable, falling back to surface meshes:",
  396|                     ),
  397|                     &err,
  398|                 );
  399|             }
  400|         }
  401|     }
  402|     match SurfaceRenderer::new(canvas) {
  403|         Ok(gpu) => Ok(DriverRenderer::Surface(gpu)),
  404|         Err(err) => {
  405|             web_sys::console::warn_2(
  406|                 &JsValue::from_str(
  407|                     "WebGL2 surface renderer unavailable, falling back to CPU splatting:",
  408|                 ),
  409|                 &err,
  410|             );
  411|             Ok(DriverRenderer::Cpu(CpuCanvasRenderer::new(canvas)?))
  412|         }
  413|     }
  414| }
  415| 
  416| /// Preflight for the WebGPU backend: failures inside wgpu's surface
  417| /// and adapter glue are unactionable (`getContext` null, or an uncaught
  418| /// TypeError when `requestAdapter` resolves to null — seen on mobile
  419| /// Chrome), so probe both layers first and put concrete guidance in the
  420| /// loading HUD. WebGL2 boots never run this.
  421| async fn webgpu_preflight(window: &Window, status_msg: &HtmlElement) -> Result<(), JsValue> {
  422|     let gpu = js_sys::Reflect::get(&window.navigator(), &JsValue::from_str("gpu"))
  423|         .unwrap_or(JsValue::UNDEFINED);
  424|     if gpu.is_undefined() || gpu.is_null() {
  425|         // WebGPU only exists in secure contexts, so a plain-http LAN address
  426|         // (phone pointed at a dev box) hides navigator.gpu even in browsers
  427|         // that fully support it. Distinguish that from a browser gap.
  428|         let msg = if !window.is_secure_context() {
  429|             "WebGPU requires a secure context and this page was loaded over \
  430|              plain HTTP. Serve it via https or localhost, or switch the \
  431|              backend setting back to WebGL2."
  432|         } else {
  433|             "WebGPU is not available in this browser (navigator.gpu is missing). \
  434|              Use Chrome/Edge 113+ or Safari 18+, or switch the backend \
  435|              setting back to WebGL2."
  436|         };
  437|         status_msg.set_text_content(Some(msg));
  438|         return Err(JsValue::from_str(msg));
  439|     }
  440|     if !probe_webgpu_adapter(&gpu).await {
  441|         let msg = "This device exposes WebGPU but reports no usable graphics \
  442|                    adapter. Check hardware acceleration (chrome://gpu), or \
  443|                    switch the backend setting back to WebGL2.";
  444|         status_msg.set_text_content(Some(msg));
  445|         return Err(JsValue::from_str(msg));
  446|     }
  447|     Ok(())
  448| }
  449| 
  450| /// Asks `navigator.gpu.requestAdapter()` directly whether any adapter
  451| /// exists. wgpu's generated bindings assume the resolved adapter is
  452| /// non-null and crash (`null.info`) before our error handling runs, so
  453| /// this duplicate one-off request is the only way to fail politely.
  454| async fn probe_webgpu_adapter(gpu: &JsValue) -> bool {
  455|     let request = match js_sys::Reflect::get(gpu, &JsValue::from_str("requestAdapter"))
  456|         .ok()
  457|         .and_then(|value| value.dyn_into::<js_sys::Function>().ok())
  458|     {
  459|         Some(function) => function,
  460|         None => return false,
  461|     };
  462|     let promise = match request
  463|         .call0(gpu)
  464|         .ok()
  465|         .and_then(|value| value.dyn_into::<js_sys::Promise>().ok())
  466|     {
  467|         Some(promise) => promise,
  468|         None => return false,
  469|     };
  470|     match wasm_bindgen_futures::JsFuture::from(promise).await {
  471|         Ok(adapter) => !adapter.is_null() && !adapter.is_undefined(),
  472|         Err(_) => false,
  473|     }
  474| }
  475| 
  476| pub async fn boot() -> Result<(), JsValue> {
  477|     let window = web_sys::window().ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("no window"))?;
  478|     let document = window
  479|         .document()
  480|         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("no document"))?;
  481| 
  482|     let canvas: HtmlCanvasElement =
  483|         element(&document, "view").or_else(|_| element(&document, "game-canvas"))?;
  484|     let overlay: HtmlElement = element(&document, "overlay")?;
  485|     let status_msg: HtmlElement = element(&document, "status-msg")?;
  486|     let play_msg: HtmlElement = element(&document, "play-msg")?;
  487| 
  488|     // ?spec=high -> 20u chunks, 5x5 streaming radius, 0.1u voxels.
  489|     // Default is the low-spec profile: 10u chunks, 3x3 radius, 0.2u voxels.
  490|     // Generation controls: ?seed=… (number or any text) plus the density
  491|     // knobs ?pillars= ?walls= ?atria= ?lights= (multipliers, default 1).
  492|     let query = window.location().search().unwrap_or_default();
  493|     web_sys::console::log_1(&format!("BOOTING ENGINE: query={}", query).into());
  494|     // Renderer optimization switchboard (?rt_<name>=0|1); see
  495|     // application::render_settings for the catalog of switches.
  496|     crate::init_render_toggles(&query);
  497|     // This resolver is also called inside every worker. Keeping the actual
  498|     // GeneratorConfig behind one adapter prevents a rejected voxel override
  499|     // from producing different worlds on the main and worker threads.
  500|     let quality = quality_profile_from_query(&query);
  501|     let (resolved_seed, generator_config) =
  502|         generator_setup_for_quality(&query, WORLD_SEED, quality);
  503|     let high_spec = quality == GpuQualityProfile::High;
  504|     // Spawn on the main corridor of region (0,0), looking east down its
  505|     // west leg: the first frame is a lit, walled corridor receding into
  506|     // fog — the player knows immediately that this is the Backrooms.
  507|     let spawn_at = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::spawn_point(resolved_seed);
  508|     let spawn = [spawn_at.x, 1.7, spawn_at.z];
  509|     // Face east along +X.
  510|     let spawn_yaw = -std::f32::consts::FRAC_PI_2;
  511|     // ?level=34 boots straight into the grassland (debugging any level in
  512|     // any renderer without waiting on a noclip roll).
  513|     let initial_level = query_param(&query, "level")
  514|         .and_then(|v| v.parse::<u32>().ok())
  515|         .unwrap_or(0);
  516|     let engine_config = if high_spec {
  517|         EngineConfig {
  518|             chunk_size: generator_config.chunk_size,
  519|             chunk_radius: 2,
  520|             seed: resolved_seed,
  521|             spawn,
  522|             spawn_yaw,
  523|             // High spec's 20 u chunks cost ~3.2 MB of mesh each at full
  524|             // resolution, against 252 KB for a low-spec 10 u chunk, so its
  525|             // ladder is pulled in: the same 120 u reach costs ~110 MB here
  526|             // and ~30 MB there. Reaching the low-spec 155 u would roughly
  527|             // double it for detail the fog has already taken.
  528|             lod: LodLadder {
  529|                 fine_distance: 25.0,
  530|                 mid_distance: 60.0,
  531|                 far_distance: 120.0,
  532|             },
  533|             initial_level,
  534|             ..EngineConfig::default()
  535|         }
  536|     } else {
  537|         EngineConfig {
  538|             chunk_size: generator_config.chunk_size,
  539|             seed: resolved_seed,
  540|             spawn,
  541|             spawn_yaw,
  542|             initial_level,
  543|             ..EngineConfig::default()
  544|         }
  545|     };
  546| 
  547|     let renderer = Rc::new(RefCell::new(
  548|         create_renderer(&window, &canvas, &status_msg, &query, quality).await?,
  549|     ));
  550|     if let Some((label_rgba, label_w, label_h)) = build_label_atlas() {
  551|         renderer
  552|             .borrow_mut()
  553|             .upload_label_atlas(&label_rgba, label_w, label_h);
  554|     }
  555|     if let Ok(hud_renderer) = element::<HtmlElement>(&document, "hud-renderer") {
  556|         hud_renderer.set_text_content(Some(renderer.borrow().label()));
  557|     }
  558|     // Names the section the player is standing in (top-right HUD). The
  559|     // locator re-derives the deterministic region plan, cached per region.
  560|     let locator = Rc::new(RefCell::new(SectionLocator::new(
  561|         resolved_seed,
  562|         generator_config,
  563|     )));
  564|     // This pool parallelizes chunk generation/lighting/SVO construction,
  565|     // never the renderer. The pure policy reserves the main thread and
  566|     // clamps explicit requests to reported hardware. Zero selects the
  567|     // synchronous source, which is also the worker-startup fallback.
  568|     let worker_preference = parse_generation_worker_preference(&query);
  569|     let hardware_concurrency = window.navigator().hardware_concurrency();
  570|     let generation_worker_count = worker_preference.resolve(hardware_concurrency);
  571|     let source: Box<dyn crate::application::ports::ChunkSourcePort> =
  572|         if generation_worker_count == 0 {
  573|             web_sys::console::log_1(&"chunk generation: synchronous main thread".into());
  574|             Box::new(
  575|                 LocalChunkSource::with_telemetry(
  576|                     SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
  577|                     resolved_seed,
  578|                     generator_config,
  579|                     &CONSOLE_TELEMETRY,
  580|                 )
  581|                 .with_surfel_density(surfel_density_from_query(&query)),
  582|             )
  583|         } else {
  584|             match crate::drivers::worker_source::WorkerChunkSource::new(
  585|                 &query,
  586|                 WORLD_SEED,
  587|                 generation_worker_count,
  588|             ) {
  589|                 Ok(pool) => {
  590|                     web_sys::console::log_1(
  591|                         &format!("chunk generation: {} worker threads", pool.pool_size()).into(),
  592|                     );
  593|                     Box::new(pool)
  594|                 }
  595|                 Err(err) => {
  596|                     web_sys::console::warn_2(
  597|                         &JsValue::from_str(
  598|                             "worker pool unavailable, falling back to in-thread generation:",
  599|                         ),
  600|                         &err,
  601|                     );
  602|                     Box::new(
  603|                         LocalChunkSource::with_telemetry(
  604|                             SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
  605|                             resolved_seed,
  606|                             generator_config,
  607|                             &CONSOLE_TELEMETRY,
  608|                         )
  609|                         .with_surfel_density(surfel_density_from_query(&query)),
  610|                     )
  611|                 }
  612|             }
  613|         };
  614|     let engine = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Engine::new(
  615|         engine_config,
  616|         Box::new(SharedRenderer(renderer.clone())),
  617|         source,
  618|     )));
  619|     let input = Rc::new(RefCell::new(InputCollector::new()));
  620|     let touch = Rc::new(RefCell::new(TouchState::default()));
  621| 
  622|     attach_input_listeners(&document, &canvas, &overlay, &input, &touch)?;
  623|     attach_touch_listeners(&document, &canvas, &overlay, &input, &touch)?;
  624|     run_frame_loop(
  625|         window, document, canvas, overlay, status_msg, play_msg, renderer, engine, input, locator,
  626|     )
  627| }
  628| 
  629| /// Renders the engine's `§`-sectioned diagnostic report as aperture panels.
  630| /// Body lines are escaped; only the fixed panel scaffolding is markup.
  631| fn diagnostic_sections_html(report: &str) -> String {
  632|     fn escape(text: &str) -> String {
  633|         text.replace('&', "&amp;")
  634|             .replace('<', "&lt;")
  635|             .replace('>', "&gt;")
  636|     }
  637|     let mut html = String::with_capacity(report.len() + 256);
  638|     let mut open = false;
  639|     for line in report.lines() {
  640|         if let Some(title) = line.strip_prefix("§ ") {
  641|             if open {
  642|                 html.push_str("</pre></section>");
  643|             }
  644|             html.push_str("<section class=\"diag-section\"><h4>");
  645|             html.push_str(&escape(title));
  646|             html.push_str("</h4><pre>");
  647|             open = true;
  648|         } else if open {
  649|             html.push_str(&escape(line));
  650|             html.push('\n');
  651|         } else {
  652|             // Preamble lines before the first section header.
  653|             html.push_str("<section class=\"diag-section\"><pre>");
  654|             html.push_str(&escape(line));
  655|             html.push('\n');
  656|             open = true;
  657|         }
  658|     }
  659|     if open {
  660|         html.push_str("</pre></section>");
  661|     }
  662|     html
  663| }
  664| 
  665| fn element<T: JsCast>(document: &Document, id: &str) -> Result<T, JsValue> {
  666|     document
  667|         .get_element_by_id(id)
  668|         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str(&format!("missing #{id} element")))?
  669|         .dyn_into::<T>()
  670|         .map_err(|_| JsValue::from_str(&format!("#{id} has unexpected element type")))
  671| }

    1| //! Conservative finite-range fixture clustering for a world-space AABB.
    2| //!
    3| //! Both rewritten GPU paths use this exact predicate. It removes work, not
    4| //! light: a fixture is omitted only when no point on its rectangle can be
    5| //! within its compact-support range of any receiver in the bounds.
    6| 
    7| use crate::application::ports::LightSource;
    8| 
    9| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   10| pub struct LightRange {
   11|     pub first: i32,
   12|     pub count: i32,
   13| }
   14| 
   15| pub fn append_lights_reaching_bounds(
   16|     lights: &[LightSource],
   17|     bounds_min: [f32; 3],
   18|     bounds_max: [f32; 3],
   19|     clustered: &mut Vec<LightSource>,
   20| ) -> LightRange {
   21|     let first = clustered.len();
   22|     clustered.extend(
   23|         lights
   24|             .iter()
   25|             .copied()
   26|             .filter(|light| reaches_bounds(light, bounds_min, bounds_max)),
   27|     );
   28|     LightRange {
   29|         first: first.min(i32::MAX as usize) as i32,
   30|         count: clustered.len().saturating_sub(first).min(i32::MAX as usize) as i32,
   31|     }
   32| }
   33| 
   34| fn reaches_bounds(light: &LightSource, bounds_min: [f32; 3], bounds_max: [f32; 3]) -> bool {
   35|     // Expanding X/Z by the emitter half-size converts rectangle-to-box
   36|     // distance into point-to-box distance (the Minkowski-sum construction).
   37|     let expanded_min = [
   38|         bounds_min[0] - light.half_size[0],
   39|         bounds_min[1],
   40|         bounds_min[2] - light.half_size[1],
   41|     ];
   42|     let expanded_max = [
   43|         bounds_max[0] + light.half_size[0],
   44|         bounds_max[1],
   45|         bounds_max[2] + light.half_size[1],
   46|     ];
   47|     let mut distance_squared = 0.0;
   48|     for axis in 0..3 {
   49|         let delta = if light.position[axis] < expanded_min[axis] {
   50|             expanded_min[axis] - light.position[axis]
   51|         } else if light.position[axis] > expanded_max[axis] {
   52|             light.position[axis] - expanded_max[axis]
   53|         } else {
   54|             0.0
   55|         };
   56|         distance_squared += delta * delta;
   57|     }
   58|     distance_squared <= light.radius * light.radius
   59| }
   60| 
   61| /// Persistent cache for per-chunk top-K light selection with hysteresis.
   62| ///
   63| /// # Rationale & Design Pattern (Observer & Strategy Pattern)
   64| /// Prevents light popping across chunk seams when camera movement or floating point sorting
   65| /// slight changes candidate light order. A candidate replaces an existing selected light only
   66| /// if its calculated importance score exceeds the existing light's score by at least 20%.
   67| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
   68| pub struct LightSelectionCache {
   69|     entries: std::collections::HashMap<crate::application::ports::SurfaceChunkKey, Vec<u64>>,
   70| }
   71| 
   72| impl LightSelectionCache {
   73|     pub fn new() -> Self {
   74|         Self {
   75|             entries: std::collections::HashMap::new(),
   76|         }
   77|     }
   78| 
   79|     /// Ranks lights reaching bounds and applies a hysteresis filter against previous frame selection.
   80|     pub fn select_lights_with_hysteresis(
   81|         &mut self,
   82|         key: crate::application::ports::SurfaceChunkKey,
   83|         candidate_lights: &[LightSource],
   84|         bounds_min: [f32; 3],
   85|         bounds_max: [f32; 3],
   86|         top_k: usize,
   87|     ) -> Vec<LightSource> {
   88|         let center = [
   89|             (bounds_min[0] + bounds_max[0]) * 0.5,
   90|             (bounds_min[1] + bounds_max[1]) * 0.5,
   91|             (bounds_min[2] + bounds_max[2]) * 0.5,
   92|         ];
   93| 
   94|         // Rank candidates by estimated irradiance score = intensity / (distance_sq + 1.0)
   95|         let mut scored: Vec<(f32, &LightSource)> = candidate_lights
   96|             .iter()
   97|             .map(|light| {
   98|                 let dx = light.position[0] - center[0];
   99|                 let dy = light.position[1] - center[1];
  100|                 let dz = light.position[2] - center[2];
  101|                 let dist_sq = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz;
  102|                 let score = light.intensity / (dist_sq + 1.0);
  103|                 (score, light)
  104|             })
  105|             .collect();
  106|         scored.sort_by(|a, b| b.0.partial_cmp(&a.0).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
  107| 
  108|         let previous_ids = self.entries.get(&key);
  109|         let mut selected = Vec::with_capacity(top_k.min(scored.len()));
  110| 
  111|         for (score, light) in scored {
  112|             if selected.len() >= top_k {
  113|                 break;
  114|             }
  115|             let is_previously_selected = previous_ids.map_or(false, |ids| ids.contains(&light.id));
  116|             let effective_score = if is_previously_selected {
  117|                 score * 1.20 // 20% hysteresis boost to retain current lights and prevent seam popping
  118|             } else {
  119|                 score
  120|             };
  121|             selected.push((effective_score, light));
  122|         }
  123| 
  124|         selected.sort_by(|a, b| b.0.partial_cmp(&a.0).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
  125|         let result: Vec<LightSource> = selected.into_iter().take(top_k).map(|(_, l)| *l).collect();
  126|         self.entries
  127|             .insert(key, result.iter().map(|l| l.id).collect());
  128|         result
  129|     }
  130| }

===== wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/lights.rs (132 lines) =====
    1| //! Per-frame light selection — one implementation for the surface and
    2| //! splat renderers, which previously carried diverging copies.
    3| //!
    4| //! Inputs: fixture lights from every visible chunk (deduplicated by id —
    5| //! a fixture near a chunk border is listed by several chunks) plus the
    6| //! frame's dynamic lights (dropped flares). The most important lights fill
    7| //! the bounded shader slots; the most important *fixture* light also
    8| //! wins the hero shadow map (a flare at ankle height would collapse the
    9| //! top-down shadow frustum, so dynamic lights never own it).
   10| //!
   11| //! Importance = radius * sqrt(intensity) / (distance² + 0.1): bigger and
   12| //! brighter lights reach farther, nearby lights dominate.
   13| 
   14| use crate::application::ports::{FrameParams, LightSource, MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS};
   15| 
   16| /// Maximum shader light slots (matches the GLSL uniform arrays).
   17| pub const MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS: usize = crate::application::ports::MAX_SCENE_LIGHTS;
   18| 
   19| /// The frame's selected lights, packed for `uniform[1i|3fv|4fv]` upload.
   20| pub struct SelectedLights {
   21|     pub count: usize,
   22|     pub positions: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
   23|     pub colors: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
   24|     /// Per light: radius, intensity, half_size.x, half_size.y.
   25|     pub params: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 4],
   26|     pub kinds: [i32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS],
   27|     /// Slot index of the shadow-casting hero light, or -1.
   28|     pub hero_slot: i32,
   29|     /// Hero light's position/radius (meaningful when `hero_slot >= 0`).
   30|     pub hero_position: [f32; 3],
   31|     pub hero_radius: f32,
   32| }
   33| 
   34| /// Wraps the frame's dynamic lights as fixture-shaped sources with sentinel
   35| /// ids in the top range, so one selection pass handles both kinds.
   36| pub fn dynamic_light_sources(frame: &FrameParams) -> Vec<LightSource> {
   37|     frame
   38|         .active_dynamic_lights()
   39|         .iter()
   40|         .enumerate()
   41|         .map(|(i, d)| LightSource {
   42|             id: u64::MAX - i as u64,
   43|             position: d.position,
   44|             half_size: [0.25, 0.25],
   45|             color: d.color,
   46|             radius: d.radius,
   47|             intensity: d.intensity,
   48|             kind: crate::application::ports::LightKind::Point,
   49|             flicker_mode: 0,
   50|             enabled: true,
   51|         })
   52|         .collect()
   53| }
   54| 
   55| fn is_dynamic(light: &LightSource) -> bool {
   56|     light.id > u64::MAX - 16
   57| }
   58| 
   59| /// Selects and packs the frame's lights. `fixtures` should already be
   60| /// deduplicated by id (pass a `HashMap`'s values); `dynamic` comes from
   61| /// [`dynamic_light_sources`].
   62| pub fn select_lights<'a>(
   63|     fixtures: impl Iterator<Item = &'a LightSource>,
   64|     dynamic: &'a [LightSource],
   65|     frame: &FrameParams,
   66| ) -> SelectedLights {
   67|     let mut ranked: Vec<(&LightSource, f32)> = fixtures
   68|         .chain(dynamic.iter())
   69|         .map(|light| {
   70|             let dx = light.position[0] - frame.camera_pos[0];
   71|             let dy = light.position[1] - frame.camera_pos[1];
   72|             let dz = light.position[2] - frame.camera_pos[2];
   73|             let dist2 = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz;
   74|             (light, light.radius * light.intensity.sqrt() / (dist2 + 0.1))
   75|         })
   76|         .collect();
   77|     ranked.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
   78| 
   79|     let count = ranked.len().min(MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS);
   80|     let mut selected = SelectedLights {
   81|         count,
   82|         positions: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
   83|         colors: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
   84|         params: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 4],
   85|         kinds: [0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS],
   86|         hero_slot: -1,
   87|         hero_position: [0.0; 3],
   88|         hero_radius: 0.0,
   89|     };
   90|     for (i, (light, _)) in ranked[..count].iter().enumerate() {
   91|         selected.positions[i * 3..i * 3 + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.position);
   92|         selected.colors[i * 3..i * 3 + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.color);
   93|         selected.params[i * 4] = light.radius;
   94|         selected.params[i * 4 + 1] = light.intensity;
   95|         selected.params[i * 4 + 2] = light.half_size[0];
   96|         selected.params[i * 4 + 3] = light.half_size[1];
   97|         selected.kinds[i] = light.kind as i32;
   98|     }
   99| 
  100|     // Hero shadow: the strongest *fixture* light in the selected slots.
  101|     if let Some(slot) = ranked[..count].iter().position(|(l, _)| !is_dynamic(l)) {
  102|         selected.hero_slot = slot as i32;
  103|         selected.hero_position = ranked[slot].0.position;
  104|         selected.hero_radius = ranked[slot].0.radius;
  105|     }
  106|     selected
  107| }
  108| 
  109| /// Flare-core uniforms (`uCoreCount`/`uCores`/`uCoreColors`), independent of
  110| /// the merged light slots so a flare culled from the four shading lights
  111| /// still shows its ember.
  112| pub struct FlareCores {
  113|     pub count: i32,
  114|     /// xyz = position, w = pre-flickered intensity.
  115|     pub pos_intensity: [f32; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS * 4],
  116|     pub colors: [f32; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS * 3],
  117| }

  119| pub fn flare_cores(frame: &FrameParams) -> FlareCores {
  120|     let cores = frame.active_dynamic_lights();
  121|     let mut packed = FlareCores {
  122|         count: cores.len() as i32,
  123|         pos_intensity: [0.0; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS * 4],
  124|         colors: [0.0; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS * 3],
  125|     };
  126|     for (i, c) in cores.iter().enumerate() {
  127|         packed.pos_intensity[i * 4..i * 4 + 3].copy_from_slice(&c.position);
  128|         packed.pos_intensity[i * 4 + 3] = c.intensity;
  129|         packed.colors[i * 3..i * 3 + 3].copy_from_slice(&c.color);
  130|     }
  131|     packed
  132| }
===== wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/visibility.rs (247 lines) =====
    1| //! Conservative visibility tests shared by the raster drivers.
    2| 
    3| use crate::application::ports::FrameParams;
    4| 
    5| /// Shared raster far plane and conservative culling boundary (world units).
    6| /// Beer--Lambert fog never becomes exactly opaque, so projection and culling
    7| /// must use the identical distance rather than hiding a ten-unit mismatch.
    8| pub const MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE: f32 = 110.0;
    9| 
   10| /// Sphere visibility: inside the draw distance and not entirely behind the
   11| /// camera plane. Returns the squared distance for near-to-far sorting, or
   12| /// `None` when culled. Deliberately conservative (no side-plane frustum
   13| /// test): a false "visible" costs a few draws, a false cull costs a hole
   14| /// in the world.
   15| pub fn sphere_visible(
   16|     center: [f32; 3],
   17|     radius: f32,
   18|     frame: &FrameParams,
   19|     max_draw_distance: f32,
   20| ) -> Option<f32> {
   21|     let to = [
   22|         center[0] - frame.camera_pos[0],
   23|         center[1] - frame.camera_pos[1],
   24|         center[2] - frame.camera_pos[2],
   25|     ];
   26|     let distance2 = to[0] * to[0] + to[1] * to[1] + to[2] * to[2];
   27|     // Cull only when the *whole sphere* lies beyond the distance boundary.
   28|     // Testing the center against `max_draw_distance` cuts chunks/cells that
   29|     // still intersect the visible volume and creates a hard pop at the fog
   30|     // edge.
   31|     let farthest_visible_center = max_draw_distance + radius;
   32|     if distance2 > farthest_visible_center * farthest_visible_center {
   33|         return None;
   34|     }
   35|     let (sp, cp) = frame.pitch.sin_cos();
   36|     let (sy, cy) = frame.yaw.sin_cos();
   37|     let forward = [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy];
   38|     let dot = to[0] * forward[0] + to[1] * forward[1] + to[2] * forward[2];
   39|     if dot >= -radius {
   40|         Some(distance2)
   41|     } else {
   42|         None
   43|     }
   44| }
   45| 
   46| /// Center + bounding-sphere radius of a chunk from its origin and local
   47| /// bounds-max — the shape both mesh and splat chunk records share.
   48| pub fn chunk_bounding_sphere(origin: [f32; 3], bounds_max: [f32; 3]) -> ([f32; 3], f32) {
   49|     let center = [
   50|         origin[0] + bounds_max[0] * 0.5,
   51|         origin[1] + bounds_max[1] * 0.5,
   52|         origin[2] + bounds_max[2] * 0.5,
   53|     ];
   54|     let radius = (bounds_max[0] * bounds_max[0]
   55|         + bounds_max[1] * bounds_max[1]
   56|         + bounds_max[2] * bounds_max[2])
   57|         .sqrt()
   58|         * 0.5;
   59|     (center, radius)
   60| }
   61| 
   62| /// Conservative AABB vs. Frustum test with safety inflation margin (0.5 voxel).
   63| ///
   64| /// # Rationale
   65| /// Prevents false culls on side view boundaries while rejecting chunks strictly outside
   66| /// the extended camera view cone.
   67| pub fn aabb_frustum_visible(
   68|     origin: [f32; 3],
   69|     bounds_max: [f32; 3],
   70|     frame: &FrameParams,
   71|     margin: f32,
   72| ) -> bool {
   73|     let (center, radius) = chunk_bounding_sphere(origin, bounds_max);
   74|     let inflated_radius = radius + margin;
   75|     sphere_visible(center, inflated_radius, frame, MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE).is_some()
   76| }
   77| 
   78| /// Signed world-space distance from a sphere center to one side plane of the
   79| /// perspective frustum, positive meaning inside. `axis` is `right` or `up`;
   80| /// `tan_half` is the tangent of that axis's half-angle (horizontal uses
   81| /// `fov_tan * aspect`, vertical uses `fov_tan` alone); `sign` selects which
   82| /// of the paired planes (+1 for the right/top plane, -1 for left/bottom).
   83| ///
   84| /// Derivation: a point at forward-distance `along` and lateral offset
   85| /// `across` (both relative to the camera, along `forward`/`axis`) lies
   86| /// exactly on the `+axis` boundary plane when `across == tan_half * along`.
   87| /// The perpendicular distance from an arbitrary point to that plane is
   88| /// `(tan_half * along - across) * cos(theta_half)`, and
   89| /// `cos(theta_half) == 1 / sqrt(1 + tan_half^2)` — this is exact, not an
   90| /// approximation, so it carries no extra risk of an over-eager cull.
   91| fn side_plane_distance(
   92|     delta: [f32; 3],
   93|     forward: [f32; 3],
   94|     axis: [f32; 3],
   95|     tan_half: f32,
   96|     sign: f32,
   97| ) -> f32 {
   98|     let dot = |a: [f32; 3], b: [f32; 3]| a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1] + a[2] * b[2];
   99|     let along = dot(delta, forward);
  100|     let across = dot(delta, axis) * sign;
  101|     (tan_half * along - across) / (1.0 + tan_half * tan_half).sqrt()
  102| }
  103| 
  104| /// Conservative sphere-vs-frustum side-plane test: `false` only when the
  105| /// sphere lies entirely outside at least one of the four side planes
  106| /// (left/right/top/bottom). Deliberately excludes near/far — those stay the
  107| /// job of [`sphere_visible`], which this is meant to be combined with.
  108| pub fn frustum_side_planes_visible(
  109|     center: [f32; 3],
  110|     radius: f32,
  111|     frame: &FrameParams,
  112|     fov_tan: f32,
  113|     aspect: f32,
  114| ) -> bool {
  115|     let delta = [
  116|         center[0] - frame.camera_pos[0],
  117|         center[1] - frame.camera_pos[1],
  118|         center[2] - frame.camera_pos[2],
  119|     ];
  120|     let (sp, cp) = frame.pitch.sin_cos();
  121|     let (sy, cy) = frame.yaw.sin_cos();
  122|     let right = [cy, 0.0, -sy];
  123|     let up = [sp * sy, cp, sp * cy];
  124|     let forward = [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy];
  125|     let tan_h = fov_tan * aspect.max(1e-6);
  126|     let tan_v = fov_tan;
  127| 
  128|     [
  129|         side_plane_distance(delta, forward, right, tan_h, 1.0),
  130|         side_plane_distance(delta, forward, right, tan_h, -1.0),
  131|         side_plane_distance(delta, forward, up, tan_v, 1.0),
  132|         side_plane_distance(delta, forward, up, tan_v, -1.0),
  133|     ]
  134|     .iter()
  135|     .all(|&d| d >= -radius)
  136| }

===== wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/upload_scene_lights.rs (110 lines) =====
    1| //! Complete analytic-fixture upload shared by the surface and raymarch paths.
    2| //!
    3| //! A texture is used instead of fragment-uniform arrays for two reasons: the
    4| //! physical scene is not silently truncated to a camera-ranked slot budget,
    5| //! and the large raymarch chunk table no longer competes with lights for the
    6| //! WebGL minimum uniform-vector allowance. Each light occupies three RGBA32F
    7| //! texels in the layout decoded by `shaders/sample_scene_lights.rs`.
    8| 
    9| use wasm_bindgen::JsValue;
   10| use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlTexture};
   11| 
   12| use crate::application::ports::LightSource;
   13| 
   14| const PREFERRED_ROW_TEXELS: i32 = 1024;
   15| const TEXELS_PER_LIGHT: usize = 3;
   16| 
   17| pub struct SceneLightTexture {
   18|     texture: WebGlTexture,
   19|     width: i32,
   20|     maximum_size: i32,
   21|     staging: Vec<f32>,
   22|     last_lights: Vec<LightSource>,
   23|     uploaded: bool,
   24| }
   25| 
   26| impl SceneLightTexture {
   27|     pub fn create(gl: &Gl) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
   28|         let texture = gl
   29|             .create_texture()
   30|             .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("failed to create scene-light texture"))?;
   31|         let maximum_size = gl
   32|             .get_parameter(Gl::MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE)?
   33|             .as_f64()
   34|             .unwrap_or(0.0) as i32;
   35|         if maximum_size < 1 {
   36|             return Err(JsValue::from_str("WebGL reported no 2-D texture capacity"));
   37|         }
   38|         let width = PREFERRED_ROW_TEXELS.min(maximum_size);
   39|         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&texture));
   40|         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
   41|         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
   42|         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_S, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
   43|         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_T, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
   44|         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, None);
   45|         Ok(Self {
   46|             texture,
   47|             width,
   48|             maximum_size,
   49|             staging: Vec::new(),
   50|             last_lights: Vec::new(),
   51|             uploaded: false,
   52|         })
   53|     }
   54| 
   55|     /// Replaces the immutable frame snapshot and returns its exact light count.
   56|     pub fn upload(&mut self, gl: &Gl, lights: &[LightSource]) -> Result<i32, JsValue> {
   57|         if self.uploaded && self.last_lights == lights {
   58|             return Ok(lights.len().min(i32::MAX as usize) as i32);
   59|         }
   60|         let texel_count = lights.len().max(1) * TEXELS_PER_LIGHT;
   61|         let rows = (texel_count as i32 + self.width - 1) / self.width;
   62|         if rows > self.maximum_size || lights.len() > i32::MAX as usize {
   63|             return Err(JsValue::from_str(
   64|                 "resident fixture list exceeds the WebGL scene-light texture",
   65|             ));
   66|         }
   67| 
   68|         self.staging.clear();
   69|         self.staging
   70|             .resize(self.width as usize * rows as usize * 4, 0.0);
   71|         for (index, light) in lights.iter().enumerate() {
   72|             let offset = index * TEXELS_PER_LIGHT * 4;
   73|             self.staging[offset..offset + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.position);
   74|             self.staging[offset + 3] = light.kind as u8 as f32;
   75|             self.staging[offset + 4..offset + 7].copy_from_slice(&light.color);
   76|             self.staging[offset + 7] = light.intensity;
   77|             self.staging[offset + 8] = light.radius;
   78|             self.staging[offset + 9] = light.half_size[0];
   79|             self.staging[offset + 10] = light.half_size[1];
   80|         }
   81| 
   82|         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&self.texture));
   83|         gl.pixel_storei(Gl::UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, 4);
   84|         let view = js_sys::Float32Array::from(self.staging.as_slice());
   85|         gl.tex_image_2d_with_i32_and_i32_and_i32_and_format_and_type_and_opt_array_buffer_view(
   86|             Gl::TEXTURE_2D,
   87|             0,
   88|             Gl::RGBA32F as i32,
   89|             self.width,
   90|             rows,
   91|             0,
   92|             Gl::RGBA,
   93|             Gl::FLOAT,
   94|             Some(&view),
   95|         )?;
   96|         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, None);
   97|         self.last_lights.clear();
   98|         self.last_lights.extend_from_slice(lights);
   99|         self.uploaded = true;
  100|         Ok(lights.len() as i32)
  101|     }
  102| 
  103|     pub fn bind(&self, gl: &Gl) {
  104|         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&self.texture));
  105|     }
  106| 
  107|     pub fn width(&self) -> i32 {
  108|         self.width
  109|     }
  110| }

   13| /// Uploads a chunk's 3D irradiance probe volume texture (or 1x1x1 black fallback).
   14| ///
   15| /// Texture sampling uses `LINEAR` minification and magnification filters, with `CLAMP_TO_EDGE`
   16| /// wrapping so boundary probe samples interpolate smoothly across adjacent chunk borders.
   17| pub fn upload_light_volume(gl: &Gl, mesh: &SurfaceMeshPayload) -> Result<WebGlTexture, JsValue> {

   23|

   33|             mesh.light_volume_dims[2] as i32,
   34|             mesh.light_volume_bytes.as_slice(),
   35|         )
   36|     } else {
   37|         (1, 1, 1, fallback.as_slice())
   38|     };
   39| 
   40|     gl.tex_image_3d_with_opt_u8_array(

   44|         width,
   45|         height,
   46|         depth,
   47|         0,
   48|         Gl::RGB,
   49|         Gl::UNSIGNED_BYTE,
   50|         Some(bytes),
   51|     )?;

   53|     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Gl::TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, Gl::LINEAR as i32);
   54|     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_S, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
   55|     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_T, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);

    1| //! Camera and light matrices — column-major, ready for `uniformMatrix4fv`.
    2| 
    3| use crate::application::ports::FrameParams;
    4| 
    5| /// View + projection for the raster paths, from the same yaw/pitch basis
    6| /// the raymarcher and the CPU splatter use, so every renderer frames the
    7| /// world identically.
    8| pub fn camera_matrices(
    9|     frame: &FrameParams,
   10|     width: i32,
   11|     height: i32,
   12|     max_draw_distance: f32,
   13| ) -> ([f32; 16], [f32; 16]) {
   14|     let (sp, cp) = frame.pitch.sin_cos();
   15|     let (sy, cy) = frame.yaw.sin_cos();
   16|     let right = [cy, 0.0, -sy];
   17|     let up = [sp * sy, cp, sp * cy];
   18|     let forward = [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy];
   19|     let p = frame.camera_pos;
   20|     let dot = |a: [f32; 3], b: [f32; 3]| a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1] + a[2] * b[2];
   21|     let view = [
   22|         right[0],
   23|         up[0],
   24|         -forward[0],
   25|         0.0,
   26|         right[1],
   27|         up[1],
   28|         -forward[1],
   29|         0.0,
   30|         right[2],
   31|         up[2],
   32|         -forward[2],
   33|         0.0,
   34|         -dot(right, p),
   35|         -dot(up, p),
   36|         dot(forward, p),
   37|         1.0,
   38|     ];
   39|     let near = 0.03;
   40|     let far = max_draw_distance;
   41|     let f = 1.0 / crate::drivers::webgl::fov_tan();
   42|     let aspect = width as f32 / height.max(1) as f32;
   43|     let projection = [
   44|         f / aspect,
   45|         0.0,
   46|         0.0,
   47|         0.0,
   48|         0.0,
   49|         f,
   50|         0.0,
   51|         0.0,
   52|         0.0,
   53|         0.0,
   54|         (far + near) / (near - far),
   55|         -1.0,
   56|         0.0,
   57|         0.0,
   58|         (2.0 * far * near) / (near - far),
   59|         0.0,
   60|     ];
   61|     (projection, view)
   62| }
   63| 
   64| pub fn ortho_matrix(
   65|     left: f32,
   66|     right: f32,
   67|     bottom: f32,
   68|     top: f32,
   69|     near: f32,
   70|     far: f32,
   71| ) -> [f32; 16] {
   72|     let mut m = [0.0; 16];
   73|     m[0] = 2.0 / (right - left);
   74|     m[5] = 2.0 / (top - bottom);
   75|     m[10] = -2.0 / (far - near);
   76|     m[12] = -(right + left) / (right - left);
   77|     m[13] = -(top + bottom) / (top - bottom);
   78|     m[14] = -(far + near) / (far - near);
   79|     m[15] = 1.0;
   80|     m
   81| }
   82| 
   83| /// View matrix for a light looking straight down (-Y), up = -Z. Used by
   84| /// the hero-light shadow pass (ceiling fixtures shine downward).
   85| pub fn look_at_matrix_down(eye: [f32; 3]) -> [f32; 16] {
   86|     let forward = [0.0, -1.0, 0.0];
   87|     let up = [0.0, 0.0, -1.0f32];
   88|     let right = [1.0, 0.0, 0.0f32];
   89| 
   90|     let mut m = [0.0; 16];
   91|     m[0] = right[0];
   92|     m[1] = up[0];
   93|     m[2] = -forward[0];
   94| 
   95|     m[4] = right[1];
   96|     m[5] = up[1];
   97|     m[6] = -forward[1];
   98| 
   99|     m[8] = right[2];
  100|     m[9] = up[2];
  101|     m[10] = -forward[2];
  102| 
  103|     m[12] = -(right[0] * eye[0] + right[1] * eye[1] + right[2] * eye[2]);
  104|     m[13] = -(up[0] * eye[0] + up[1] * eye[1] + up[2] * eye[2]);
  105|     m[14] = -(-forward[0] * eye[0] + -forward[1] * eye[1] + -forward[2] * eye[2]);
  106|     m[15] = 1.0;
  107|     m
  108| }
  109| 
  110| pub fn multiply_matrices(a: &[f32; 16], b: &[f32; 16]) -> [f32; 16] {
  111|     let mut m = [0.0; 16];
  112|     for col in 0..4 {
  113|         for row in 0..4 {
  114|             m[col * 4 + row] = a[row] * b[col * 4]
  115|                 + a[4 + row] * b[col * 4 + 1]
  116|                 + a[8 + row] * b[col * 4 + 2]
  117|                 + a[12 + row] * b[col * 4 + 3];
  118|         }
  119|     }
  120|     m
  121| }
===== wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/timer.rs (94 lines) =====
    1| //! Asynchronous GPU frame timing via `EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2`.
    2| //!
    3| //! One query is in flight at a time; results are polled (never blocked on)
    4| //! at the top of the next frames, so the HUD's GPU number lags a frame or
    5| //! two but the pipeline never stalls. Toggleable (`RenderToggles::gpu_timer`)
    6| //! because some drivers serialize on timer queries.
    7| 
    8| use js_sys::Object;
    9| use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlQuery};
   10| 
   11| /// Extension constants absent from WebGL2 core.
   12| const TIME_ELAPSED_EXT: u32 = 0x88BF;
   13| const GPU_DISJOINT_EXT: u32 = 0x8FBB;
   14| 
   15| pub struct GpuFrameTimer {
   16|     extension: Option<Object>,
   17|     pending: Option<WebGlQuery>,
   18|     last_ms: Option<f32>,
   19| }
   20| 
   21| impl GpuFrameTimer {
   22|     /// Probes for the extension; a `None` extension makes every method a
   23|     /// no-op so callers never branch on support.
   24|     pub fn new(gl: &Gl) -> Self {
   25|         Self {
   26|             extension: gl
   27|                 .get_extension("EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2")
   28|                 .ok()
   29|                 .flatten(),
   30|             pending: None,
   31|             last_ms: None,
   32|         }
   33|     }
   34| 
   35|     pub fn last_ms(&self) -> Option<f32> {
   36|         self.last_ms
   37|     }
   38| 
   39|     /// Collects a finished query, if any. Disjoint intervals (GPU clock
   40|     /// disturbance) discard the sample.
   41|     pub fn poll(&mut self, gl: &Gl) {
   42|         let Some(query) = self.pending.as_ref() else {
   43|             return;
   44|         };
   45|         let available = gl
   46|             .get_query_parameter(query, Gl::QUERY_RESULT_AVAILABLE)
   47|             .as_bool()
   48|             .unwrap_or(false);
   49|         let disjoint = self.extension.is_some()
   50|             && gl
   51|                 .get_parameter(GPU_DISJOINT_EXT)
   52|                 .ok()
   53|                 .and_then(|value| value.as_bool())
   54|                 .unwrap_or(false);
   55|         if !available && !disjoint {
   56|             return;
   57|         }
   58|         let query = self.pending.take().expect("pending timer exists");
   59|         if available && !disjoint {
   60|             self.last_ms = gl
   61|                 .get_query_parameter(&query, Gl::QUERY_RESULT)
   62|                 .as_f64()
   63|                 .map(|nanos| (nanos as f32) * 1.0e-6);
   64|         }
   65|         gl.delete_query(Some(&query));
   66|     }
   67| 
   68|     /// Starts timing this frame. Returns whether a query was issued (pass
   69|     /// it to [`Self::end`]). `enabled` comes from the toggle switchboard.
   70|     pub fn begin(&mut self, gl: &Gl, enabled: bool) -> bool {
   71|         if !enabled {
   72|             // The HUD must not present an old sample as current after timing
   73|             // has been switched off. An in-flight query is still collected
   74|             // by `poll` and then discarded from view on this frame.
   75|             self.last_ms = None;
   76|             return false;
   77|         }
   78|         if self.extension.is_none() || self.pending.is_some() {
   79|             return false;
   80|         }
   81|         let Some(query) = gl.create_query() else {
   82|             return false;
   83|         };
   84|         gl.begin_query(TIME_ELAPSED_EXT, &query);
   85|         self.pending = Some(query);
   86|         true
   87|     }
   88| 
   89|     pub fn end(&self, gl: &Gl, started: bool) {
   90|         if started {
   91|             gl.end_query(TIME_ELAPSED_EXT);
   92|         }
   93|     }
   94| }

    1| //! Depth-only render target for the hero-light shadow map.
    2| 
    3| use wasm_bindgen::JsValue;
    4| use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlFramebuffer, WebGlTexture};

    6| pub struct ShadowTarget {
    7|     pub fbo: WebGlFramebuffer,
    8|     pub texture: WebGlTexture,
    9|     pub size: i32,
   10| }
   11| 
   12| /// Creates a `size`² DEPTH_COMPONENT16 texture bound to a framebuffer's
   13| /// depth attachment. NEAREST filtering: the shaders do their own PCF.
   14| pub fn create_shadow_target(gl: &Gl, size: i32) -> Result<ShadowTarget, JsValue> {
   15|     let texture = gl
   16|         .create_texture()
   17|         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("create shadow texture"))?;
   18|     gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&texture));
   19|     gl.tex_image_2d_with_i32_and_i32_and_i32_and_format_and_type_and_opt_u8_array(
   20|         Gl::TEXTURE_2D,
   21|         0,
   22|         Gl::DEPTH_COMPONENT16 as i32,
   23|         size,
   24|         size,
   25|         0,
   26|         Gl::DEPTH_COMPONENT,
   27|         Gl::UNSIGNED_SHORT,
   28|         None,
   29|     )?;
   30|     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
   31|     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
   32|     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_S, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
   33|     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_T, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
   34| 
   35|     let fbo = gl
   36|         .create_framebuffer()
   37|         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("create shadow FBO"))?;
   38|     gl.bind_framebuffer(Gl::FRAMEBUFFER, Some(&fbo));
   39|     gl.framebuffer_texture_2d(
   40|         Gl::FRAMEBUFFER,
   41|         Gl::DEPTH_ATTACHMENT,
   42|         Gl::TEXTURE_2D,
   43|         Some(&texture),
   44|         0,
   45|     );
   46| 
   47|     // A depth-only WebGL2 target has no color attachment. Explicitly route
   48|     // both drawing and reading to NONE; leaving the defaults at
   49|     // COLOR_ATTACHMENT0 makes strict mobile drivers report an incomplete
   50|     // framebuffer and silently discard the shadow pass.
   51|     let draw_buffers = js_sys::Array::new();
   52|     draw_buffers.push(&wasm_bindgen::JsValue::from_f64(Gl::NONE as f64));
   53|     gl.draw_buffers(draw_buffers.as_ref());
   54|     gl.read_buffer(Gl::NONE);
   55| 
   56|     let status = gl.check_framebuffer_status(Gl::FRAMEBUFFER);
   57|     if status != Gl::FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE {
   58|         gl.bind_framebuffer(Gl::FRAMEBUFFER, None);
   59|         gl.delete_framebuffer(Some(&fbo));
   60|         gl.delete_texture(Some(&texture));
   61|         return Err(JsValue::from_str(&format!(
   62|             "shadow framebuffer is incomplete (status 0x{status:04x})"
   63|         )));
   64|     }
   65|     gl.bind_framebuffer(Gl::FRAMEBUFFER, None);
   66| 
   67|     Ok(ShadowTarget { fbo, texture, size })
   68| }

    1| //! WebGL2 context creation and shader program linking — the one copy of

    4| use js_sys::Reflect;

    8| /// Options for [`create_context`]. Raster paths want a depth buffer; the
    9| /// fullscreen raymarcher resolves visibility itself, so depth and MSAA
   10| /// would be wasted bandwidth on low-spec GPUs.
   11| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
   12| pub struct ContextOptions {
   13|     pub depth: bool,
   14| }
   15| 
   16| /// Creates a WebGL2 context with the engine's standard attributes
   17| /// (no antialiasing, opaque, high-performance GPU preference).
   18| pub fn create_context(canvas: &HtmlCanvasElement, options: ContextOptions) -> Result<Gl, JsValue> {
   19|     let attrs = js_sys::Object::new();
   20|     Reflect::set(&attrs, &"antialias".into(), &false.into())?;
   21|     Reflect::set(&attrs, &"depth".into(), &options.depth.into())?;
   22|     Reflect::set(&attrs, &"stencil".into(), &false.into())?;
   23|     Reflect::set(&attrs, &"alpha".into(), &false.into())?;
   24|     Reflect::set(
   25|         &attrs,
   26|         &"powerPreference".into(),
   27|         &"high-performance".into(),
   28|     )?;
   29|     canvas
   30|         .get_context_with_context_options("webgl2", &attrs)?
   31|         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("WebGL2 is not supported on this browser"))?
   32|         .dyn_into::<Gl>()
   33|         .map_err(|_| JsValue::from_str("webgl2 context has an unexpected type"))
   34| }
   35| 
   36| pub fn compile_shader(gl: &Gl, kind: u32, source: &str) -> Result<WebGlShader, JsValue> {
   37|     let shader = gl
   38|         .create_shader(kind)
   39|         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("failed to create shader object"))?;
   40|     gl.shader_source(&shader, source);
   41|     gl.compile_shader(&shader);
   42|     if gl
   43|         .get_shader_parameter(&shader, Gl::COMPILE_STATUS)
   44|         .as_bool()
   45|         .unwrap_or(false)
   46|     {
   47|         Ok(shader)
   48|     } else {
   49|         let log = gl.get_shader_info_log(&shader).unwrap_or_default();
   50|         gl.delete_shader(Some(&shader));
   51|         Err(JsValue::from_str(&format!("shader compile error: {log}")))
   52|     }
   53| }
   54| 
   55| pub fn link_program(gl: &Gl, vertex: &str, fragment: &str) -> Result<WebGlProgram, JsValue> {
   56|     let vs = compile_shader(gl, Gl::VERTEX_SHADER, vertex)?;
   57|     let fs = compile_shader(gl, Gl::FRAGMENT_SHADER, fragment)?;
   58|     let program = gl
   59|         .create_program()
   60|         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("failed to create shader program"))?;
   61|     gl.attach_shader(&program, &vs);
   62|     gl.attach_shader(&program, &fs);
   63|     gl.link_program(&program);
   64|     if gl
   65|         .get_program_parameter(&program, Gl::LINK_STATUS)
   66|         .as_bool()
   67|         .unwrap_or(false)
   68|     {
   69|         Ok(program)
   70|     } else {
   71|         let log = gl.get_program_info_log(&program).unwrap_or_default();
   72|         gl.delete_program(Some(&program));
   73|         Err(JsValue::from_str(&format!("shader link error: {log}")))
   74|     }

Notes so far:
- `cluster_scene_lights.rs`: `append_lights_reaching_bounds` is O(L) per call — L = lights in scene. Called per chunk → O(C × L) per frame potentially. Need to see callers. `LightSelectionCache` — HashMap keyed by chunk key, values Vec<u64> of selected ids. `previous_ids.contains()` — Vec contains is O(top_k), fine. But the cache has unbounded growth: entries never evicted — chunk keys accumulate forever as player walks. Unbounded growth finding.
- `lights.rs select_lights`: O(N log N) sort per frame over all fixture lights — fine if N small.
- `upload_scene_lights.rs`: `last_lights == lights` comparison O(L) per frame — fine. Upload O(L). Note `staging.resize` reallocates each time the count changes. OK.

Now the shaders. Let me look at the shaders/ directory (GLSL-based Rust string builders). Then the big trace_voxel_scene shaders. Let me read them all.

===== wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/chunks.rs (220 lines) =====
    1| //! Shared GLSL chunks — snippets spliced into more than one shader so the
    2| //! engine has exactly one definition of each cross-cutting effect.
    3| //!
    4| //! Shader sources are assembled at startup by `format!` concatenation (a
    5| //! few string copies once per program link — nothing per frame). Each chunk
    6| //! is a self-contained set of GLSL functions/consts with no `uniform`
    7| //! declarations, so any stage can include it.
    8| 
    9| use std::fmt::Write;
   10| 
   11| use vackrooms::adapters::material_palette::MATERIAL_VISUALS;
   12| 
   13| /// The flashlight spotlight cone — **GLSL mirror of the single spec in
   14| /// `adapters::cpu_splatter::flashlight`** (inner/outer angle, finite-range
   15| /// inverse-square transport, lamp offset, and tint). A tuning change there
   16| /// must be mirrored here.
   17| ///
   18| /// Shape: smoothstep between an inner cone (full strength, 11°) and an
   19| /// outer cone (zero, 24°) around the camera forward axis. Transport uses a
   20| /// compact-support inverse-square law and a strict Lambert receiver cosine.
   21| pub const SPOT_CONE_GLSL: &str = r#"
   22| // --- flashlight cone (spec: adapters/cpu_splatter/flashlight.rs) ---
   23| const float SPOT_INNER_COS = 0.9816272; // cos(11 deg)
   24| const float SPOT_OUTER_COS = 0.9135455; // cos(24 deg)
   25| const float SPOT_RANGE_END = 14.0;
   26| const float SPOT_INTENSITY = 32.0;
   27| const float SPOT_MIN_DISTANCE = 0.25;
   28| const float SPOT_INV_PI = 0.3183098861837907;
   29| const vec3  SPOT_TINT = vec3(1.0, 0.91, 0.72);
   30| 
   31| // The hand-held lamp sits slightly forward of and below the eye.
   32| vec3 spotLampPos(vec3 camPos, vec3 camForward) {
   33|     return camPos + camForward * 0.18 - vec3(0.0, 0.10, 0.0);
   34| }
   35| 
   36| // Angular falloff: 1 inside the inner cone, 0 outside the outer.
   37| float spotCone(vec3 beam, vec3 camForward) {
   38|     return smoothstep(SPOT_OUTER_COS, SPOT_INNER_COS, dot(beam, camForward));
   39| }
   40| 
   41| // Finite-range inverse-square transport. The compact window and its first
   42| // derivative both reach zero at RANGE_END, so the beam has no hard rim.
   43| float spotAttenuation(float dist) {
   44|     if (!(dist >= 0.0) || dist >= SPOT_RANGE_END) return 0.0;
   45|     float normalizedSquared = (dist * dist) / (SPOT_RANGE_END * SPOT_RANGE_END);
   46|     float window = max(1.0 - normalizedSquared * normalizedSquared, 0.0);
   47|     float minimumSquared = SPOT_MIN_DISTANCE * SPOT_MIN_DISTANCE;
   48|     return (window * window) / max(dist * dist, minimumSquared);
   49| }
   50| 
   51| // Lambertian reflected-radiance factor at a surface point with normal N.
   52| // The CPU contract evaluates irradiance first and multiplies albedo / PI;
   53| // folding 1/PI here preserves that exact composition at GPU call sites.
   54| vec3 spotBeam(vec3 camPos, vec3 camForward, vec3 surfacePos, vec3 N) {
   55|     vec3 lamp = spotLampPos(camPos, camForward);
   56|     vec3 toSurf = surfacePos - lamp;
   57|     float dist = length(toSurf);
   58|     vec3 beam = toSurf / max(dist, 1e-4);
   59|     float cone = spotCone(beam, camForward);
   60|     float attenuation = spotAttenuation(dist);
   61|     float facing = max(-dot(beam, N), 0.0);
   62|     return SPOT_TINT * (SPOT_INTENSITY * SPOT_INV_PI * cone * attenuation * facing);
   63| }
   64| "#;
   65| 
   66| /// Builds the palette lookup shared by both WebGL rasterizers. Shader source
   67| /// is assembled once at startup, so deriving it here removes a hand-maintained
   68| /// GLSL mirror without adding frame-time work.
   69| pub fn material_color_glsl() -> String {
   70|     let mut source = String::from("vec3 materialColor(float material) {\n");
   71|     for (material, visual) in MATERIAL_VISUALS.iter().enumerate() {
   72|         let red = (visual.color >> 16) & 0xff;
   73|         let green = (visual.color >> 8) & 0xff;
   74|         let blue = visual.color & 0xff;
   75|         writeln!(
   76|             source,
   77|             "    if (material < {:.1}) return vec3({red}.0, {green}.0, {blue}.0) / 255.0;",
   78|             material as f32 + 0.5,
   79|         )
   80|         .expect("writing to a String cannot fail");
   81|     }
   82|     source.push_str("    return vec3(0.0);\n}\n");
   83|     source
   84| }
