===== wasm_frontend/src/drivers/webgpu/shaders/surfel.wgsl (127 lines) =====
    1| // Instanced surfel strategy: the surface as a cloud of oriented discs.
    2| //
    3| // The other raster strategies draw the mesher's topology -- merged quads as
    4| // triangles, or one rectangle per merged quad. Both can only draw less by
    5| // re-meshing at a coarser voxel scale, which changes what the geometry is.
    6| // A surfel cloud samples that same surface into discs at a chosen spacing,
    7| // so density is a dial rather than a rebuild.
    8| //
    9| // The work splits like the splat path's, and for the same reason:
   10| //
   11| //   vertex   -- irradiance once per disc, flat interpolated. A disc that
   12| //               covers more than a handful of pixels beats per-fragment
   13| //               shading outright.
   14| //   fragment -- the disc mask, albedo, fog. No light loop.
   15| 
   16| // There is deliberately no rim feather here.
   17| //
   18| // Fading a disc's albedo toward its edge looks like the obvious way to let
   19| // neighbours blend, and in an opaque pass it is exactly wrong: with no
   20| // alpha blending the fade is not a cross-fade, it is a darkening, so every
   21| // disc draws its own outline and the wall comes out as fish scales. The
   22| // first version of this shader did that, and the image was convincing
   23| // enough to look intentional.
   24| //
   25| // Overlap alone is what makes the surface continuous: each disc reaches
   26| // the corner of its own cell (see `radius_for_spacing`), so coverage is
   27| // complete without any edge treatment. Blending, if it is ever wanted,
   28| // needs a real weighted-average resolve, not a multiply.
   29| 
   30| /// Minecraft's per-face directional constants, shared with the splat path
   31| /// so the two strategies light an identical wall identically.
   32| fn surfel_direction_gain(axis: u32) -> f32 {
   33|     switch axis {
   34|         case 0u: { return 1.00; }  // up
   35|         case 1u: { return 0.52; }  // down
   36|         case 2u, 3u: { return 0.80; }  // north / south
   37|         default: { return 0.64; }  // east / west
   38|     }
   39| }
   40| 
   41| struct SurfelVertex {
   42|     @builtin(position) clip_position: vec4<f32>,
   43|     @location(0) world: vec3<f32>,
   44|     /// Position within the disc; the fragment stage cuts the circle.
   45|     @location(1) disc: vec2<f32>,
   46|     /// Interpolated, not flat -- see the note in the vertex stage.
   47|     @location(2) irradiance: vec3<f32>,
   48|     @location(3) @interpolate(flat) visual: u32,
   49|     @location(4) @interpolate(flat) material: u32,
   50|     @location(5) @interpolate(flat) axis: u32,
   51| };
   52| 
   53| @vertex
   54| fn surfel_vertex(
   55|     @builtin(vertex_index) corner_index: u32,
   56|     @builtin(instance_index) surfel_index: u32,
   57| ) -> SurfelVertex {
   58|     let packed = packed_surfels[surfel_index];
   59|     let axis = surfel_axis(packed);
   60|     let material = packed.surface & 255u;
   61|     let baked = f32((packed.surface >> 8u) & 255u) / 15.0;
   62|     let ao = 1.0 - f32((packed.surface >> 16u) & 1u);
   63|     let normal = normal_for_axis(axis);
   64|     let world = surfel_world_position(packed, corner_index);
   65| 
   66|     // Shade at the corner, and interpolate.
   67|     //
   68|     // The splat path shades once per face and flat-interpolates, which is
   69|     // what makes a voxel read as a block. Copying that here produced a
   70|     // wall of fish scales, and the reason is structural rather than
   71|     // cosmetic: splat faces *tile*, so a constant colour per face has no
   72|     // visible seam, while surfels *overlap* by design -- 41% of each
   73|     // disc's area, so its radius can reach the corners of its own cell.
   74|     // Two overlapping constants meet along a circular arc, and every one
   75|     // of those arcs is visible. Sampling the shared lighting function at
   76|     // the corner's own position instead makes two discs agree wherever
   77|     // they overlap, because they are asking the same question about the
   78|     // same point in the world.
   79|     let irradiance = raster_surface_radiance(
   80|         world,
   81|         normal,
   82|         vec3<f32>(1.0),
   83|         baked,
   84|         ao,
   85|         chunk.draw.x,
   86|         chunk.draw.y
   87|     ) * surfel_direction_gain(axis);
   88| 
   89|     var output: SurfelVertex;
   90|     output.clip_position = frame.view_projection * vec4<f32>(world, 1.0);
   91|     output.world = world;
   92|     output.disc = vec2<f32>(
   93|         select(-1.0, 1.0, corner_index == 1u || corner_index == 3u),
   94|         select(-1.0, 1.0, corner_index >= 2u)
   95|     );
   96|     output.irradiance = irradiance;
   97|     output.visual = packed.visual;
   98|     output.material = material;
   99|     output.axis = axis;
  100|     return output;
  101| }
  102| 
  103| @fragment
  104| fn surfel_fragment(input: SurfelVertex) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
  105|     // The disc. Without this the cloud is a field of squares, which tiles
  106|     // suspiciously well and hides exactly the coverage gaps the radius was
  107|     // chosen to close -- a bug that looks like success.
  108|     let r = length(input.disc);
  109|     if r > 1.0 {
  110|         discard;
  111|     }
  112| 
  113|     let voxel = chunk.bounds_voxel_size.w;
  114|     let normal = normal_for_axis(input.axis);
  115|     let albedo = apply_material_pattern(
  116|         input.material,
  117|         packed_srgb_to_linear(input.visual),
  118|         input.world,
  119|         normal,
  120|         voxel
  121|     );
  122| 
  123|     let emission = f32(input.visual >> 24u) / 25.5;
  124|     let emits = emission > 0.0 && normal.y < -0.5;
  125|     let radiance = select(albedo * input.irradiance, albedo * emission, emits);
  126|     return present_radiance(radiance, input.world, input.clip_position.xy);
  127| }
===== wasm_frontend/src/drivers/webgpu/shaders/surfel_geometry.wgsl (83 lines) =====
    1| // Surfel expansion: one 16-byte record becomes a quad in the surface's own
    2| // tangent plane, with the disc cut out in the fragment stage.
    3| 
    4| struct PackedSurfel {
    5|     // x | y << 16, chunk-local fixed point (1/1024 u).
    6|     xy: u32,
    7|     // z | radius << 16 | normal_axis << 24. Radius is in 1/32 u steps,
    8|     // matching adapters::surfel_cloud::RADIUS_QUANT.
    9|     z_radius_axis: u32,
   10|     // material | baked_light << 8 | ao << 16 | flags << 24.
   11|     surface: u32,
   12|     // low 24: domain sRGB color; high 8: authored emission over 0..=10.
   13|     visual: u32,
   14| };
   15| 
   16| @group(1) @binding(1) var<storage, read> packed_surfels: array<PackedSurfel>;
   17| 
   18| // In-plane basis with U x V = outward normal, so the strip corner order
   19| // (-1,-1)(1,-1)(-1,1)(1,1) is counter-clockwise seen from the front and
   20| // back-face culling removes the inside of every wall for free.
   21| fn surfel_u(axis: u32) -> vec3<f32> {
   22|     if axis <= 3u { return vec3<f32>(1.0, 0.0, 0.0); }
   23|     return vec3<f32>(0.0, 1.0, 0.0);
   24| }
   25| 
   26| fn surfel_v(axis: u32) -> vec3<f32> {
   27|     switch axis {
   28|         case 0u: { return vec3<f32>(0.0, 0.0, -1.0); }
   29|         case 1u: { return vec3<f32>(0.0, 0.0, 1.0); }
   30|         case 2u: { return vec3<f32>(0.0, -1.0, 0.0); }
   31|         case 3u: { return vec3<f32>(0.0, 1.0, 0.0); }
   32|         case 4u: { return vec3<f32>(0.0, 0.0, 1.0); }
   33|         default: { return vec3<f32>(0.0, 0.0, -1.0); }
   34|     }
   35| }
   36| 
   37| fn surfel_centre(packed: PackedSurfel) -> vec3<f32> {
   38|     let centre_local = vec3<f32>(
   39|         f32(packed.xy & 65535u),
   40|         f32(packed.xy >> 16u),
   41|         f32(packed.z_radius_axis & 65535u)
   42|     ) * (1.0 / 1024.0);
   43|     return chunk.origin_world_size.xyz + centre_local;
   44| }
   45| 
   46| fn surfel_radius(packed: PackedSurfel) -> f32 {
   47|     return f32((packed.z_radius_axis >> 16u) & 255u) * (1.0 / 32.0);
   48| }
   49| 
   50| fn surfel_axis(packed: PackedSurfel) -> u32 {
   51|     return packed.z_radius_axis >> 24u;
   52| }
   53| 
   54| // The quad lies *in* the surface rather than facing the camera.
   55| //
   56| // A camera-facing billboard is the obvious way to draw a disc and it is
   57| // wrong here: where two walls meet, billboards from the two clouds
   58| // interpenetrate, and the seam crawls as the camera turns. A quad in the
   59| // tangent plane carries the surface's own depth at every fragment, so the
   60| // walls meet along their true intersection and stay there.
   61| //
   62| // It also removes the software splatter's hardest problem. That path holds
   63| // one depth per surfel and needs a per-pixel depth window to stop coplanar
   64| // neighbours arbitrating for pixels; here depth is interpolated across the
   65| // quad, so overlapping neighbours agree exactly and the ordinary depth test
   66| // is enough.
   67| fn surfel_world_position(packed: PackedSurfel, corner_index: u32) -> vec3<f32> {
   68|     let axis = surfel_axis(packed);
   69|     let normal = normal_for_axis(axis);
   70|     let radius = surfel_radius(packed);
   71|     let corner = vec2<f32>(
   72|         select(-1.0, 1.0, corner_index == 1u || corner_index == 3u),
   73|         select(-1.0, 1.0, corner_index >= 2u)
   74|     );
   75| 
   76|     // Lift a hair along the normal. A disc and the surface it samples are
   77|     // exactly coplanar, and exact coplanarity is the one configuration a
   78|     // depth buffer reliably z-fights on.
   79|     return surfel_centre(packed)
   80|         + normal * 0.0015
   81|         + surfel_u(axis) * corner.x * radius
   82|         + surfel_v(axis) * corner.y * radius;
   83| }
===== wasm_frontend/src/drivers/webgpu/shaders/raster_shadow.wgsl (92 lines) =====
    1| // Receiver-side hero shadow sampling shared by Surface and Splat.
    2| 
    3| @group(2) @binding(0) var<uniform> hero_shadow: HeroShadowUniforms;
    4| @group(2) @binding(1) var hero_shadow_depth: texture_depth_2d;
    5| @group(2) @binding(2) var hero_shadow_sampler: sampler_comparison;
    6| 
    7| fn hero_shadow_visibility(
    8|     world: vec3<f32>,
    9|     normal: vec3<f32>,
   10|     surface_to_light: vec3<f32>,
   11| ) -> f32 {
   12|     if hero_shadow.options.x == 0u {
   13|         return 1.0;
   14|     }
   15|     let clip = hero_shadow.light_view_projection
   16|         * vec4<f32>(world + normal * 0.0005, 1.0);
   17|     let projected = clip.xyz / max(abs(clip.w), 1e-8);
   18|     // WebGPU texture coordinates start at the top-left; NDC Y points up.
   19|     let uv = vec2<f32>(projected.x * 0.5 + 0.5, 0.5 - projected.y * 0.5);
   20|     let receiver_depth = projected.z;
   21|     if any(uv < vec2<f32>(0.0)) || any(uv > vec2<f32>(1.0))
   22|         || receiver_depth <= 0.0 || receiver_depth >= 1.0 {
   23|         return 1.0;
   24|     }
   25| 
   26|     let slope = 1.0 - clamp(dot(normal, surface_to_light), 0.0, 1.0);
   27|     let bias = max(hero_shadow.sampling.z, hero_shadow.sampling.w * slope);
   28|     let reference_depth = receiver_depth - bias;
   29|     if hero_shadow.options.z <= 1u {
   30|         return textureSampleCompareLevel(
   31|             hero_shadow_depth,
   32|             hero_shadow_sampler,
   33|             uv,
   34|             reference_depth
   35|         );
   36|     }
   37| 
   38|     let offsets = array<vec2<f32>, 4>(
   39|         vec2<f32>(-0.5, -0.5),
   40|         vec2<f32>( 0.5, -0.5),
   41|         vec2<f32>(-0.5,  0.5),
   42|         vec2<f32>( 0.5,  0.5)
   43|     );
   44|     var visibility = 0.0;
   45|     for (var tap = 0u; tap < 4u; tap += 1u) {
   46|         visibility += textureSampleCompareLevel(
   47|             hero_shadow_depth,
   48|             hero_shadow_sampler,
   49|             uv + offsets[tap] * hero_shadow.sampling.xy,
   50|             reference_depth
   51|         );
   52|     }
   53|     return visibility * 0.25;
   54| }
   55| 
   56| fn raster_surface_radiance(
   57|     world: vec3<f32>,
   58|     normal: vec3<f32>,
   59|     albedo: vec3<f32>,
   60|     baked: f32,
   61|     ao: f32,
   62|     light_first: u32,
   63|     light_count: u32,
   64| ) -> vec3<f32> {
   65|     var analytic_direct = vec3<f32>(0.0);
   66|     let safe_count = min(
   67|         light_count,
   68|         frame.render_options.x - min(light_first, frame.render_options.x)
   69|     );
   70|     for (var local = 0u; local < safe_count; local += 1u) {
   71|         let light_index = light_first + local;
   72|         let light = lights[light_index];
   73|         if light.half_size_kind.w < 0.5 {
   74|             continue;
   75|         }
   76|         var contribution = evaluate_scene_light(world, normal, light);
   77|         if hero_shadow.options.x != 0u && light_index == hero_shadow.options.y {
   78|             let delta = light.position_radius.xyz - world;
   79|             let surface_to_light = delta / sqrt(max(dot(delta, delta), 1e-8));
   80|             contribution *= hero_shadow_visibility(world, normal, surface_to_light);
   81|         }
   82|         analytic_direct += contribution;
   83|     }
   84|     return surface_radiance_from_analytic_direct(
   85|         world,
   86|         normal,
   87|         albedo,
   88|         baked,
   89|         ao,
   90|         analytic_direct
   91|     );
   92| }

   15|     @builtin(position) clip_position: vec4<f32>,

   21| fn supply_corner(index: u32) -> vec2<f32> {
   22|     switch index {
   23|         case 0u: { return vec2<f32>(-1.0, -1.0); }
   24|         case 1u: { return vec2<f32>( 1.0, -1.0); }
   25|         case 2u: { return vec2<f32>( 1.0,  1.0); }
   26|         case 3u: { return vec2<f32>(-1.0, -1.0); }
   27|         case 4u: { return vec2<f32>( 1.0,  1.0); }
   28|         default: { return vec2<f32>(-1.0, 1.0); }
   29|     }
   30| }
   31| 
   32| @vertex
   33| fn supply_label_vertex(
   34|     @builtin(vertex_index) vertex_index: u32,
   35|     @builtin(instance_index) sprite_index: u32,
   36| ) -> SupplyVertex {
   37|     let sprite = supply_sprites[sprite_index];
   38|     let corner = supply_corner(vertex_index);
   39|     let world = sprite.position_atlas_row.xyz
   40|         + frame.camera_right.xyz * (corner.x * 0.26)
   41|         + vec3<f32>(0.0, corner.y * 0.195, 0.0);
   42| 
   43|     var output: SupplyVertex;
   44|     output.clip_position = frame.view_projection * vec4<f32>(world, 1.0);
   45|     output.uv = vec2<f32>(corner.x * 0.5 + 0.5, 0.5 - corner.y * 0.5);
   46|     output.atlas_row = sprite.position_atlas_row.w;
   47|     output.world = world;
   48|     return output;
   49| }

   52| fn supply_label_fragment(input: SupplyVertex) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
   53|     let uv = vec2<f32>(input.uv.x, (input.uv.y + input.atlas_row) * 0.5);
   54|     let label = textureSample(supply_atlas, supply_sampler, uv);
   55|     if label.a < 0.5 {
   56|         discard;
   57|     }
   58| 
   59|     let view_distance = length(input.world - frame.camera_position.xyz);
   60|     let fog_distance = max(view_distance - frame.viewport_fov_start.w, 0.0);
   61|     let transmittance = exp(-max(frame.fog_color_density.w, 0.0) * fog_distance);
   62|     let radiance = mix(frame.fog_color_density.xyz, label.rgb * 0.92, transmittance);

The raster surface/splat WGSL shading (`raster_surface_radiance`) loops over per-chunk clustered light ranges (chunk.draw.x/y = light_first/light_count) — good, bounded by cluster. And `evaluate_scene_light` for rectangle lights loops 4 Gauss samples. And shadow sample 4 taps for the hero light. So the WGSL raster path is O(L_c × 4) per fragment — reasonable.

The WGSL raymarch path loops over ALL lights with per-light visibility traces — the hotspot.

Now let me check the remaining webgpu pipelines (surface.rs, splat.rs, surfel.rs, raster_shadow.rs, supply_labels.rs, cpu_present.rs, visibility.rs, mod.rs, config.rs, shader.rs) — mostly resource management. Let me read the important parts: pipelines/surface.rs, splat.rs (resource upload/removal, sorting?), visibility.rs (light clustering on GPU?), config.rs quickly.
===== wasm_frontend/src/drivers/webgpu/pipelines/visibility.rs (207 lines) =====
    1| use crate::application::ports::FrameParams;
    2| use crate::application::rendering::camera_basis;
    3| 
    4| /// Conservative chunk/cell sphere test shared by raster strategies.
    5| pub(super) fn sphere_is_visible(
    6|     center: [f32; 3],
    7|     radius: f32,
    8|     frame: &FrameParams,
    9|     max_distance: f32,
   10| ) -> bool {
   11|     let delta = [
   12|         center[0] - frame.camera_pos[0],
   13|         center[1] - frame.camera_pos[1],
   14|         center[2] - frame.camera_pos[2],
   15|     ];
   16|     let distance_squared = delta[0] * delta[0] + delta[1] * delta[1] + delta[2] * delta[2];
   17|     let reach = max_distance + radius.max(0.0);
   18|     if distance_squared > reach * reach {
   19|         return false;
   20|     }
   21|     let forward = camera_basis(frame.yaw, frame.pitch).forward;
   22|     let forward_distance = delta[0] * forward[0] + delta[1] * forward[1] + delta[2] * forward[2];
   23|     forward_distance + radius >= -0.03
   24| }
   25| 
   26| pub(super) fn bounds_sphere(origin: [f32; 3], bounds_max: [f32; 3]) -> ([f32; 3], f32) {
   27|     let half = [
   28|         bounds_max[0] * 0.5,
   29|         bounds_max[1] * 0.5,
   30|         bounds_max[2] * 0.5,
   31|     ];
   32|     (
   33|         [
   34|             origin[0] + half[0],
   35|             origin[1] + half[1],
   36|             origin[2] + half[2],
   37|         ],
   38|         (half[0] * half[0] + half[1] * half[1] + half[2] * half[2]).sqrt(),
   39|     )
   40| }
   41| 
   42| /// Signed world-space distance from a sphere center to one side plane of the
   43| /// perspective frustum, positive meaning inside. `axis` is `right` or `up`;
   44| /// `tan_half` is that axis's half-angle tangent (horizontal uses
   45| /// `fov_tan * aspect`, vertical uses `fov_tan` alone); `sign` selects which
   46| /// of the paired planes (+1 for the right/top plane, -1 for left/bottom).
   47| ///
   48| /// A point at forward-distance `along` and lateral offset `across` lies
   49| /// exactly on the `+axis` boundary plane when `across == tan_half * along`.
   50| /// The perpendicular distance from an arbitrary point to that plane is
   51| /// `(tan_half * along - across) * cos(theta_half)`, and
   52| /// `cos(theta_half) == 1 / sqrt(1 + tan_half^2)` exactly — no small-angle
   53| /// approximation, so it carries no extra risk of an over-eager cull.
   54| fn side_plane_distance(
   55|     delta: [f32; 3],
   56|     forward: [f32; 3],
   57|     axis: [f32; 3],
   58|     tan_half: f32,
   59|     sign: f32,
   60| ) -> f32 {
   61|     let dot = |a: [f32; 3], b: [f32; 3]| a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1] + a[2] * b[2];
   62|     let along = dot(delta, forward);
   63|     let across = dot(delta, axis) * sign;
   64|     (tan_half * along - across) / (1.0 + tan_half * tan_half).sqrt()
   65| }
   66| 
   67| /// Conservative sphere-vs-frustum side-plane test: `false` only when the
   68| /// sphere lies entirely outside at least one of the four side planes
   69| /// (left/right/top/bottom). Deliberately excludes near/far — those stay the
   70| /// job of [`sphere_is_visible`], which this is meant to be combined with.
   71| pub(super) fn frustum_side_planes_visible(
   72|     center: [f32; 3],
   73|     radius: f32,
   74|     frame: &FrameParams,
   75|     fov_tan: f32,
   76|     aspect: f32,
   77| ) -> bool {
   78|     let delta = [
   79|         center[0] - frame.camera_pos[0],
   80|         center[1] - frame.camera_pos[1],
   81|         center[2] - frame.camera_pos[2],
   82|     ];
   83|     let basis = camera_basis(frame.yaw, frame.pitch);
   84|     let tan_h = fov_tan * aspect.max(1e-6);
   85|     let tan_v = fov_tan;
   86| 
   87|     [
   88|         side_plane_distance(delta, basis.forward, basis.right, tan_h, 1.0),
   89|         side_plane_distance(delta, basis.forward, basis.right, tan_h, -1.0),
   90|         side_plane_distance(delta, basis.forward, basis.up, tan_v, 1.0),
   91|         side_plane_distance(delta, basis.forward, basis.up, tan_v, -1.0),
   92|     ]
   93|     .iter()
   94|     .all(|&d| d >= -radius)
   95| }
   96|

    1| //! Depth-tested supply-label overlay shared by the raster strategies.
    2| //!
    3| //! The application supplies only world-space centers and atlas rows. WGSL

   99|     /// Replaces the immutable label atlas. Invalid decoder output is ignored
  100|     /// and leaves the previous valid texture intact.
  101|     pub fn upload_atlas(
  102|         &mut self,
  103|         device: &wgpu::Device,
  104|         queue: &wgpu::Queue,
  105|         rgba: &[u8],
  106|         width: u32,
  107|         height: u32,
  108|     ) {
  109|         let Some(byte_len) = width
  110|             .checked_mul(height)
  111|             .and_then(|pixels| pixels.checked_mul(4))
  112|             .and_then(|bytes| usize::try_from(bytes).ok())
  113|         else {
  114|             return;
  115|         };
  116|         if width == 0 || height == 0 || rgba.len() != byte_len {
  117|             return;
  118|         }
  119| 
  120|         let atlas = create_atlas_texture(device, width, height);
  121|         queue.write_texture(
  122|             atlas.as_image_copy(),
  123|             rgba,
  124|             wgpu::TexelCopyBufferLayout {
  125|                 offset: 0,
  126|                 bytes_per_row: Some(width * 4),
  127|                 rows_per_image: Some(height),
  128|             },
  129|             wgpu::Extent3d {
  130|                 width,
  131|                 height,
  132|                 depth_or_array_layers: 1,
  133|             },
  134|         );
  135|         self.atlas = atlas;
  136|         self.bind_group = create_bind_group(
  137|             device,
  138|             &self.layout,
  139|             &self.sprites,
  140|             &self.atlas,
  141|             &self.sampler,
  142|         );
  143|         self.atlas_initialized = true;
  144|     }
  145| 
  146|     pub fn draw(
  147|         &self,
  148|         queue: &wgpu::Queue,
  149|         encoder: &mut wgpu::CommandEncoder,
  150|         target: &wgpu::TextureView,
  151|         depth: &wgpu::TextureView,
  152|         frame_resources: &FrameResources,
  153|         frame: &FrameParams,
  154|     ) {
  155|         let sprites: Vec<_> = frame
  156|             .supply_sprites
  157|             .iter()
  158|             .take(MAX_SUPPLY_SPRITES)
  159|             .map(GpuSupplySprite::from)
  160|             .collect();
  161|         if !self.atlas_initialized || sprites.is_empty() {
  162|             return;
  163|         }
  164|         queue.write_buffer(&self.sprites, 0, bytemuck::cast_slice(&sprites));
  165| 
  166|         let color_attachments = [Some(wgpu::RenderPassColorAttachment {
  167|             view: target,
  168|             resolve_target: None,
  169|             depth_slice: None,
  170|             ops: wgpu::Operations {
  171|                 load: wgpu::LoadOp::Load,
  172|                 store: wgpu::StoreOp::Store,
  173|             },
  174|         })];
  175|         let mut pass = encoder.begin_render_pass(&wgpu::RenderPassDescriptor {
  176|             label: Some("webgpu.supply-labels.pass"),
  177|             color_attachments: &color_attachments,
  178|             depth_stencil_attachment: Some(wgpu::RenderPassDepthStencilAttachment {
  179|                 view: depth,
  180|                 depth_ops: Some(wgpu::Operations {
  181|                     load: wgpu::LoadOp::Load,
  182|                     store: wgpu::StoreOp::Discard,
  183|                 }),
  184|                 stencil_ops: None,
  185|             }),
  186|             ..Default::default()
  187|         });
  188|         pass.set_pipeline(&self.pipeline);
  189|         pass.set_bind_group(0, frame_resources.bind_group(), &[]);
  190|         pass.set_bind_group(1, &self.bind_group, &[]);
  191|         pass.draw(0..6, 0..sprites.len() as u32);
  192|     }
  193| }

  185|     #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
  186|     pub fn draw(
  187|         &self,
  188|         queue: &wgpu::Queue,
  189|         encoder: &mut wgpu::CommandEncoder,
  190|         target: &wgpu::TextureView,
  191|         depth: &wgpu::TextureView,
  192|         frame_resources: &FrameResources,
  193|         frame: &FrameParams,
  194|         toggles: RenderToggles,
  195|         light_count: u32,
  196|         fov_tan: f32,
  197|         aspect: f32,
  198|     ) {
  199|         for chunk in self.chunks.values() {
  200|             let uniforms = GpuChunkUniforms {
  201|                 origin_world_size: [chunk.origin[0], chunk.origin[1], chunk.origin[2], 0.0],
  202|                 bounds_voxel_size: [
  203|                     chunk.bounds_max[0],
  204|                     chunk.bounds_max[1],
  205|                     chunk.bounds_max[2],
  206|                     chunk.voxel_size,
  207|                 ],
  208|                 draw: [0, light_count, 0, 0],
  209|             };
  210|             queue.write_buffer(&chunk.uniforms, 0, bytemuck::bytes_of(&uniforms));
  211|         }
  212|         if self.shadow.prepare(queue, frame, toggles.shadow_pass) {
  213|             self.draw_shadow_pass(encoder);
  214|         }
  215| 
  216|         let environment = frame.environment;
  217|         let clear_linear = if environment.outdoor {
  218|             environment.sky_color
  219|         } else {
  220|             environment.fog_color
  221|         };
  222|         let clear = encode_display_color(clear_linear);
  223|         let color_attachments = [Some(wgpu::RenderPassColorAttachment {
  224|             view: target,
  225|             resolve_target: None,
  226|             depth_slice: None,
  227|             ops: wgpu::Operations {
  228|                 load: wgpu::LoadOp::Clear(wgpu::Color {
  229|                     r: clear[0] as f64,
  230|                     g: clear[1] as f64,
  231|                     b: clear[2] as f64,
  232|                     a: 1.0,
  233|                 }),
  234|                 store: wgpu::StoreOp::Store,
  235|             },
  236|         })];
  237|         let mut pass = encoder.begin_render_pass(&wgpu::RenderPassDescriptor {
  238|             label: Some("webgpu.surface.pass"),
  239|             color_attachments: &color_attachments,
  240|             depth_stencil_attachment: Some(wgpu::RenderPassDepthStencilAttachment {
  241|                 view: depth,
  242|                 depth_ops: Some(wgpu::Operations {
  243|                     load: wgpu::LoadOp::Clear(1.0),
  244|                     store: wgpu::StoreOp::Store,
  245|                 }),
  246|                 stencil_ops: None,
  247|             }),
  248|             ..Default::default()
  249|         });
  250|         pass.set_pipeline(&self.pipeline);
  251|         pass.set_bind_group(0, frame_resources.bind_group(), &[]);
  252|         pass.set_bind_group(2, self.shadow.receiver_bind_group(), &[]);
  253|         for chunk in self.chunks.values() {
  254|             if toggles.distance_cull {
  255|                 let (center, radius) = bounds_sphere(chunk.origin, chunk.bounds_max);
  256|                 if !sphere_is_visible(center, radius, frame, self.max_draw_distance)
  257|                     || !frustum_side_planes_visible(center, radius, frame, fov_tan, aspect)
  258|                 {
  259|                     continue;
  260|                 }
  261|             }
  262|             // Keep the storage buffer alive and make its ownership explicit,
  263|             // even though vertex pulling references it through the bind group.
  264|             let _keep_alive = &chunk.vertices;
  265|             pass.set_bind_group(1, &chunk.bind_group, &[]);
  266|             pass.set_index_buffer(chunk.indices.slice(..), wgpu::IndexFormat::Uint32);
  267|             pass.draw_indexed(0..chunk.index_count, 0, 0..1);
  268|         }
  269|     }

  271|     /// Every resident indexed surface casts. Camera visibility cannot reject
  272|     /// an off-screen object whose shadow reaches an on-screen receiver.
  273|     fn draw_shadow_pass(&self, encoder: &mut wgpu::CommandEncoder) {
  274|         let mut pass = encoder.begin_render_pass(&wgpu::RenderPassDescriptor {
  275|             label: Some("webgpu.surface.hero-shadow-pass"),
  276|             color_attachments: &[],
  277|             depth_stencil_attachment: Some(wgpu::RenderPassDepthStencilAttachment {
  278|                 view: self.shadow.view(),
  279|                 depth_ops: Some(wgpu::Operations {
  280|                     load: wgpu::LoadOp::Clear(1.0),
  281|                     store: wgpu::StoreOp::Store,
  282|                 }),
  283|                 stencil_ops: None,
  284|             }),
  285|             ..Default::default()
  286|         });
  287|         pass.set_pipeline(&self.shadow_pipeline);
  288|         pass.set_bind_group(0, self.shadow.caster_bind_group(), &[]);
  289|         for chunk in self.chunks.values() {
  290|             let _keep_alive = &chunk.vertices;
  291|             pass.set_bind_group(1, &chunk.bind_group, &[]);
  292|             pass.set_index_buffer(chunk.indices.slice(..), wgpu::IndexFormat::Uint32);
  293|             pass.draw_indexed(0..chunk.index_count, 0, 0..1);
  294|         }
  295|     }

Interesting: WebGPU SurfacePipeline draw — `draw: [0, light_count, 0, 0]` — light_first=0, light_count=ALL frame lights for every chunk. So the WebGPU surface fragment shader loops over ALL lights for every fragment (raster_surface_radiance with light_first=0, light_count=frame light count). In contrast, WebGL2 surface uses per-chunk clustered ranges. So the WebGPU surface path does O(P × L) per frame with L = all frame lights (unclustered). That's another finding: WebGPU raster paths don't use per-chunk light clustering at all; every fragment evaluates every light (rectangular lights = 4 Gauss samples each). This is a real regression vs the WebGL2 path.

Also note draw_shadow_pass draws EVERY resident chunk into the shadow map with no culling — matches WebGL (documented) but shadow pass cost.

    1| //! Surfel cache and instanced disc pass.
    2| //!
    3| //! Structurally the splat pipeline with two deliberate omissions:
    4| //!
    5| //! * **No hero shadow pass.** The splat path casts shadows from a retained
    6| //!   greedy mesh. A surfel cloud has no mesh, and building one purely to
    7| //!   cast with would let the caster and the visible surface disagree about
    8| //!   the silhouette — a shadow whose outline does not match the thing
    9| //!   throwing it.

   11| //!   culling cells at extraction; a surfel cloud is a flat array, so a

  278|             depth_slice: None,
  279|             ops: wgpu::Operations {
  280|                 load: wgpu::LoadOp::Clear(wgpu::Color {
  281|                     r: clear[0] as f64,
  282|                     g: clear[1] as f64,
  283|                     b: clear[2] as f64,
  284|                     a: 1.0,
  285|                 }),
  286|                 store: wgpu::StoreOp::Store,
  287|             },
  288|         })];
  289|         let mut pass = encoder.begin_render_pass(&wgpu::RenderPassDescriptor {
  290|             label: Some("webgpu.splat.pass"),
  291|             color_attachments: &color_attachments,
  292|             depth_stencil_attachment: Some(wgpu::RenderPassDepthStencilAttachment {
  293|                 view: depth,
  294|                 depth_ops: Some(wgpu::Operations {
  295|                     load: wgpu::LoadOp::Clear(1.0),
  296|                     store: wgpu::StoreOp::Store,
  297|                 }),
  298|                 stencil_ops: None,
  299|             }),
  300|             ..Default::default()
  301|         });
  302|         pass.set_pipeline(&self.pipeline);
  303|         pass.set_bind_group(0, frame_resources.bind_group(), &[]);
  304|         pass.set_bind_group(2, self.shadow.receiver_bind_group(), &[]);
  305| 
  306|         for chunk in chunks {
  307|             if toggles.distance_cull {
  308|                 let (center, radius) = bounds_sphere(chunk.origin, chunk.bounds_max);
  309|                 if !sphere_is_visible(center, radius, frame, self.max_draw_distance)
  310|                     || !frustum_side_planes_visible(center, radius, frame, fov_tan, aspect)
  311|                 {
  312|                     self.stats.faces_dropped =
  313|                         self.stats.faces_dropped.saturating_add(chunk.face_count);
  314|                     continue;
  315|                 }
  316|             }
  317|             if face_budget_is_exhausted(
  318|                 toggles.face_budget,
  319|                 self.stats.faces_drawn,
  320|                 self.face_budget,
  321|             ) {
  322|                 self.stats.faces_dropped =
  323|                     self.stats.faces_dropped.saturating_add(chunk.face_count);
  324|                 continue;
  325|             }
  326|             let _keep_alive = &chunk.faces;
  327|             pass.set_bind_group(1, &chunk.bind_group, &[]);
  328|             if toggles.cell_culling && !chunk.cells.is_empty() {
  329|                 for cell in &chunk.cells {
  330|                     let center = [
  331|                         chunk.origin[0] + (f32::from(cell.cell[0]) + 0.5) * chunk.cell_size,
  332|                         chunk.origin[1] + (f32::from(cell.cell[1]) + 0.5) * chunk.cell_size,
  333|                         chunk.origin[2] + (f32::from(cell.cell[2]) + 0.5) * chunk.cell_size,
  334|                     ];
  335|                     let radius = conservative_cell_radius(chunk.cell_size);
  336|                     if !sphere_is_visible(center, radius, frame, self.max_draw_distance)
  337|                         || (toggles.distance_cull
  338|                             && !frustum_side_planes_visible(center, radius, frame, fov_tan, aspect))
  339|                     {
  340|                         self.stats.cells_culled = self.stats.cells_culled.saturating_add(1);
  341|                         continue;
  342|                     }
  343|                     let end = cell.offset.saturating_add(cell.count).min(chunk.face_count);
  344|                     if cell.offset < end {
  345|                         pass.draw(0..4, cell.offset..end);
  346|                         self.stats.faces_drawn =
  347|                             self.stats.faces_drawn.saturating_add(end - cell.offset);
  348|                         self.stats.draw_calls = self.stats.draw_calls.saturating_add(1);
  349|                     }
  350|                 }
  351|             } else {
  352|                 pass.draw(0..4, 0..chunk.face_count);
  353|                 self.stats.faces_drawn = self.stats.faces_drawn.saturating_add(chunk.face_count);
  354|                 self.stats.draw_calls = self.stats.draw_calls.saturating_add(1);
  355|             }
  356|         }
  357|     }
  358| 
  359|     /// Every resident packed face casts, independently from camera cells and
  360|     /// the visible-face budget. This path never materializes indexed geometry.
  361|     fn draw_shadow_pass(&self, encoder: &mut wgpu::CommandEncoder) {
  362|         let mut pass = encoder.begin_render_pass(&wgpu::RenderPassDescriptor {
  363|             label: Some("webgpu.splat.hero-shadow-pass"),
  364|             color_attachments: &[],
  365|             depth_stencil_attachment: Some(wgpu::RenderPassDepthStencilAttachment {
  366|                 view: self.shadow.view(),
  367|                 depth_ops: Some(wgpu::Operations {
  368|                     load: wgpu::LoadOp::Clear(1.0),
  369|                     store: wgpu::StoreOp::Store,
  370|                 }),
  371|                 stencil_ops: None,
  372|             }),
  373|             ..Default::default()
  374|         });
  375|         pass.set_pipeline(&self.shadow_pipeline);
  376|         pass.set_bind_group(0, self.shadow.caster_bind_group(), &[]);
  377|         for chunk in self.chunks.values() {
  378|             let _keep_alive = &chunk.faces;
  379|             pass.set_bind_group(1, &chunk.bind_group, &[]);
  380|             pass.draw(0..4, 0..chunk.face_count);
  381|         }

WebGPU splat sort: `chunks.sort_by` with `distance_squared(left.origin, ...)` computed inside the comparator — O(M log M) comparisons × O(1) distance computation. Fine for M~25.

Note: WebGPU splat draw passes `draw: [0, light_count, 0, 0]` — again light_first=0, light_count=all lights → per-vertex lighting loops over ALL lights (in splat_vertex → raster_surface_radiance). This is per-face-vertex (4 per face) — vertex-stage cost. With ~50-100k faces, 4 corners × L lights each... 100k faces × 4 × 60 lights = 24M light evaluations per frame on GPU vertex stage. Hmm, but this is GPU parallel. Still, the WebGL2 splat path used the top-16 selected lights via uniforms, while WebGPU splat loops over the whole light list per vertex (with early `continue` on `half_size_kind.w < 0.5` i.e., disabled lights only — no distance culling inside the loop; every light is evaluated fully, including 4 Gauss samples for rectangle lights, even if out of range!). Actually evaluate_scene_light → evaluate_rectangle_light computes area then loops 4 samples with finite_range_inverse_square — the weight becomes 0 if out of range but the work is still done. No distance-based early-out per light. So the WebGPU raster paths pay L × 4 ALU per vertex/fragment with no spatial pruning, unlike WebGL2 where the top-16 camera-ranked lights were selected CPU-side (MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS=16) for splat, and per-chunk clustering for surface.

So the top findings are solidifying:
1. WebGPU raster paths (surface/splat/surfel): every vertex evaluates ALL frame lights with no per-chunk clustering and no early range rejection (half_size_kind.w<0.5 only filters disabled). WebGL2 counterparts cluster per chunk. → High.
2. WebGPU raymarch: per-hit shading loops ALL lights; with direct visibility, per-light secondary ray tracing up to 4096 steps × 25 chunks. → High/Critical perf (only when shadow_pass + profile on; default? RenderToggles default shadow_pass probably true. Let me check default toggles. In compat preset for native it's false, but browser default toggles — let me check render_settings.rs default).
3. GLSL raymarch: shade_voxel_hit loops chunk light count × 4 Gauss × 25 chunks × 768 steps — even worse per light; but GLSL version gates light counts per chunk via clustering... the per-light visibility traces ALL 25 chunks each — O(L_c × 4 × C × S). Both are bad; WebGPU has a global budget (4096 total per light), GLSL has per-trace 768 budget with no global budget: per Gauss sample per light, up to 25×768 = 19,200 steps. GLSL is worse in the worst case.

Let me now check render_settings default toggles, and the remaining drivers files. Also check `ports.rs::active_scene_lights` for typical L.

  356| impl FrameParams {

  358|         let count = (self.dynamic_light_count as usize).min(self.dynamic_lights.len());
  359|         &self.dynamic_lights[..count]
  360|     }
  361| 
  362|     pub fn active_scene_lights(&self) -> &[LightSource] {
  363|         &self.scene_lights
  364|     }
  365| }
  366| 
  367| impl Default for FrameParams {
  368|     fn default() -> Self {
  369|         Self {
  370|             camera_pos: [0.0; 3],
  371|             yaw: 0.0,
  372|             pitch: 0.0,
  373|             flashlight: false,
  374|             dynamic_lights: [DynamicLight::default(); MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS],
  375|             dynamic_light_count: 0,
  376|             scene_lights: Vec::new(),
  377|             environment: Environment::default(),
  378|             supply_sprites: Vec::new(),
  379|         }
  380|     }
  381| }
  382| 
  383| /// Renderer-selected chunk artifacts, encoded as a stable compact bitfield.
  384| ///
  385| /// Collision and semantic data are application requirements and are always
  386| /// generated. These bits describe only optional presentation products, so a
  387| /// raymarcher never pays to build greedy faces and a rasterizer never pays to
  388| /// serialize GPU SVO nodes.
  389| #[repr(transparent)]
  390| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default)]
  391| pub struct RenderArtifactNeeds(u8);
  392| 
  393| impl RenderArtifactNeeds {
  394|     const INDEXED_SURFACE_MESH_BIT: u8 = 1 << 0;
  395|     const FACE_SPLATS_BIT: u8 = 1 << 1;
  396|     const SVO_NODES_BIT: u8 = 1 << 2;
  397|     /// Bricked hierarchy plus its dense voxel arena. Mutually exclusive with
  398|     /// [`Self::SVO_NODES_BIT`] in practice: both describe the same volume and
  399|     /// both land in `ChunkPayload::nodes`, so a renderer asks for one or the
  400|     /// other and never pays for the volume twice.
  401|     const BRICKS_BIT: u8 = 1 << 3;
  402|     /// Oriented surface discs. Derived from the same greedy quads as the
  403|     /// mesh and the face splats, so it costs the extraction pass but not a
  404|     /// second one.
  405|     const SURFELS_BIT: u8 = 1 << 4;
  406|     const KNOWN_BITS: u8 = Self::INDEXED_SURFACE_MESH_BIT
  407|         | Self::FACE_SPLATS_BIT
  408|         | Self::SVO_NODES_BIT
  409|         | Self::BRICKS_BIT
  410|         | Self::SURFELS_BIT;
  411| 
  412|     pub const NONE: Self = Self(0);
  413|     pub const SURFACE: Self = Self(Self::INDEXED_SURFACE_MESH_BIT);
  414|     pub const SPLAT: Self = Self(Self::FACE_SPLATS_BIT);
  415|     pub const RAYMARCH: Self = Self(Self::SVO_NODES_BIT);
  416|     /// What a brick-aware ray marcher asks for.
  417|     pub const BRICKS: Self = Self(Self::BRICKS_BIT);
  418|     /// What the surfel splatter asks for.
  419|     pub const SURFEL: Self = Self(Self::SURFELS_BIT);
  420|     pub const CPU: Self = Self(Self::SVO_NODES_BIT);
  421|     /// What a blanket request means: the union of what the shipped
  422|     /// renderers ask for, and nothing else.
  423|     ///
  424|     /// Deliberately *excludes* bricks, because they and the plain SVO both
  425|     /// land in `ChunkPayload::nodes` and only one encoding can occupy it,
  426|     /// so a blanket request has to name the one every consumer can decode.
  427|     ///
  428|     /// Deliberately excludes surfels too, for a different reason. They can
  429|     /// coexist with anything -- they occupy their own field -- but they are
  430|     /// a *third* encoding of the same surface, and a caller asking for
  431|     /// everything already receives two. Folding them in would charge every
  432|     /// mesh and splat frame for a few hundred thousand discs nothing reads.
  433|     /// Both exclusions are opt-in for the renderer that wants them.
  434|     pub const ALL: Self = Self(Self::KNOWN_BITS & !Self::BRICKS_BIT & !Self::SURFELS_BIT);
  435| 
  436|     pub const fn from_bits(bits: u8) -> Option<Self> {
  437|         if bits & !Self::KNOWN_BITS == 0 {
  438|             Some(Self(bits))
  439|         } else {
  440|             None
  441|         }
  442|     }
  443| 
  444|     pub const fn bits(self) -> u8 {
  445|         self.0
  446|     }
  447| 
  448|     pub const fn indexed_surface_mesh(self) -> bool {
  449|         self.0 & Self::INDEXED_SURFACE_MESH_BIT != 0
  450|     }
  451| 
  452|     pub const fn face_splats(self) -> bool {
  453|         self.0 & Self::FACE_SPLATS_BIT != 0
  454|     }
  455| 
  456|     pub const fn surfels(self) -> bool {
  457|         self.0 & Self::SURFELS_BIT != 0
  458|     }
  459| 
  460|     pub const fn svo_nodes(self) -> bool {
  461|         self.0 & Self::SVO_NODES_BIT != 0
  462|     }
  463| 
  464|     /// Whether the bricked encoding was asked for. False when the plain SVO
  465|     /// was also requested: `nodes` holds one encoding, and the SVO is the
  466|     /// one every consumer -- the WebGL marcher, the CPU splatter, the
  467|     /// collision walk -- knows how to read.
  468|     pub const fn bricks(self) -> bool {
  469|         self.0 & Self::BRICKS_BIT != 0 && self.0 & Self::SVO_NODES_BIT == 0
  470|     }
  471| 
  472|     /// Whether some node hierarchy must be built at all, in either encoding.
  473|     pub const fn needs_node_arena(self) -> bool {
  474|         self.svo_nodes() || self.bricks()
  475|     }
  476| 
  477|     pub const fn union(self, other: Self) -> Self {
  478|         Self(self.0 | other.0)
  479|     }
  480| 
  481|     pub const fn needs_surface_extraction(self) -> bool {
  482|         self.indexed_surface_mesh() || self.face_splats() || self.surfels()
  483|     }
  484| }
  485| 
  486| /// Abstraction over the actual renderer back end.
  487| /// Implemented by `drivers::webgpu::renderer::WebGpuRenderer` in the browser
  488| /// and by recording test doubles in native unit tests.
  489| pub trait RendererPort {
  490|     /// Optional presentation products consumed by this renderer. The default
  491|     /// preserves older test doubles while concrete renderers report the exact
  492|     /// representation they own.
  493|     fn artifact_needs(&self) -> RenderArtifactNeeds {
  494|         if self.uses_surface_meshes() {
  495|             RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE
  496|         } else {
  497|             RenderArtifactNeeds::RAYMARCH
  498|         }
  499|     }
  500| 
  501|     /// Compatibility query for older callers and test doubles. New code uses
  502|     /// [`Self::artifact_needs`]; true means some surface-derived representation
  503|     /// is required, not necessarily an indexed mesh.
  504|     fn uses_surface_meshes(&self) -> bool {
  505|         false
  506|     }
  507| 
  508|     /// Incrementally uploads newly loaded or refined chunk meshes.
  509|     fn upload_surfaces(&mut self, _chunks: &[SurfaceChunk<'_>]) {}
  510| 
  511|     /// Releases meshes for chunks that left the streaming footprint.
  512|     fn remove_surfaces(&mut self, _keys: &[SurfaceChunkKey]) {}
  513| 
  514|     /// Drops all resident meshes (used when noclipping to another level).
  515|     fn clear_surfaces(&mut self) {}
  516| 
  517|     /// Telemetry data from the CPU reference strategy, if applicable.
  518|     fn cpu_telemetry_string(&self) -> Option<String> {
  519|         None
  520|     }
  521| 
  522|     /// Uploads the merged SVO node atlas (four `u32` words per node, padded
  523|     /// in 1024-node rows; see `OctreeGpuSerializer` in the core).
  524|     fn upload_atlas(&mut self, texels: &[u32]);
  525| 
  526|     /// Uploads the merged dense voxel arena the brick nodes index into.
  527|     /// Ships alongside `upload_atlas` and is ignored by back ends that
  528|     /// requested the plain SVO encoding.
  529|     fn upload_brick_voxels(&mut self, _words: &[u32]) {}
  530| 
  531|     /// Overwrites whole atlas rows starting at `first_row` (1024 nodes per
  532|     /// row) without reallocating or re-uploading the rest of the atlas.
  533|     /// Returns `false` if the back end can't do partial updates (or has no
  534|     /// atlas yet), in which case the caller must fall back to `upload_atlas`.
  535|     fn upload_atlas_rows(&mut self, _first_row: u32, _texels: &[u32]) -> bool {
  536|         false
  537|     }
  538| 
  539|     /// Overwrites whole brick-arena rows starting at `first_row` (words per
  540|     /// row shared with `application::atlas::BRICK_ROW_WORDS`) without
  541|     /// reallocating or re-uploading the rest of the arena. Returns `false`
  542|     /// if the back end can't do partial brick updates (or has no arena
  543|     /// yet), in which case the caller must fall back to `upload_atlas` plus
  544|     /// `upload_brick_voxels` for the whole pool. Unlike `upload_atlas_rows`
  545|     /// this defaults to unsupported: `upload_brick_voxels` itself documents
  546|     /// that a back end may only ever replace its whole buffer, and the
  547|     /// default here preserves that for any back end that doesn't override it.
  548|     fn upload_brick_voxels_rows(&mut self, _first_row: u32, _words: &[u32]) -> bool {
  549|         false
  550|     }
  551| 
  552|     /// Receives the decoded RGBA label atlas (stacked product logos). Ships
  553|     /// once at boot; renderers without a sprite path simply ignore it.
  554|     fn upload_label_atlas(&mut self, _rgba: &[u8], _width: u32, _height: u32) {}
  555| 
  556|     /// Draws one frame: fullscreen raymarch of every chunk in `chunks`.
  557|     fn draw(&mut self, frame: &FrameParams, chunks: &[ChunkDraw]);
  558| }
  559| 
  560| /// A fully prepared chunk as the application consumes it.
  561| #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
  562| pub struct ChunkPayload {
  563|     /// Root node index local to this chunk's `nodes` array.
  564|     pub root: u32,
  565|     /// GPU-serialized node hierarchy (row-padded, 4 u32 per node).
  566|     ///
  567|     /// Holds the plain SVO encoding under [`RenderArtifactNeeds::RAYMARCH`]
  568|     /// and the bricked hierarchy under [`RenderArtifactNeeds::BRICKS`]. The
  569|     /// brick encoding is a strict superset -- internal and leaf nodes are
  570|     /// bit-identical, and only the brick-pointer kind is new -- so one array
  571|     /// and one atlas serve both.
  572|     pub nodes: Vec<u32>,
  573|     /// Dense voxel arena the brick nodes point into, empty unless
  574|     /// [`RenderArtifactNeeds::BRICKS`] was requested.
  575|     pub brick_voxels: Vec<u32>,
  576|     /// Side length of the SVO cube in world units.
  577|     pub world_size: f32,
  578|     /// Exact leaf size/depth used to build `nodes`.
  579|     pub voxel_size: f32,
  580|     pub svo_depth: u8,
  581|     /// Renderer-selected raster artifacts. Unrequested representations are
  582|     /// empty while bounds/LOD metadata stays valid for the selected path.
  583|     pub surface: SurfaceMeshPayload,
  584|     /// Renderer-neutral analytic emitters used by rendering and thermal
  585|     /// simulation even when no surface artifact was requested.
  586|     pub lights: Vec<LightSource>,
  587|     /// Solid-voxel bounding boxes in world space, for player collision.
  588|     pub collision: Vec<Aabb>,
  589|     /// Semantic threshold planes derived by the same generation snapshot as
  590|     /// the voxel grid. The engine folds crossings into the next reality.
  591|     pub traversal_gates: Vec<TraversalGate>,
  592|     /// Authored floor openings with deterministic recovery destinations.
  593|     pub pit_hazards: Vec<PitHazard>,
  594|     /// Consumable pickups exported beside the geometry.
  595|     pub supply_items: Vec<SupplyItem>,
  596|     /// Physical doorways to other Backrooms levels.
  597|     pub level_exits: Vec<LevelExit>,
  598| }
  599| 
  600| /// One background chunk-load order, echoed back verbatim with its result so
  601| /// the engine can reject stale work (wrong level, chunk no longer desired,
  602| /// or already refined past this LOD).
  603| #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
  604| pub struct ChunkRequest {
  605|     /// Monotonic identity assigned by the engine. A completion may only
  606|     /// clear the pending entry carrying this exact id; this prevents a late
  607|     /// result from an evicted/re-requested chunk from cancelling newer work.
  608|     pub request_id: u32,
  609|     pub origin_x: f32,
  610|     pub origin_z: f32,
  611|     pub level: u32,
  612|     pub lod: u8,
  613|     /// Compact renderer-owned presentation request, echoed by workers as part
  614|     /// of exact asynchronous request identity.
  615|     pub artifacts: RenderArtifactNeeds,
  616|     /// Immutable encounter state used to generate this chunk. It is part of
  617|     /// request identity, not ambient worker state.
  618|     pub reality: RealitySnapshot,
  619| }
  620| 
  621| impl ChunkRequest {
  622|     /// Exact identity check for asynchronous completion validation. Origins
  623|     /// compare by bits so this remains an identity operation rather than an
  624|     /// approximate spatial comparison.
  625|     pub fn is_same_request(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
  626|         self.request_id == other.request_id
  627|             && self.origin_x.to_bits() == other.origin_x.to_bits()
  628|             && self.origin_z.to_bits() == other.origin_z.to_bits()
  629|             && self.level == other.level
  630|             && self.lod == other.lod
  631|             && self.artifacts == other.artifacts
  632|             && self.reality == other.reality
  633|     }
  634| }
  635| 
  636| /// A finished background load.
  637| #[derive(Debug)]
  638| pub struct CompletedChunk {
  639|     pub request: ChunkRequest,
  640|     pub payload: ChunkPayload,
  641| }
  642| 
  643| /// Abstraction over where chunks come from. The browser build implements
  644| /// this with in-wasm procedural generation (`adapters::local_chunk_source`)
  645| /// or a Web Worker pool (`drivers::worker_source`); a networked build could
  646| /// implement it with HTTP fetches instead.
  647| pub trait ChunkSourcePort {
  648|     /// Loads the chunk at `origin` for the given Backrooms level
  649|     /// (0 = backrooms, 34 = grassland; see the core's `level_generator`).
  650|     ///
  651|     /// `lod` selects the level of detail: 0 is full resolution and each
  652|     /// step doubles the voxel size, costing ~1/8 as much to produce. Any
  653|     /// LOD of a chunk covers the same world cube (`world_size` invariant),
  654|     /// so payloads are interchangeable to the renderer.
  655|     fn load(&self, origin_x: f32, origin_z: f32, level: u32, lod: u8) -> ChunkPayload;
  656| 
  657|     /// Loads against an explicit immutable reality snapshot. Stateless
  658|     /// sources retain source compatibility through the default implementation;
  659|     /// procedural sources override this and route the snapshot into generation.
  660|     fn load_with_reality(
  661|         &self,
  662|         origin_x: f32,
  663|         origin_z: f32,
  664|         level: u32,
  665|         lod: u8,
  666|         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
  667|     ) -> ChunkPayload {
  668|         let _ = reality;
  669|         self.load(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod)
  670|     }
  671| 
  672|     /// Loads against an explicit reality while requesting only the optional
  673|     /// presentation products consumed by the active renderer. Sources that
  674|     /// do not specialize artifact production remain compatible by generating
  675|     /// their ordinary complete payload.
  676|     fn load_with_artifacts(
  677|         &self,
  678|         origin_x: f32,
  679|         origin_z: f32,
  680|         level: u32,
  681|         lod: u8,
  682|         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
  683|         artifacts: RenderArtifactNeeds,
  684|     ) -> ChunkPayload {
  685|         let _ = artifacts;
  686|         self.load_with_reality(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, reality)
  687|     }
  688| 
  689|     /// True when the source generates in the background. The engine then
  690|     /// drives it with [`Self::request`]/[`Self::poll_completed`] instead of
  691|     /// the blocking [`Self::load`], keeping the frame loop responsive.
  692|     fn is_async(&self) -> bool {
  693|         false
  694|     }
  695| 
  696|     /// Maximum useful number of simultaneous background requests. Async
  697|     /// transports override this so streaming can saturate their worker pool
  698|     /// without coupling the application layer to browser worker types.
  699|     fn max_concurrent_requests(&self) -> usize {
  700|         1
  701|     }
  702| 
  703|     /// Queues a background load. Deduplication is the caller's concern.
  704|     fn request(&mut self, _request: ChunkRequest) {}
  705| 
  706|     /// Takes every finished background load. Results may arrive in any
  707|     /// order and may be stale; the caller validates against its own state.
  708|     fn poll_completed(&mut self) -> Vec<CompletedChunk> {
  709|         Vec::new()
  710|     }
  711| 
  712|     /// Takes requests which the asynchronous transport definitively could
  713|     /// not complete. The engine validates the full request identity before
  714|     /// clearing pending state, then issues a fresh request on the same tick.
  715|     /// Synchronous sources and infallible test doubles need not override it.
  716|     fn poll_failed_requests(&mut self) -> Vec<ChunkRequest> {
  717|         Vec::new()
  718|     }
  719| }
  720| 
  721| #[cfg(test)]
  722| mod artifact_tests {
  723|     use super::RenderArtifactNeeds;
  724| 
  725|     #[test]
  726|     fn artifact_bitfield_round_trips_every_valid_combination() {
  727|         for bits in 0..=RenderArtifactNeeds::ALL.bits() {
  728|             let needs = RenderArtifactNeeds::from_bits(bits).expect("known bit combination");
  729|             assert_eq!(needs.bits(), bits);
  730|             assert_eq!(needs.indexed_surface_mesh(), bits & 1 != 0);
  731|             assert_eq!(needs.face_splats(), bits & 2 != 0);
  732|             assert_eq!(needs.svo_nodes(), bits & 4 != 0);
  733|         }
  734|         assert_eq!(RenderArtifactNeeds::from_bits(1 << 7), None);
  735|     }
  736| 
  737|     #[test]
  738|     fn renderer_artifact_sets_are_minimal_and_composable() {
  739|         assert!(RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE.indexed_surface_mesh());
  740|         assert!(!RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE.face_splats());
  741|         assert!(!RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE.svo_nodes());
  742| 
  743|         assert!(!RenderArtifactNeeds::SPLAT.indexed_surface_mesh());
  744|         assert!(RenderArtifactNeeds::SPLAT.face_splats());
  745|         assert!(!RenderArtifactNeeds::SPLAT.svo_nodes());
  746| 
  747|         assert_eq!(RenderArtifactNeeds::RAYMARCH, RenderArtifactNeeds::CPU);
  748|         assert!(RenderArtifactNeeds::CPU.svo_nodes());
  749|         assert_eq!(
  750|             RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE
  751|                 .union(RenderArtifactNeeds::SPLAT)
  752|                 .union(RenderArtifactNeeds::RAYMARCH),
  753|             RenderArtifactNeeds::ALL,
  754|         );
  755|     }
  756| 
  757|     /// Surfels are opt-in. They are a third encoding of a surface that
  758|     /// `ALL` already describes twice, so a blanket request must not build
  759|     /// them -- and a surfel renderer must not be handed a mesh instead.
  760|     #[test]
  761|     fn surfels_are_asked_for_or_not_built() {
  762|         assert!(RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFEL.surfels());
  763|         assert!(RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFEL.needs_surface_extraction());
  764|         assert!(!RenderArtifactNeeds::ALL.surfels());
  765|         assert!(!RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE.surfels());
  766|         assert!(!RenderArtifactNeeds::SPLAT.surfels());
  767|         // And it composes: a debug view wanting both is representable.
  768|         let both = RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE.union(RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFEL);
  769|         assert!(both.surfels() && both.indexed_surface_mesh());
  770|         assert!(RenderArtifactNeeds::from_bits(both.bits()).is_some());
  771|     }
  772| }
  200| pub struct ChunkDraw {
  201|     /// World-space origin (min corner) of the chunk's SVO cube.
  202|     pub origin: [f32; 3],
  203|     /// Root node index within the merged SVO atlas.
  204|     pub root_index: i32,
  205|     /// Side length of the chunk's SVO cube in world units.
  206|     pub world_size: f32,
  207|     /// Exact world-space edge length of a leaf voxel at this chunk's LOD.
  208|     /// Never infer this from `world_size`: the SVO cube is power-of-two
  209|     /// padded and deliberately larger than the logical chunk.
  210|     pub voxel_size: f32,
  211|     /// Exact SVO depth. Kept beside the voxel size so traversal has no
  212|     /// profile-specific constants or hidden maximum-depth guesses.
  213|     pub svo_depth: u8,
  214| }
  215| 
  216| /// Upper bound on per-frame dynamic lights handed to renderers (flares).
  217| pub const MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS: usize = 4;
  218| 
  219| /// Compatibility budget for callers that still expose fixed light arrays.
  220| /// Production WebGPU strategies use dynamically sized frame storage, but see
  221| /// [`MAX_ANALYTIC_SCENE_LIGHTS_PER_FRAME`] for the budget that actually
  222| /// bounds their per-fragment cost.
  223| pub const MAX_SCENE_LIGHTS: usize = 16;
  224| 
  225| /// Upper bound on how many fixtures the engine hands a production renderer
  226| /// for full per-fragment analytic evaluation in one frame.
  227| ///
  228| /// `select_scene_lights` deliberately never discards (a distant light can
  229| /// still be local to a visible receiver through a doorway), so the resident
  230| /// streaming neighborhood can easily hold 100+ enabled fixtures at once —
  231| /// every one of them gets a full rectangle-light quadrature per fragment in
  232| /// the raster shaders, uncapped, every frame. This budget is generous
  233| /// enough that ordinary rooms never notice it (nearest/most-important first,
  234| /// same ranking `select_scene_lights` already produces), while bounding the
  235| /// pathological case of a fixture-dense layout spanning a wide visual
  236| /// radius. Applied only to the copy handed to the renderer — thermal
  237| /// simulation and any other consumer of the full ranked list are unaffected.
  238| pub const MAX_ANALYTIC_SCENE_LIGHTS_PER_FRAME: usize = 48;
  239| 
  240| /// A short-lived runtime light (dropped flare). World-space state owned by
  241| /// the engine — never part of chunk payloads, baked light volumes, or the
  242| /// reality snapshot. Renderers treat it as one more point light; intensity
  243| /// already includes CPU-side flicker and fade so no shader needs a clock.
  244| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Default)]
  245| pub struct DynamicLight {
  246|     pub position: [f32; 3],
  247|     pub color: [f32; 3],
  248|     pub radius: f32,
  249|     pub intensity: f32,
  250| }
  251| 
  252| /// Per-level atmosphere handed to every renderer with the frame, so a level
  253| /// switch (noclip) changes the sky/fog/ambient identically in the surface,
  254| /// splat, raymarch, and CPU paths. `outdoor == false` means "keep your
  255| /// interior Backrooms look" — the colors below are only consulted outdoors,
  256| /// which keeps the four hand-tuned indoor palettes byte-identical.
  257| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
  258| pub struct Environment {
  259|     /// True on open-sky levels (the grassland). Renderers clear to
  260|     /// `sky_color`, fog toward `fog_color`, and scale ambient response.
  261|     pub outdoor: bool,
  262|     /// Clear color behind all geometry.
  263|     pub sky_color: [f32; 3],
  264|     /// Distance-fog blend target (slightly hazier than the sky).
  265|     pub fog_color: [f32; 3],
  266|     /// Multiplier on the ambient/indirect lighting response (>1 = daylight).
  267|     pub ambient_scale: f32,
  268|     /// Beer-Lambert extinction coefficient in inverse world units.
  269|     pub fog_density: f32,
  270|     /// Clear near-field distance before extinction begins.
  271|     pub fog_start: f32,
  272| }
  273| 
  274| impl Environment {
  275|     /// Level 0 and every other interior: renderers use their own palettes.
  276|     pub fn interior() -> Self {
  277|         Self {
  278|             outdoor: false,
  279|             sky_color: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
  280|             // Linear RGB; display encoding happens exactly once after fog.
  281|             fog_color: [0.020, 0.014, 0.0045],
  282|             ambient_scale: 1.0,

  383| /// Renderer-selected chunk artifacts, encoded as a stable compact bitfield.
  384| ///
  385| /// Collision and semantic data are application requirements and are always
  386| /// generated. These bits describe only optional presentation products, so a
  387| /// raymarcher never pays to build greedy faces and a rasterizer never pays to
  388| /// serialize GPU SVO nodes.
  389| #[repr(transparent)]
  390| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default)]
  391| pub struct RenderArtifactNeeds(u8);
  392| 
  393| impl RenderArtifactNeeds {
  394|     const INDEXED_SURFACE_MESH_BIT: u8 = 1 << 0;
  395|     const FACE_SPLATS_BIT: u8 = 1 << 1;
  396|     const SVO_NODES_BIT: u8 = 1 << 2;
  397|     /// Bricked hierarchy plus its dense voxel arena. Mutually exclusive with
  398|     /// [`Self::SVO_NODES_BIT`] in practice: both describe the same volume and
  399|     /// both land in `ChunkPayload::nodes`, so a renderer asks for one or the
  400|     /// other and never pays for the volume twice.
  401|     const BRICKS_BIT: u8 = 1 << 3;
  402|     /// Oriented surface discs. Derived from the same greedy quads as the
  403|     /// mesh and the face splats, so it costs the extraction pass but not a
  404|     /// second one.
  405|     const SURFELS_BIT: u8 = 1 << 4;
  406|     const KNOWN_BITS: u8 = Self::INDEXED_SURFACE_MESH_BIT
  407|         | Self::FACE_SPLATS_BIT
  408|         | Self::SVO_NODES_BIT
  409|         | Self::BRICKS_BIT
  410|         | Self::SURFELS_BIT;
  411| 
  412|     pub const NONE: Self = Self(0);
  413|     pub const SURFACE: Self = Self(Self::INDEXED_SURFACE_MESH_BIT);
  414|     pub const SPLAT: Self = Self(Self::FACE_SPLATS_BIT);
  415|     pub const RAYMARCH: Self = Self(Self::SVO_NODES_BIT);
  416|     /// What a brick-aware ray marcher asks for.
  417|     pub const BRICKS: Self = Self(Self::BRICKS_BIT);
  418|     /// What the surfel splatter asks for.
  419|     pub const SURFEL: Self = Self(Self::SURFELS_BIT);
  420|     pub const CPU: Self = Self(Self::SVO_NODES_BIT);
  421|     /// What a blanket request means: the union of what the shipped
  422|     /// renderers ask for, and nothing else.
  423|     ///
  424|     /// Deliberately *excludes* bricks, because they and the plain SVO both
  425|     /// land in `ChunkPayload::nodes` and only one encoding can occupy it,
  426|     /// so a blanket request has to name the one every consumer can decode.
  427|     ///
  428|     /// Deliberately excludes surfels too, for a different reason. They can
  429|     /// coexist with anything -- they occupy their own field -- but they are
  430|     /// a *third* encoding of the same surface, and a caller asking for

Key facts:
- Frame scene_lights can be 100+ fixtures; capped at MAX_ANALYTIC_SCENE_LIGHTS_PER_FRAME = 48 in the copy handed to renderer (per the comment — need to confirm where the cap is applied — in engine prepare_frame_lighting presumably; that's out of scope but the cap exists).
- WebGL2 raster drivers (surface/splat/surfel) select top-16 (MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS=16) camera-ranked lights for the uniform arrays — bounded 16.
- WebGPU raster drivers use the whole frame list (up to 48) with no clustering and no ranking. Every vertex of every face evaluates up to 48 lights × 4 Gauss samples.

Wait, actually for WebGPU surface: `draw: [0, light_count, 0, 0]` where light_count = lights.len() passed to pipeline.draw — which is `collect_frame_lights(frame).len()`. So all 48 max. And no distance rejection in shader (evaluate_scene_light computes everything). Actually wait — finite_range_inverse_square returns 0 quickly if d2 >= range2? Let's check: it computes rangeSquared, normalizedSquared, window = max(1 - ns², 0)... it still computes the full formula. There is no `if distanceSquared >= rangeSquared return 0` early-out in evaluate_scene_light — only in the WebGL2 splat shader (`if (d2 >= range2) continue;`). So WebGPU evaluates all lights fully.

So: WebGPU surface/splat fragment+vertex = O(L) per sample with no spatial pruning, L ≤ 48. WebGL2 = O(16) with early range rejection. Both bounded, but WebGPU's is 3× more lights and no early-out. The important nuance: WebGL2 splat has `if (d2 >= range2) continue` per light (early exit), WebGPU has none. And in WebGL2 the vertex shader light loop is 16 fixed, in WebGPU it's the full list.

Hmm, but the bigger problem: 100+ fixture lights, capped at 48 — the WebGPU raster shaders always pay 48 × 4 = 192 quadrature samples per vertex even when the light is across the map. The per-chunk clustering (append_lights_reaching_bounds) exists in WebGL2 but WebGPU doesn't use it at all for raster. This is a solid High finding.

Now, WebGPU raymarch: `raymarch_analytic_direct` loops `frame.render_options.x` lights (up to 48+4 dynamic), each with `finite_segment_visible` (when direct visibility enabled: profile capability && rt shadow_pass default true) — per light up to 4096 steps across 25 chunks. Worst case 52 × 4096 = 213k leaf lookups per pixel. With 1080p ≈ 2M pixels — utterly prohibitive; but real-world: `has_positive_rgb` gates most lights out (only lights near the surface contribute; the light's range check inside point_light_sample_irradiance returns 0 weight → has_positive_rgb false → skip visibility). So effective cost = number of lights within range of the hit point. In a dense corridor, maybe 10-30 lights in range → 30 × 4096 = 123k steps/pixel worst case, average maybe 100-1000 steps per light. Still the dominant cost. It's a genuine High/Critical perf issue — the parent's focus area. It is bounded by DIRECT_VISIBILITY_TRACE_BUDGET per light per pixel.

GLSL raymarch: worse — per light, per Gauss sample (4), per chunk (25) with 768-step loops, no global budget. `directSampleIsVisible` loop over uNumChunks with traceChunk inside (768 steps each). So O(L_c × 4 × C × 768). L_c = chunk light count (could be 40+ in a dense chunk). Unbounded (no cap on lightCount per chunk — the clustered list has no cap; append_lights_reaching_bounds has no slot cap. In the test, 40 lights all reach bounds). This is the worst shader: 40 lights × 4 samples × 25 chunks × 768 = 3M steps per pixel worst case. High/Critical.

Also GLSL raymarch `shade_voxel_hit` uses `uChunkLightCounts[receiverChunkIndex]` — the light count per chunk is derived from `append_lights_reaching_bounds` — no cap. And the scene light texture can be huge (all lights in frame). OK.

    1| //! Per-chunk GPU resources for the face-splat renderer.
    2| //!
    3| //! A chunk owns two representations derived from the same surface payload:
    4| //!
    5| //! * one packed instance page for the visible splat pass;
    6| //! * one retained greedy mesh used only as the hero-light shadow caster.
    7| //!
    8| //! WebGL2 has no `baseInstance`, so a cell-range draw re-points the four
    9| //! instance attributes at that range's byte offset before submission.

   11| use js_sys::{Uint8Array, Uint32Array};
   12| use wasm_bindgen::JsValue;
   13| use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlBuffer, WebGlProgram, WebGlVertexArrayObject};
   14|

   20| /// Bytes per packed face instance uploaded to WebGL.

   22| const SHADOW_VERTEX_STRIDE: i32 = 10;
   23| 
   24| /// Attribute locations are resolved once because every chunk uses the same
   25| /// packed instance layout.
   26| pub(crate) struct InstanceAttribs {
   27|     pos: u32,
   28|     extents: u32,
   29|     meta: u32,
   30|     flags: u32,
   31| }
   32| 
   33| impl InstanceAttribs {
   34|     pub(crate) fn resolve(gl: &Gl, program: &WebGlProgram) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
   35|         let lookup = |name: &str| -> Result<u32, JsValue> {
   36|             let location = gl.get_attrib_location(program, name);
   37|             if location < 0 {
   38|                 return Err(JsValue::from_str(&format!("splat shader lost {name}")));
   39|             }
   40|             Ok(location as u32)
   41|         };
   42| 
   43|         Ok(Self {
   44|             pos: lookup("aFacePos")?,
   45|             extents: lookup("aFaceExtents")?,
   46|             meta: lookup("aFaceMeta")?,
   47|             flags: lookup("aFaceFlags")?,
   48|         })
   49|     }
   50| 
   51|     fn enable(&self, gl: &Gl) {
   52|         for location in [self.pos, self.extents, self.meta, self.flags] {
   53|             gl.enable_vertex_attrib_array(location);
   54|             gl.vertex_attrib_divisor(location, 1);
   55|         }
   56|     }
   57| 
   58|     /// Records attribute pointers for a range beginning at `first_instance`.
   59|     /// The caller must have the chunk VAO and its instance buffer bound.
   60|     pub(crate) fn point_at(&self, gl: &Gl, first_instance: u32) {
   61|         let base = first_instance as i32 * INSTANCE_STRIDE;
   62|         gl.vertex_attrib_pointer_with_i32(
   63|             self.pos,
   64|             3,
   65|             Gl::UNSIGNED_SHORT,
   66|             false,
   67|             INSTANCE_STRIDE,
   68|             base,
   69|         );
   70|         gl.vertex_attrib_pointer_with_i32(
   71|             self.extents,
   72|             2,
   73|             Gl::UNSIGNED_BYTE,
   74|             false,
   75|             INSTANCE_STRIDE,
   76|             base + 6,
   77|         );
   78|         gl.vertex_attrib_pointer_with_i32(
   79|             self.meta,
   80|             4,
   81|             Gl::UNSIGNED_BYTE,
   82|             false,
   83|             INSTANCE_STRIDE,
   84|             base + 8,
   85|         );
   86|         gl.vertex_attrib_pointer_with_i32(
   87|             self.flags,
   88|             1,
   89|             Gl::UNSIGNED_BYTE,
   90|             false,
   91|             INSTANCE_STRIDE,
   92|             base + 12,
   93|         );
   94|     }
   95| }

========================= drivers/surfel_webgl/mod.rs (171 lines)
    1| //! Instanced surfel renderer — the WebGL2 disc splatter.
    2| //!
    3| //! One instance is one oriented disc (`PackedSurfel`). The vertex shader
    4| //! builds a square in the disc's own tangent plane from `gl_VertexID` and the
    5| //! fragment shader discards everything outside the inscribed circle.
    6| //!
    7| //! This is the splat driver with the entire shadow subsystem removed — no
    8| //! caster program, no framebuffer, no retained mesh, no second VAO. That is
    9| //! not a simplification for its own sake: a surfel cloud has no mesh to cast
   10| //! with, and building one purely to cast would let the caster and the visible
   11| //! surface disagree about the silhouette.
   12| //!
   13| //! The other structural difference is that a chunk draws in one call. The
   14| //! splat path buckets its face page into culling cells and re-points
   15| //! attributes per range because WebGL2 has no `baseInstance`; a surfel cloud
   16| //! is a flat array, so there is no range to point at.
   17| //!
   18| //! The module is split like its sibling:
   19| //!
   20| //! * this file owns composition, profile settings, the program and uniforms;
   21| //! * [`resources`] owns per-chunk GPU buffers and textures;
   22| //! * [`draw`] owns the frame pipeline and renderer-port implementation.
   23| //!
   24| //! The byte layout the instance buffer uses lives in
   25| //! [`crate::drivers::surfel_layout`], which compiles natively so it can be
   26| //! tested; everything in this module needs a live WebGL2 context.
   27| 
   28| mod draw;
   29| mod resources;
   30|

   32|

   34| use web_sys::{
   35|     HtmlCanvasElement, WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlProgram, WebGlUniformLocation,
   36| };

   38| use crate::application::ports::SurfaceChunkKey;

========================= drivers/surfel_layout.rs (120 lines)
    1| //! The byte layout one surfel takes on its way to WebGL, and the attribute
    2| //! names the vertex shader reads it back through.
    3| //!
    4| //! This is deliberately separate from [`crate::drivers::surfel_webgl`], which
    5| //! is `wasm32`-only and therefore untestable under `cargo test`. The layout is
    6| //! the part that can be silently wrong -- a shifted offset or a flipped byte
    7| //! order yields discs at plausible-looking wrong positions rather than an
    8| //! error -- so it lives where the test runner can reach it, following
    9| //! `generation_worker_requests`.
   10| 
   11| use crate::adapters::surfel_cloud::PackedSurfel;
   12| 
   13| /// Bytes per surfel uploaded to WebGL.
   14| ///
   15| /// `PackedSurfel` is 12 bytes. The upload pads to 16 to match
   16| /// `GpuPackedSurfel`'s WebGPU footprint, so the two backends describe one
   17| /// record rather than two, and so the stride stays a power of two.
   18| pub const SURFEL_STRIDE: i32 = 16;
   19| 
   20| /// `aSurfelPos` — disc centre, chunk-local fixed point at 1/1024 u.
   21| /// Three `UNSIGNED_SHORT`, unnormalized: the shader applies the scale.
   22| pub const ATTRIB_POS: &str = "aSurfelPos";
   23| pub const OFFSET_POS: i32 = 0;
   24| 
   25| /// `aSurfelMeta` — radius, normal_axis, material, baked_light.
   26| /// Four `UNSIGNED_BYTE`, unnormalized: radius decodes by `RADIUS_QUANT` and
   27| /// the other three are indices, none of which survive a 0..1 remap.
   28| pub const ATTRIB_META: &str = "aSurfelMeta";
   29| pub const OFFSET_META: i32 = 6;
   30| 
   31| /// `aSurfelFlags` — ao, flags (bit 0: emissive). Two `UNSIGNED_BYTE`.
   32| pub const ATTRIB_FLAGS: &str = "aSurfelFlags";
   33| pub const OFFSET_FLAGS: i32 = 10;
   34| 
   35| /// Serializes a cloud explicitly, so the GPU layout is stable across Rust
   36| /// compiler versions and host alignment rules. `pack_instances` in the splat
   37| /// driver does the same thing for the same reason.
   38| pub fn pack_surfels(surfels: &[PackedSurfel]) -> Vec<u8> {
   39|     let mut packed = Vec::with_capacity(surfels.len() * SURFEL_STRIDE as usize);
   40|     for surfel in surfels {
   41|         packed.extend_from_slice(&surfel.position[0].to_le_bytes());
   42|         packed.extend_from_slice(&surfel.position[1].to_le_bytes());
   43|         packed.extend_from_slice(&surfel.position[2].to_le_bytes());
   44|         packed.push(surfel.radius);
   45|         packed.push(surfel.normal_axis);
   46|         packed.push(surfel.material);
   47|         packed.push(surfel.baked_light);
   48|         packed.push(surfel.ao);
   49|         packed.push(surfel.flags);
   50|         packed.extend_from_slice(&[0, 0, 0, 0]);
   51|     }
   52|     packed
   53| }
   54|

   12|         // Encode raw RGBA bytes into a PNG file.
   13|         image::save_buffer(
