   23|     fn write_obj(&self, path: &Path, chunks: &[SurfaceChunk<'_>]) -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {
   24|         let mut file = fs::File::create(path)?;
   25| 
   26|         writeln!(file, "o backrooms_scene")?;
   27| 
   28|         let mut vertex_offset = 1; // OBJ indices are 1-based
   29| 
   30|         for chunk in chunks {
   31|             writeln!(file, "g chunk_{}_{}", chunk.key.0, chunk.key.1)?;
   32| 
   33|             for v in &chunk.mesh.vertices {
   34|                 let px = (v.position[0] as f32 / POSITION_FIXED_SCALE) + chunk.origin[0];
   35|                 let py = (v.position[1] as f32 / POSITION_FIXED_SCALE) + chunk.origin[1];
   36|                 let pz = (v.position[2] as f32 / POSITION_FIXED_SCALE) + chunk.origin[2];
   37|                 writeln!(file, "v {:.6} {:.6} {:.6}", px, py, pz)?;
   38|             }
   39| 
   40|             let mut i = 0;
   41|             while i + 2 < chunk.mesh.indices.len() {
   42|                 let i1 = (chunk.mesh.indices[i] as usize) + vertex_offset;
   43|                 let i2 = (chunk.mesh.indices[i + 1] as usize) + vertex_offset;
   44|                 let i3 = (chunk.mesh.indices[i + 2] as usize) + vertex_offset;
   45|                 writeln!(file, "f {} {} {}", i1, i2, i3)?;
   46|                 i += 3;
   47|             }
   48| 
   49|             vertex_offset += chunk.mesh.vertices.len();
   50|         }
   51| 
   52|         Ok(())
   53|     }
   54| }

========================= application/generation_worker_policy.rs (176 lines)
    1| //! Select concurrency for the browser's chunk-generation worker pool.
    2| //!
    3| //! This policy configures world generation and streaming only. The software
    4| //! splat renderer remains on the browser's main thread. Keeping query parsing
    5| //! and hardware clamping here makes the contract natively testable and keeps
    6| //! browser APIs out of the application layer.
    7| 
    8| /// Safety ceiling for generation workers — not a target. `Auto` should use
    9| /// every hardware thread the browser reports (minus one reserved for the
   10| /// main/render thread), including on high-core-count machines; this only
   11| /// guards against a browser misreporting an absurd `hardwareConcurrency`
   12| /// value and spawning an unreasonable number of Worker instances (each one
   13| /// duplicates the WASM module and atlas-building scratch memory).
   14| pub const MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS: u8 = 32;
   15| 
   16| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   17| pub enum GenerationWorkerPreference {
   18|     /// Reserve one reported hardware thread for the browser/render loop.
   19|     Auto,
   20|     /// Generate synchronously through `LocalChunkSource` on the main thread.
   21|     Disabled,
   22|     /// Request an explicit number, still bounded by reported hardware.
   23|     Fixed(u8),
   24| }
   25| 
   26| impl Default for GenerationWorkerPreference {
   27|     fn default() -> Self {
   28|         Self::Auto
   29|     }
   30| }
   31| 
   32| impl GenerationWorkerPreference {
   33|     /// Resolve a safe pool size from `Navigator.hardwareConcurrency`.
   34|     /// Unknown/invalid reports use the conservative historical fallback of
   35|     /// two hardware threads; automatic selection therefore uses one worker.
   36|     pub fn resolve(self, hardware_concurrency: f64) -> usize {
   37|         if self == Self::Disabled {
   38|             return 0;
   39|         }
   40| 
   41|         let reported_threads = if hardware_concurrency.is_finite() && hardware_concurrency >= 1.0 {
   42|             hardware_concurrency.floor().min(u32::MAX as f64) as u32
   43|         } else {
   44|             2
   45|         };
   46|         let auto_workers = reported_threads
   47|             .saturating_sub(1)
   48|             .clamp(1, u32::from(MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS)) as u8;
   49|         let fixed_worker_ceiling =
   50|             reported_threads.clamp(1, u32::from(MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS)) as u8;
   51|         match self {
   52|             Self::Auto => auto_workers,
   53|             Self::Fixed(requested) => requested.clamp(1, fixed_worker_ceiling),
   54|             Self::Disabled => 0,
   55|         }
   56|         .into()
   57|     }
   58| }
   59| 
   60| /// Parses the last exact `workers` query pair. Canonical values are `auto`,
   61| /// `0`, and positive integers; oversized integers clamp to the product cap.
   62| /// Missing or malformed values safely restore automatic selection.
   63| pub fn parse_generation_worker_preference(query: &str) -> GenerationWorkerPreference {
   64|     let mut preference = GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto;
   65|     for (key, value) in query
   66|         .trim_start_matches('?')
   67|         .split('&')
   68|         .filter_map(|pair| pair.split_once('='))
   69|     {
   70|         if key != "workers" {
   71|             continue;
   72|         }
   73|         preference = match value {
   74|             "auto" => GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto,
   75|             "0" => GenerationWorkerPreference::Disabled,
   76|             _ => value
   77|                 .parse::<u32>()
   78|                 .ok()
   79|                 .filter(|requested| *requested > 0)
   80|                 .map(|requested| {
   81|                     GenerationWorkerPreference::Fixed(
   82|                         requested.min(u32::from(MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS)) as u8,
   83|                     )
   84|                 })
   85|                 .unwrap_or(GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto),
   86|         };
   87|     }
   88|     preference
   89| }
   90|

===== static/worker.js (106 lines) =====
    1| // Generation worker: a second instance of the same wasm module, producing
    2| // renderer-selected chunk artifacts off the main thread. The handler is
    3| // registered synchronously at module scope so no message can be lost while
    4| // the wasm module is still instantiating; work is serialized through a
    5| // promise chain.
    6| //
    7| // Protocol (main -> worker):
    8| //   { type: "init", query, seed }        one-time generator setup
    9| //   { type: "gen", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality }
   10| //                   one chunk order; artifacts is a u8 bitfield and reality
   11| //                   is Uint32Array
   12| // (worker -> main):
   13| //   { type: "done", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality, ms, buf }
   14| //                                   buf transferred, encoded by chunk_codec
   15| //   { type: "failed", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality, message }
   16| //                                   one request failed and may be retried
   17| //   { type: "fatal", message }      worker initialization failed
   18| import init, { worker_init, worker_generate } from "./pkg/wasm_frontend.js";
   19| 
   20| let wasmReady = null;
   21| function ensureWasm() {
   22|   if (!wasmReady) wasmReady = init();
   23|   return wasmReady;
   24| }
   25| 
   26| let queue = Promise.resolve();
   27| 
   28| function errorMessage(error) {
   29|   if (error instanceof Error) return error.message;
   30|   return String(error);
   31| }
   32| 
   33| function reportFailure(message, error) {
   34|   const description = errorMessage(error);
   35|   console.error("[WORKER] generation failure:", description);
   36|   try {
   37|     if (message?.type === "gen") {
   38|       postMessage({
   39|         type: "failed",
   40|         requestId: message.requestId,
   41|         ox: message.ox,
   42|         oz: message.oz,
   43|         level: message.level,
   44|         lod: message.lod,
   45|         artifacts: message.artifacts,
   46|         reality: new Uint32Array(message.reality),
   47|         message: description,
   48|       });
   49|     } else {
   50|       postMessage({ type: "fatal", message: description });
   51|     }
   52|   } catch (reportError) {
   53|     // The browser's Worker error event is the final recovery path when even
   54|     // the structured failure message cannot be cloned or delivered.
   55|     console.error("[WORKER] could not report generation failure:", reportError);
   56|   }
   57| }
   58| 
   59| async function processMessage(message) {
   60|   await ensureWasm();
   61|   if (message.type === "init") {
   62|     worker_init(message.query, message.seed >>> 0);
   63|     return;
   64|   }
   65|   if (message.type !== "gen") return;
   66| 
   67|   const t0 = performance.now();
   68|   const reality = new Uint32Array(message.reality);
   69|   const bytes = worker_generate(
   70|     message.requestId >>> 0,
   71|     message.ox,
   72|     message.oz,
   73|     message.level,
   74|     message.lod,
   75|     message.artifacts >>> 0,
   76|     reality
   77|   );
   78|   const ms = performance.now() - t0;
   79|   console.debug(
   80|     `[WORKER] chunk (${message.ox}, ${message.oz}) lod ${message.lod} generated in ${ms.toFixed(1)} ms`
   81|   );
   82|   postMessage(
   83|     {
   84|       type: "done",
   85|       requestId: message.requestId,
   86|       ox: message.ox,
   87|       oz: message.oz,
   88|       level: message.level,

   91|       reality,
   92|       ms,
   93|       buf: bytes.buffer,
   94|     },
   95|     [bytes.buffer]
   96|   );
   97| }
   98| 
   99| onmessage = (event) => {
  100|   const message = event.data;
  101|   // Catch each queue item independently. A failed request must not leave the
  102|   // promise chain rejected, which would silently skip every later request.
  103|   queue = queue
  104|     .then(() => processMessage(message))
  105|     .catch((error) => reportFailure(message, error));
  106| };

worker.js analysis:

1. **Unbounded queue**: `queue = queue.then(...)` — messages posted to the worker are queued in the JS promise chain unboundedly. The main thread assigns work only to workers that are "accepting" (in_flight queue in GenerationWorkerRequests), and streaming is bounded by max_concurrent_requests... but requests can be assigned to a worker whose promise chain already has many pending messages? Let's think: main thread's `request()` → `next_accepting(preferred)` picks the first worker with accepting_work=true. `accepting_work` only becomes false on disable_and_drain (worker failure). So all workers always accept work regardless of how many messages are queued in their promise chain. The engine bounds total in-flight requests by max_concurrent_requests() = pool_size. So at most pool_size outstanding requests total → each worker ≤ 1 pending... wait, is that so? The engine's streaming drives `request()` up to max_concurrent_requests concurrently. If the engine only issues requests when in-flight count < max_concurrent_requests, then each worker has at most 1 in-flight request at a time. But note the request → post_message → worker processes serially. If the engine issues a new request before the previous completes, the worker gets 2 messages queued. Given the engine's bookkeeping, requests are issued as completions come in... Actually the engine keeps at most max_concurrent_requests in flight, so with pool_size workers, at most pool_size messages outstanding — the worker promise chain queue length ≤ 1 per worker (since a worker completes before... no — the main thread can issue a new request to the same worker before the previous completes if other workers are also busy? If all pool_size slots are in flight, and one completes, the engine issues exactly one new request, possibly to the same worker that just completed. So queue depth ≤ 1. OK, but the worker-side promise chain is unbounded in principle — if the main thread ever posts faster (e.g., the fallback path or a burst after failure), messages queue up with no cap. The in_flight VecDeque in GenerationWorkerRequests is also unbounded (push_back with no cap). If the engine bugged or called request() more than max_concurrent_requests, it would grow without bound. Also: a worker that is slow (each chunk takes 42ms) — the engine keeps issuing requests as completions arrive, so ≤ 1 outstanding per worker on average. So bounded in practice by the engine's credit system. Medium/Low finding: no explicit backpressure at the driver boundary; worker promise chain unbounded if the engine's credit accounting ever diverges.

2. **Message ordering / lost replies**: worker serializes via promise chain — replies are posted in the same order as messages processed (order preserved per worker). The exact-match validation in finish_exact handles staleness. But there's a subtle race: **reality cloning**. `const reality = new Uint32Array(message.reality);` — the worker copies the reality words; main thread's `request()` builds `reality` from `request.reality.to_words()` — a fresh Uint32Array per message, no transfer, so no race there.

3. **The transfer** `[bytes.buffer]` transfers the buffer. decode on main via parse_payload → Uint8Array::new(&buffer).to_vec() — copies. Fine.

4. **Failure path**: `reportFailure` catches exceptions during `processMessage` — including a failure of `postMessage` itself? If `postMessage({type:"done"...})` throws (e.g., buffer transfer error), the catch calls `reportFailure(message, error)` — which tries to post a "failed" reply with `reality: new Uint32Array(message.reality)` — that works. OK.

5. **Race between worker replies and rAF**: main thread message events and rAF are both on the JS event loop; poll_completed is called during engine.tick inside rAF. Since JS is single-threaded, no data race; ordering is by event loop. Stale data handled by request id validation in engine.

6. **Fatal handling**: `WorkerReply::Fatal` → disable_and_drain + terminate. But a fatal message could also be followed by worker error event → disable_and_drain called twice — harmless (documented). But note: after `terminate()`, a `done` message already queued in the event loop may still be delivered? Per spec, terminate discards queued tasks. The `finished` handler uses worker_index captured by closure — after terminate, any queued message events are dropped, so fine.

7. **Missing: no timeout/hang detection**: a worker that hangs (infinite loop in wasm) never replies; the request stays in in_flight forever; the engine never fails it; streaming stalls on that chunk forever. There's no watchdog. That's a real robustness gap: "lost replies" — a hung worker permanently occupies its slot and its chunk never resolves. Also `max_concurrent_requests` = pool_size means if one worker hangs, capacity drops. Severity Medium (hang detection missing).

8. **Worker spawn**: `Worker::new_with_options` — synchronous spawn, error → Err → fallback to same-thread. OK.

9. **postMessage ordering with init**: init is posted after handlers are set — fine. But note `worker_index` captured in closures by value — each closure has its own index. Good.

10. **reported_emergency_fallback** — only warns once, but keeps falling back on every request while pool is exhausted — sync generation on main thread per request → main-thread jank. Acceptable given it's the fallback.

Now, one more subtle issue in worker_source.rs: In the `request()` method, `assign` is called BEFORE `post_message`. If post_message fails → disable_and_drain drains the assigned request — good. But if post_message succeeds, the request is in in_flight. If the worker dies without replying and without error event (e.g., terminated by browser), the request stays forever. Again no timeout.

Another subtle issue: `next_accepting` is called on `self.requests.borrow()` then `assign` on `borrow_mut()` — two separate borrows, no interleaving issue (single-threaded).

**Potential race on `WorkerReply::Completed` vs engine re-request**: `finish_exact` returns true only for the exact request; if the request was already failed and re-issued with a new id, the stale reply is dropped. Good.

Now lib.rs — the atomics + spawn_local + settings crossing JS boundary.
//! # wasm_frontend — browser client for the vackrooms voxel engine
//!
//! This crate is the *outer rings* of the engine's Clean Architecture when it
//! runs in a browser. The dependency rule points strictly inward:
//!
//! ```text
//! drivers (portable WebGPU + wasm DOM)  <- outer layer
//!    |
//! adapters (input mapping, SVO atlas, local chunk source)
//!    |
//! application (player physics, streaming policy, frame orchestration, ports)
//!    |
//! vackrooms core (entities + use cases: VoxelGrid, SVO, generation, lighting)
//! ```
//!
//! * `application` and `adapters` are platform-agnostic and unit-tested with
//!   plain `cargo test` on the host.
//! * Portable WebGPU pipeline/configuration modules also compile natively for
//!   headless Vulkan tests; DOM, events, surfaces, and rAF remain wasm-only.
//! * The `#[wasm_bindgen(start)]` entry point below is the composition root:
//!   it wires concrete drivers into the application's ports.

pub mod adapters;
pub mod application;
pub mod drivers;
pub mod reference;

#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU32, Ordering};

#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
pub static DOOM_CONTROLS: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

/// Mouse look inversion (Y axis).
#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
pub static INVERT_Y: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

/// Mouse sensitivity multiplier, stored as f32 bits. 1.0 = default.
#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
pub static MOUSE_SENSITIVITY_BITS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0x3F80_0000); // 1.0f32

/// Manual internal-resolution override as f32 bits; 0.0 = automatic
/// (adaptive governor).
#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
pub static RENDER_SCALE_BITS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);

/// Anomaly debug overlay visibility (settings switch and the F3 key).
#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
pub static ANOMALY_DEBUG: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

/// Accessibility: automatic consumption of carried supplies when a vital
/// runs low. Off by default — drinking and eating are deliberate acts. The
/// frame loop forwards this to the engine each HUD refresh.
#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
pub static ASSISTED_CONSUMPTION: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
#[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
pub fn set_anomaly_debug(enabled: bool) {
    ANOMALY_DEBUG.store(enabled, Ordering::Relaxed);
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
#[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
pub fn set_assisted_consumption(enabled: bool) {
    ASSISTED_CONSUMPTION.store(enabled, Ordering::Relaxed);
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
#[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
pub fn set_doom_controls(enabled: bool) {
    DOOM_CONTROLS.store(enabled, Ordering::Relaxed);
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
#[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
pub fn set_invert_y(enabled: bool) {
    INVERT_Y.store(enabled, Ordering::Relaxed);
}

/// Mouse/touch look sensitivity multiplier (clamped to 0.1–5.0).
#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
#[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
pub fn set_mouse_sensitivity(multiplier: f32) {
    let m = if multiplier.is_finite() {
        multiplier.clamp(0.1, 5.0)
    } else {
        1.0
    };
    MOUSE_SENSITIVITY_BITS.store(m.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
}

/// Forces the internal render resolution scale (0.25–1.0), or restores the
/// adaptive governor when `scale` is 0.
#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
#[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
pub fn set_render_scale(scale: f32) {
    let s = if scale.is_finite() && scale > 0.0 {
        scale.clamp(0.25, 1.0)
    } else {
        0.0
    };
    RENDER_SCALE_BITS.store(s.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
}

/// CPU render settings are atomics only at the browser boundary. Every
/// public setter rebuilds and validates a typed `CpuRenderSettings` snapshot;
/// the splatter itself never reads these globals.

/// Applies one of the typed quality profiles. Individual optimization
/// switches are intentionally untouched.
#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
#[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
pub fn set_cpu_quality_preset(preset_id: u32) {

lib.rs atomics: all Relaxed, single f32 via bits — each atomic store of a u32 is atomic; torn reads impossible since u32 stores are atomic on wasm32 (single word). Multi-word state (CpuRenderSettings) is snapshotted by loading each atomic separately in get_cpu_settings — a concurrent JS settings write between two loads can produce a mixed snapshot (e.g., scale from new preset but max splat radius from old). That's a benign race in practice (JS settings writes are user-driven, and the snapshot is read per frame), but it's a genuine non-atomic multi-word read: get_cpu_settings loads 8 atomics individually — a mid-frame settings change could yield a torn *combination*. Severity Low (visual-only, rare).

Also `RENDER_SCALE_BITS` and the governor — fine.

Let me check the rest of lib.rs (spawn_local at 1061) and get_cpu_settings + set_* functions.

}

/// Renderer optimization toggles as a bitfield — see
/// [`application::render_settings::RenderToggles`]. Initialized from the URL
/// query at boot; the settings menu flips individual switches afterwards.
#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
pub static RENDER_TOGGLE_BITS: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(u32::MAX);

/// Flips one renderer optimization switch by name (`"hiz"`, `"f2b"`,
/// `"skip"`, `"mips"`, `"beam_occlusion"`, `"shadows"`, `"cells"`,
/// `"deferred"`, `"ao"`, `"cull"`, `"budget"`, `"dither"`, and `"bake"`).
/// Unknown names are ignored.
#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
#[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
pub fn set_render_toggle(name: &str, enabled: bool) {
    let mut toggles = get_render_toggles();
    toggles.set(name, enabled);
    RENDER_TOGGLE_BITS.store(toggles.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
}

/// Returns one renderer switch by its short URL name. This small diagnostic
/// export lets the settings UI and browser smoke tests verify the effective
/// state after URL and local-preference overrides have been composed.
#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
#[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
pub fn render_toggle_enabled(name: &str) -> Option<bool> {
    get_render_toggles().enabled(name)
}

/// Snapshot of the toggle switchboard, taken once per frame by each driver
/// and passed by value into the platform-free render code.
#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
pub fn get_render_toggles() -> crate::application::render_settings::RenderToggles {
    let bits = RENDER_TOGGLE_BITS.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
    if bits == u32::MAX {
        crate::application::render_settings::RenderToggles::default()
    } else {
        crate::application::render_settings::RenderToggles::from_bits(bits)
    }
}

/// Boot-time initialization from the URL query (`?rt_<name>=0|1`).
#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
pub fn init_render_toggles(query: &str) {
    let toggles = crate::application::render_settings::parse_render_toggles(query);
    RENDER_TOGGLE_BITS.store(toggles.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
pub fn get_cpu_settings() -> crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::CpuRenderSettings {
    let scale = f32::from_bits(CPU_SCALE_BITS.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
    let lod_cutoff = f32::from_bits(CPU_LOD_CUTOFF_BITS.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
    let max_splat_radius = f32::from_bits(CPU_MAX_SPLAT_RADIUS_BITS.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
    let max_virtual_depth = CPU_MAX_VIRTUAL_DEPTH.load(Ordering::Relaxed) as u8;
    let min_mip_occupancy = f32::from_bits(CPU_MIN_MIP_OCCUPANCY_BITS.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
    let max_draw_dist = f32::from_bits(CPU_MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE_BITS.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
    let shadow_mode = CPU_SHADOWS.load(Ordering::Relaxed);

    crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::CpuRenderSettings {
        internal_scale: scale,
        lod_cutoff_px: lod_cutoff,
        max_splat_radius_px: max_splat_radius,
        max_virtual_depth,
        min_mip_occupancy,
        max_draw_distance: max_draw_dist,
        shadows: crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::CpuShadowMode::from_id(shadow_mode),
        ..crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::CpuRenderSettings::default()
    }
    .validated()
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
fn update_cpu_settings(update: impl FnOnce(&mut crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::CpuRenderSettings)) {
    let mut settings = get_cpu_settings();
    update(&mut settings);
    store_cpu_settings(settings);
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
fn store_cpu_settings(settings: crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::CpuRenderSettings) {
    let settings = settings.validated();
    CPU_SCALE_BITS.store(settings.internal_scale.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
    CPU_LOD_CUTOFF_BITS.store(settings.lod_cutoff_px.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
    CPU_MAX_SPLAT_RADIUS_BITS.store(settings.max_splat_radius_px.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
    CPU_MAX_VIRTUAL_DEPTH.store(settings.max_virtual_depth as u32, Ordering::Relaxed);
    CPU_MIN_MIP_OCCUPANCY_BITS.store(settings.min_mip_occupancy.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
    CPU_MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE_BITS.store(settings.max_draw_distance.to_bits(), Ordering::Relaxed);
    CPU_SHADOWS.store(settings.shadows.id(), Ordering::Relaxed);
}

#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
mod entry {
    use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;

    /// Composition root. Runs automatically when the wasm module is
    /// instantiated by `static/index.html`.
    ///
    /// `static/worker.js` instantiates this same module inside a Web Worker
    /// with `#[wasm_bindgen(start)]` skipped (`init` is passed
    /// `{ skip_start: true }` is not available for start fns, so instead the
    /// worker checks for a missing DOM and bails out here).
    #[wasm_bindgen(start)]
    pub fn start() -> Result<(), JsValue> {
        console_error_panic_hook::set_once();
        // Inside a Web Worker there is no `window`/DOM: this module was
        // loaded as the generation worker, which drives itself through
        // `worker_init`/`worker_generate` instead of `boot`.
        if web_sys::window().is_none() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        // A page that wants to choose its world before one is built sets
        // `__VACKROOMS_DEFER_BOOT__` before importing this module, then calls
        // `boot_world()` once the player has picked a seed. Booting here
        // regardless would generate one world and immediately throw it away —
        // and, worse, would read a `location.search` the setup screen has not
        // written yet, so the main thread and its generation workers could
        // disagree about which world this is.
        //
        // The flag is opt-in so every other entry point (the debug map, a
        // shared link, the capture harness) keeps booting on load exactly as
        // before.
        if boot_deferred() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        spawn_boot();
        Ok(())
    }

    fn boot_deferred() -> bool {
        js_sys::Reflect::get(&js_sys::global(), &"__VACKROOMS_DEFER_BOOT__".into())
            .ok()
            .and_then(|value| value.as_bool())
            .unwrap_or(false)
    }

    /// Starts the engine against whatever world the URL now describes.
    ///
    /// The setup screen writes its seed and sliders into `location.search`
    /// and then calls this. Everything downstream — the composition root and
    /// every generation worker — reads that same query string, so choosing a
    /// world costs no new configuration plumbing and the resulting URL is a
    /// shareable reproduction for free.
    ///
    /// Safe to call more than once only in the sense that it will not panic;
    /// the caller is expected to invoke it once, when the player commits.
    #[wasm_bindgen]
    pub fn boot_world() {
        spawn_boot();
    }

    /// Adapter/device acquisition is asynchronous in WebGPU. Keep the callers
    /// synchronous and let the composition root own the future; failures are
    /// surfaced both in the console and the loading HUD.
    fn spawn_boot() {
        wasm_bindgen_futures::spawn_local(async {
            if let Err(error) = crate::drivers::browser::boot().await {
                web_sys::console::error_2(&"Failed to start WebGPU engine:".into(), &error);
                if let Some(document) = web_sys::window().and_then(|window| window.document()) {
                    if let Some(status) = document.get_element_by_id("status-msg") {
                        let detail = error.as_string().unwrap_or_else(|| format!("{error:?}"));
                        status.set_text_content(Some(&format!(
                            "Failed to start WebGPU engine: {detail}"
                        )));
                    }
                }
            }
        });
    }
}

/// Generation-worker entry points. A worker is a second instance of this
/// same wasm module: `worker_init` builds a chunk source from the *same*
/// URL query the main thread used (identical world by construction), and
/// `worker_generate` runs architectural generation, lighting, the
/// collision-authority SVO, and only the renderer artifacts named by the
/// request bitfield. It returns one transferable byte buffer (see
/// `adapters::chunk_codec`).
#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
mod worker_entry {
    use std::cell::RefCell;

    use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;

    use crate::adapters::archived_chunk_source::ArchivedChunkSource;
    use crate::adapters::chunk_codec::encode_chunk_payload;
    use crate::adapters::query_config::{generator_setup_from_query, surfel_density_from_query};
    use crate::application::chunk_archive::MemoryStorage;
    use crate::application::ports::{ChunkSourcePort, RenderArtifactNeeds};
    use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
    use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;

    thread_local! {
        static SOURCE: RefCell<Option<ArchivedChunkSource<SimpleNoiseProvider>>> =
            const { RefCell::new(None) };
    }

    /// Per-worker archive ceiling, bytes.
    ///
    /// The pool shards the world by chunk affinity, so each worker archives
    /// roughly `1/n` of what the player visits and the pool's total stays near
    /// this figure however many workers there are. 32 MB is a few thousand
    /// coarse chunks — comfortably more than a rolling window holds, so
    /// pacing an area never empties it.
    const WORKER_ARCHIVE_BYTES: u64 = 32 * 1024 * 1024;

    /// `default_seed` must match the main thread's `WORLD_SEED`.
    #[wasm_bindgen]
    pub fn worker_init(query: &str, default_seed: u32) {
        let (seed, config) = generator_setup_from_query(query, default_seed);
        // In-memory for now: OPFS would make this outlive the tab, but even
        // held in the worker's own heap the archive is what makes the rolling
        // window cheap. A chunk evicted when the player turned away and
        // wanted again a moment later is a 0.46 ms decode instead of a 42 ms
        // regeneration, and the worker it comes back to is the one holding it

Confirmed: WebGPU raymarch low: 768 trace steps, 9 chunks; high: 1536 steps, 25 chunks, direct_light_visibility: true for both low and high (lines 377, 386 — default true!). And area_light_visibility_samples 4 for high. So with default toggles (shadow_pass: true), the WebGPU raymarch path runs DIRECT light visibility: per-hit-pixel, per contributing light, up to 4096-step secondary traces. High profile: 25 chunks × 1536 primary steps. This is the biggest per-pixel cost.

Now I have enough. Let me check a few remaining details:

1. The GLSL raymarcher `uDirectVisibilityEnabled` bound to `toggles.shadow_pass` — confirmed at webgl/draw.rs:243-246.
2. GLSL raymarch shader — `directSampleIsVisible` loops `uNumChunks` chunks × traceChunk (768 steps each) per Gauss sample per light. Note: unlike WGSL, GLSL has NO global budget across lights, and the per-chunk light count (uChunkLightCounts) can be up to ~48. So worst case per hit pixel: L_c × 4 × C × 768. With L_c = 48, C = 25, 768: 3.7M steps. In practice the visibility trace stops early when a blocker is found, but for open rooms rays go far. It's the biggest algorithmic hazard in the GLSL path.

3. Also `evaluateVisibleSceneLight` is called for EVERY light in the chunk's range even when the light is far (finiteRangeInverseSquare computes weight; weight > 0.0 check gates visibility trace). Only lights with weight>0 get traced. OK — same as WGSL.

4. `worker_source.rs` — one more check: `GenerationWorkerRequests::take_exact` — VecDeque::remove(position) is O(n) with n = in-flight queue length (typically ≤ 1-2) — fine.

5. In `worker_source.rs` line 231-234 — emergency fallback pushes CompletedChunk synchronously — fine.

6. `browser.rs` — `effective_resolution_scale` reads RENDER_SCALE_BITS every frame; the rAF closure borrows renderer.borrow() and engine.borrow() — potential RefCell borrow panic if re-entrant? No.

7. `browser.rs` run_frame_loop — `std::mem::forget(raf_handle)` — leaks the Rc intentionally. Fine.

8. HUD interval — DOM writes every 30 frames — good.

9. In browser.rs: `engine.borrow_mut().tick(dt, &frame_input)` — tick includes renderer draw; the renderer (SharedRenderer → Rc<RefCell<DriverRenderer>>) is borrowed inside tick via `self.0.borrow_mut()`. But `run_frame_loop` also holds `renderer: Rc<RefCell<DriverRenderer>>` and borrows it at line 753-755 (`renderer.borrow()`) BEFORE `engine.borrow_mut().tick`. Sequential — no overlap. But wait — inside the same closure, at line 807 `renderer.borrow()` is called AFTER tick (line 780). No nested borrows. OK.

10. `play/app.rs` — `SharedNativeRenderer` is Rc<RefCell<NativeRenderer>> — engine holds Box<dyn RendererPort> = SharedNativeRenderer clone; event loop holds another clone. All calls happen on the main thread sequentially (resumed/window_event/RedrawRequested). `engine.tick` → `renderer.draw` → `borrow_mut` — and no other borrow active. The Arc<Window> is only passed to wgpu Instance (display handle) and create_surface. wgpu may call window methods from its own threads? The `InstanceDescriptor::new_with_display_handle(Box::new(window.clone()))` — wgpu holds an Arc<Window> and may access it on other threads; winit Window is Send+Sync? On some platforms Window is !Send? wgpu requires the display handle to be Send. This compiles, so fine.

One concurrency observation for app.rs: `state.engine.tick()` runs synchronously with generation on the main thread (LocalChunkSource — the native build has NO worker pool; chunks generate synchronously inside tick → frame hitches of ~42ms+ during world streaming). That's by design (documented: "native twin... generation stays shared"). But it's a real frame-pacing issue: chunk generation happens inside tick on the main thread; no workers in the native build. Medium perf note.

Also `random_seed()` uses RandomState — fine.

  273|             &wgpu::vertex_attr_array![0 => Float32x2, 1 => Float32x2, 2 => Float32x4],
  274|         );

  276|         let rect_buffer = device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
  277|             label: Some("native.terminal.rects"),
  278|             size: (RECT_CAPACITY * size_of::<RectVertex>()) as u64,
  279|             usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::VERTEX | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
  280|             mapped_at_creation: false,
  281|         });
  282|         let text_buffer = device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
  283|             label: Some("native.terminal.text"),
  284|             size: (TEXT_CAPACITY * size_of::<TextVertex>()) as u64,
  285|             usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::VERTEX | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
  286|             mapped_at_creation: false,
  287|         });

  306|     /// Starts a frame's overlay; all push coordinates are window pixels.
  307|     pub fn begin(&mut self, width: u32, height: u32) {
  308|         self.width = width.max(1) as f32;
  309|         self.height = height.max(1) as f32;
  310|         self.rects.clear();
  311|         self.texts.clear();
  312|     }
  313| 
  314|     pub fn rect(&mut self, x: f32, y: f32, w: f32, h: f32, color: [f32; 4]) {
  315|         let x0 = x / self.width * 2.0 - 1.0;
  316|         let x1 = (x + w) / self.width * 2.0 - 1.0;
  317|         let y0 = 1.0 - y / self.height * 2.0;
  318|         let y1 = 1.0 - (y + h) / self.height * 2.0;
  319|         for pos in [[x0, y0], [x0, y1], [x1, y1], [x0, y0], [x1, y1], [x1, y0]] {
  320|             self.rects.push(RectVertex { pos, color });
  321|         }
  322|     }
  323| 
  324|     /// Draws one line; `px` is the on-screen glyph size (16/24/32 keep the
  325|     /// pixel grid exact). Returns the pen x after the last glyph.
  326|     pub fn text(&mut self, text: &str, x: f32, y_baseline: f32, px: f32, color: [f32; 4]) -> f32 {
  327|         let scale = px / RASTER_PX;
  328|         let mut pen = x;
  329|         for ch in text.chars() {
  330|             if ch == ' ' {
  331|                 pen += self.space_advance * scale;
  332|                 continue;
  333|             }
  334|             let Some(glyph) = self.glyphs.get(&ch) else {
  335|                 pen += self.space_advance * scale;
  336|                 continue;
  337|             };
  338|             let gx = pen + glyph.bearing[0] * scale;
  339|             let gy = y_baseline + glyph.bearing[1] * scale;
  340|             let gw = glyph.size[0] * scale;
  341|             let gh = glyph.size[1] * scale;
  342|             let x0 = gx / self.width * 2.0 - 1.0;
  343|             let x1 = (gx + gw) / self.width * 2.0 - 1.0;
  344|             let y0 = 1.0 - gy / self.height * 2.0;
  345|             let y1 = 1.0 - (gy + gh) / self.height * 2.0;
  346|             let (u0, v0) = (glyph.uv_min[0], glyph.uv_min[1]);
  347|             let (u1, v1) = (glyph.uv_max[0], glyph.uv_max[1]);
  348|             let quad = [
  349|                 ([x0, y0], [u0, v0]),
  350|                 ([x0, y1], [u0, v1]),
  351|                 ([x1, y1], [u1, v1]),
  352|                 ([x0, y0], [u0, v0]),
  353|                 ([x1, y1], [u1, v1]),
  354|                 ([x1, y0], [u1, v0]),
  355|             ];
  356|             for (pos, uv) in quad {
  357|                 self.texts.push(TextVertex { pos, uv, color });
  358|             }
  359|             pen += glyph.advance * scale;
  360|         }
  361|         pen
  362|     }
  363| 
  364|     /// Measures a line's advance width at `px` without emitting quads.
  365|     pub fn measure(&self, text: &str, px: f32) -> f32 {
  366|         let scale = px / RASTER_PX;
  367|         text.chars()
  368|             .map(|ch| match self.glyphs.get(&ch) {
  369|                 Some(glyph) => glyph.advance * scale,
  370|                 None => self.space_advance * scale,
  371|             })
  372|             .sum()
  373|     }
  374| 
  375|     pub fn line_height(&self, px: f32) -> f32 {
  376|         self.line_height * (px / RASTER_PX)
  377|     }
  378| 
  379|     pub fn draw(
  380|         &mut self,
  381|         queue: &wgpu::Queue,
  382|         encoder: &mut wgpu::CommandEncoder,
  383|         target: &wgpu::TextureView,
  384|     ) {
  385|         self.rects.truncate(RECT_CAPACITY);
  386|         self.texts.truncate(TEXT_CAPACITY);
  387|         if self.rects.is_empty() && self.texts.is_empty() {
  388|             return;
  389|         }
  390|         if !self.rects.is_empty() {
  391|             queue.write_buffer(&self.rect_buffer, 0, bytemuck::cast_slice(&self.rects));
  392|         }
  393|         if !self.texts.is_empty() {
  394|             queue.write_buffer(&self.text_buffer, 0, bytemuck::cast_slice(&self.texts));
  395|         }
  396|         let mut pass = encoder.begin_render_pass(&wgpu::RenderPassDescriptor {
  397|             label: Some("native.terminal.pass"),
  398|             color_attachments: &[Some(wgpu::RenderPassColorAttachment {
  399|                 view: target,
  400|                 depth_slice: None,
  401|                 resolve_target: None,
  402|                 ops: wgpu::Operations {
  403|                     load: wgpu::LoadOp::Load,
  404|                     store: wgpu::StoreOp::Store,
  405|                 },
  406|             })],
  407|             depth_stencil_attachment: None,
  408|             ..Default::default()
  409|         });
  410|         if !self.rects.is_empty() {
  411|             pass.set_pipeline(&self.rect_pipeline);
  412|             pass.set_vertex_buffer(0, self.rect_buffer.slice(..));
  413|             pass.draw(0..self.rects.len() as u32, 0..1);
  414|         }
  415|         if !self.texts.is_empty() {
  416|             pass.set_pipeline(&self.text_pipeline);
  417|             pass.set_bind_group(0, &self.text_bind_group, &[]);
  418|             pass.set_vertex_buffer(0, self.text_buffer.slice(..));
  419|             pass.draw(0..self.texts.len() as u32, 0..1);
  420|         }
  421|     }
  422| }

        // regeneration, and the worker it comes back to is the one holding it
        // because the pool routes by chunk affinity.
        //
        // `generator_id` is the query string's own hash: it changes whenever
        // any world parameter does, which is exactly when archived geometry
        // stops being valid. It does *not* change when the generator's code
        // changes — a worker is rebuilt with the wasm module, so a code change
        // replaces the archive along with everything else. A persistent
        // archive would have to fold in a build hash.
        let generator_id = fnv64(query.as_bytes());
        SOURCE.with(|s| {
            *s.borrow_mut() = Some(ArchivedChunkSource::with_budget(
                SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
                seed,
                config,
                Box::new(MemoryStorage::new()),
                generator_id,
                WORKER_ARCHIVE_BYTES,
            )
            // Extraction happens here, not on the main thread, so the surfel
            // density has to be read from the query on this side of the
            // worker boundary too.
            .with_surfel_density(surfel_density_from_query(query)));
        });
    }

    fn fnv64(bytes: &[u8]) -> u64 {
        let mut h: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
        for &byte in bytes {
            h ^= byte as u64;
            h = h.wrapping_mul(0x1000_0000_01b3);
        }
        h
    }

    #[wasm_bindgen]
    pub fn worker_generate(
        _request_id: u32,
        origin_x: f32,
        origin_z: f32,
        level: u32,
        lod: u8,
        artifact_bits: u8,
        reality_words: Vec<u32>,
    ) -> Vec<u8> {
        let artifacts = RenderArtifactNeeds::from_bits(artifact_bits)
            .expect("worker_generate received invalid artifact bits");
        let reality = RealitySnapshot::from_words(&reality_words)
            .expect("worker_generate received an invalid reality snapshot");
        SOURCE.with(|s| {
            let source = s.borrow();
            let source = source
                .as_ref()
                .expect("worker_generate called before worker_init");
            encode_chunk_payload(
                &source.load_with_artifacts(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, &reality, artifacts),
            )
        })
    }

Confirmed: `scene_lights.truncate(MAX_ANALYTIC_SCENE_LIGHTS_PER_FRAME)` at engine.rs:517 — so per-frame scene light list ≤ 48. So:
- WebGPU raster paths: every vertex evaluates up to 48 lights (each rectangle light = 4 Gauss samples = 192 evaluations per vertex), no clustering, no range early-out. Splat budget high = 150k faces → 150k × 4 corners × 48 lights = 28.8M light evaluations/frame on the GPU vertex stage (with SIMD-ish GPU parallelism, still the dominant vertex cost).
- WebGPU raymarch: per hit-pixel, up to 52 lights (48 + 4 dynamic); each light within range spawns a visibility trace of up to 4096 steps × 25 chunks when direct_light_visibility is on (default).

  509|         self.survival.advance_vitals(dt, instantaneous_c);
  510| 
  511|         // OPTIMIZATION: bound the fixtures a production renderer evaluates
  512|         // per fragment. Thermal already consumed the full ranked list above;
  513|         // `select_scene_lights` sorts nearest/most-important first, so this
  514|         // keeps ordinary rooms visually identical while capping the
  515|         // pathological case of a fixture-dense layout across the whole
  516|         // streaming neighborhood. See `MAX_ANALYTIC_SCENE_LIGHTS_PER_FRAME`.
  517|         scene_lights.truncate(MAX_ANALYTIC_SCENE_LIGHTS_PER_FRAME);
  518| 
  519|         // Consumption is deliberate; the survival aggregate also owns the
  520|         // optional accessibility policy that acts after explicit choices.
  521|         self.survival.consume(ConsumptionIntent {
  522|             drink: input.drink,
  523|             eat: input.eat,
  524|         });
  525|         // The body listens to the same survival state the vitals own; the
  526|         // resolved walking distance is the only movement it ever sees.
  527|         let survival = self.survival.readout();

  529|             dt,
  530|             walked_m,
  531|             BodyContext {
  532|                 hydration: survival.vitals.hydration,
  533|                 satiety: survival.vitals.satiety,
  534|                 condition: survival.vitals.condition,
  535|                 ambient_c: survival.ambient_c,
  536|             },
  537|         );
  538|         self.update_route(dt);
  539|         if self.survival.succumb_if_dead() {
  540|             self.respawn_after_attrition();
  541|         }
  542|         // Strain: mismanagement in either direction raises the reality's
  543|         // delirium tier, and chunks generated from here on carry more
  544|         // anomalous infill, sealed doorways, shut corridor mouths, and
  545|         // thinner provisions. Resident chunks are untouched — the world
  546|         // worsens as it streams, never as a visible pop. Dehydration bands
  547|         // punish the underconsumer; the excess meter (wasted supplies)
  548|         // punishes the overconsumer with the very same tiers.
  549|         let tier = self.survival.advance_strain(dt);
  550|         if tier != self.reality.delirium() {
  551|             self.reality = self.reality.with_delirium(tier);
  552|         }
  553| 
  554|         let flare_lights = self
  555|             .flares
  556|             .lights(self.player.position, self.time_seconds as f32);
  557|         let frame = FrameParams {
  558|             camera_pos: self.player.position,
  559|             yaw: self.player.yaw,
  560|             pitch: self.player.pitch,
  561|             flashlight: input.flashlight,
  562|             dynamic_lights: flare_lights.lights,
  563|             dynamic_light_count: flare_lights.count,
  564|             scene_lights,
  565|             environment: self.environment(),
  566|             supply_sprites: self.collect_supply_sprites(),
  567|         };
  568|         self.renderer.draw(&frame, &self.draws);
  569|     }

    1| //! Prepare the immutable fixture list consumed by a render frame.
    2| //!
    3| //! Chunk payloads overlap on purpose, so the same ceiling panel can arrive
    4| //! from several neighboring halos. Selection belongs here, before any GPU
    5| //! driver: all renderers must see the same deduplicated physical scene.
    6| 
    7| use std::collections::HashMap;
    8| 
    9| use crate::application::ports::LightSource;
   10| 
   11| /// Collects every finite, enabled fixture and orders it by conservative
   12| /// contribution at `camera_position`.
   13| ///
   14| /// The ordering is not a budget: no fixture is discarded. It keeps the hero
   15| /// shadow choice stable and makes output independent of hash-map/chunk arrival
   16| /// order. Projected emitter area and authored intensity raise importance while
   17| /// squared distance lowers it.
   18| pub fn select_scene_lights<'a>(
   19|     lights: impl Iterator<Item = &'a LightSource>,
   20|     camera_position: [f32; 3],
   21| ) -> Vec<LightSource> {
   22|     let mut unique = HashMap::<u64, LightSource>::new();
   23|     for light in lights.copied() {
   24|         if light.enabled && valid(&light) {
   25|             unique.entry(light.id).or_insert(light);
   26|         }
   27|     }
   28| 
   29|     let mut ranked: Vec<(LightSource, f32)> = unique
   30|         .into_values()
   31|         .map(|light| {
   32|             let delta = [
   33|                 light.position[0] - camera_position[0],
   34|                 light.position[1] - camera_position[1],
   35|                 light.position[2] - camera_position[2],
   36|             ];
   37|             let distance_squared = delta.into_iter().map(|v| v * v).sum::<f32>();
   38|             let area = (4.0 * light.half_size[0] * light.half_size[1]).max(0.01);
   39|             let importance = light.intensity * area / (distance_squared + area);
   40|             (light, importance)
   41|         })
   42|         .collect();
   43|     ranked.sort_by(|(a, a_score), (b, b_score)| {
   44|         b_score.total_cmp(a_score).then_with(|| a.id.cmp(&b.id))
   45|     });
   46| 
   47|     ranked.into_iter().map(|(light, _)| light).collect()
   48| }
   49| 
   50| fn valid(light: &LightSource) -> bool {
   51|     light.position.into_iter().all(f32::is_finite)
   52|         && light.color.into_iter().all(f32::is_finite)
   53|         && light
   54|             .half_size
   55|             .into_iter()
   56|             .all(|v| v.is_finite() && v >= 0.0)
   57|         && light.radius.is_finite()
   58|         && light.radius > 0.0
   59|         && light.intensity.is_finite()
   60|         && light.intensity > 0.0
   61| }

===== wasm_frontend/src/drivers/worker_source.rs (343 lines) =====
    1| //! Web Worker chunk source — the multithreaded [`ChunkSourcePort`].
    2| //!
    3| //! Each worker (`static/worker.js`) is a second instance of this same wasm
    4| //! module running on its own OS thread. The main thread posts small
    5| //! `{gen, requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality}` messages
    6| //! round-robin. Workers always generate, bake, build the collision SVO, and
    7| //! extract collision; the artifact bitfield requests only the active
    8| //! renderer's mesh, face, or serialized-node products. One encoded byte
    9| //! buffer returns through `adapters::chunk_codec`; GPU resources remain owned
   10| //! by the main-thread render driver. Healthy pools keep generation off the
   11| //! frame loop. If every worker fatally fails, the driver uses its same-thread
   12| //! source as a correctness fallback instead of leaving the world pending.
   13| //!
   14| //! Stale-result rejection lives in the engine (`install_completed`), keyed
   15| //! by the echoed request. This driver owns transport failure detection and
   16| //! reports exact failed requests through the same application port.
   17| 
   18| use std::cell::RefCell;
   19| use std::rc::Rc;
   20| 
   21| use js_sys::{ArrayBuffer, Reflect, Uint8Array};
   22| use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
   23| use web_sys::{MessageEvent, Worker, WorkerOptions, WorkerType};
   24| 
   25| use crate::adapters::chunk_codec::decode_chunk_payload;
   26| use crate::adapters::local_chunk_source::LocalChunkSource;
   27| use crate::application::generation_worker_policy::MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS;
   28| use crate::application::ports::{
   29|     ChunkPayload, ChunkRequest, ChunkSourcePort, CompletedChunk, RenderArtifactNeeds,
   30| };
   31| use crate::application::streaming::chunk_key;
   32| use crate::drivers::generation_worker_requests::GenerationWorkerRequests;
   33| use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
   34| use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
   35| 
   36| pub struct WorkerChunkSource {
   37|     workers: Vec<Worker>,
   38|     completed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<CompletedChunk>>>,
   39|     failed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<ChunkRequest>>>,
   40|     requests: Rc<RefCell<GenerationWorkerRequests>>,
   41|     /// Keeps browser callbacks alive for the workers' lifetime.
   42|     _message_handlers: Vec<Closure<dyn FnMut(MessageEvent)>>,
   43|     _error_handlers: Vec<Closure<dyn FnMut(web_sys::Event)>>,
   44|     /// Same-thread source for the synchronous [`ChunkSourcePort::load`]
   45|     /// contract and as a last-resort recovery if every worker has failed.
   46|     fallback: LocalChunkSource<SimpleNoiseProvider>,
   47|     reported_emergency_fallback: bool,
   48| }
   49| 
   50| impl WorkerChunkSource {
   51|     /// Spawns the pool and hands every worker the URL query, so main thread
   52|     /// and workers derive the identical generator configuration.
   53|     pub fn new(query: &str, default_seed: u32, pool_size: usize) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
   54|         if !(1..=usize::from(MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS)).contains(&pool_size) {
   55|             return Err(JsValue::from_str(
   56|                 "generation worker pool size must be 1..=32",
   57|             ));
   58|         }
   59| 
   60|         let completed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<CompletedChunk>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
   61|         let failed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<ChunkRequest>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
   62|         let requests = Rc::new(RefCell::new(GenerationWorkerRequests::new(pool_size)));
   63|         // The single-file bundle (scripts/build-single-file.mjs) has no
   64|         // sibling worker.js on disk; it publishes a blob: URL for the inlined
   65|         // worker script on the global scope instead.
   66|         let script_url = Reflect::get(&js_sys::global(), &"__VACKROOMS_WORKER_URL__".into())
   67|             .ok()
   68|             .and_then(|value| value.as_string())
   69|             .unwrap_or_else(|| "worker.js".to_string());
   70|         let mut workers = Vec::with_capacity(pool_size);
   71|         let mut message_handlers = Vec::with_capacity(pool_size);
   72|         let mut error_handlers = Vec::with_capacity(pool_size);
   73|         for worker_index in 0..pool_size {
   74|             let options = WorkerOptions::new();
   75|             options.set_type(WorkerType::Module);
   76|             // Relative (not `/worker.js`): resolved against the document's
   77|             // URL, so this still finds the sibling file when the site is
   78|             // served from a subpath (e.g. a GitHub Pages project page at
   79|             // `<user>.github.io/<repo>/`) instead of the domain root.
   80|             let worker = Worker::new_with_options(&script_url, &options)?;
   81| 
   82|             let completed_sink = completed.clone();
   83|             let failed_sink = failed.clone();
   84|             let message_requests = requests.clone();
   85|             let worker_for_fatal_reply = worker.clone();
   86|             let handler = Closure::<dyn FnMut(MessageEvent)>::new(move |event: MessageEvent| {
   87|                 match parse_worker_reply(&event) {
   88|                     WorkerReply::Completed(done) => {
   89|                         if message_requests
   90|                             .borrow_mut()
   91|                             .finish_exact(worker_index, &done.request)
   92|                         {
   93|                             completed_sink.borrow_mut().push(done);
   94|                         }
   95|                     }
   96|                     WorkerReply::Failed(echoed) => {
   97|                         if let Some(failed_request) = message_requests
   98|                             .borrow_mut()
   99|                             .fail_exact(worker_index, &echoed)
  100|                         {
  101|                             failed_sink.borrow_mut().push(failed_request);
  102|                         }
  103|                     }
  104|                     WorkerReply::Fatal => {
  105|                         let abandoned = message_requests
  106|                             .borrow_mut()
  107|                             .disable_and_drain(worker_index);
  108|                         failed_sink.borrow_mut().extend(abandoned);
  109|                         worker_for_fatal_reply.terminate();
  110|                     }
  111|                     WorkerReply::Malformed => {
  112|                         if let Some(failed_request) =
  113|                             message_requests.borrow_mut().fail_oldest(worker_index)
  114|                         {
  115|                             failed_sink.borrow_mut().push(failed_request);
  116|                         }
  117|                     }
  118|                 }
  119|             });
  120|             worker.set_onmessage(Some(handler.as_ref().unchecked_ref()));
  121| 
  122|             let failed_sink = failed.clone();
  123|             let error_requests = requests.clone();
  124|             let worker_for_error = worker.clone();
  125|             let error_handler = Closure::<dyn FnMut(web_sys::Event)>::new(move |_event| {
  126|                 let abandoned = error_requests.borrow_mut().disable_and_drain(worker_index);
  127|                 failed_sink.borrow_mut().extend(abandoned);
  128|                 worker_for_error.terminate();
  129|             });
  130|             worker.set_onerror(Some(error_handler.as_ref().unchecked_ref()));
  131| 
  132|             let init = js_sys::Object::new();
  133|             Reflect::set(&init, &"type".into(), &"init".into())?;
  134|             Reflect::set(&init, &"query".into(), &query.into())?;
  135|             Reflect::set(&init, &"seed".into(), &(default_seed as f64).into())?;
  136|             worker.post_message(&init)?;
  137| 
  138|             workers.push(worker);
  139|             message_handlers.push(handler);
  140|             error_handlers.push(error_handler);
  141|         }
  142| 
  143|         let (seed, config) =
  144|             crate::adapters::query_config::generator_setup_from_query(query, default_seed);
  145|         Ok(Self {
  146|             workers,
  147|             completed,
  148|             failed,
  149|             requests,
  150|             _message_handlers: message_handlers,
  151|             _error_handlers: error_handlers,
  152|             fallback: LocalChunkSource::new(SimpleNoiseProvider::new(), seed, config),
  153|             reported_emergency_fallback: false,
  154|         })
  155|     }
  156| 
  157|     pub fn pool_size(&self) -> usize {
  158|         self.workers.len()
  159|     }
  160| }
  161| 
  162| impl ChunkSourcePort for WorkerChunkSource {
  163|     fn load(&self, origin_x: f32, origin_z: f32, level: u32, lod: u8) -> ChunkPayload {
  164|         self.fallback.load(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod)
  165|     }
  166| 
  167|     fn load_with_reality(
  168|         &self,
  169|         origin_x: f32,
  170|         origin_z: f32,
  171|         level: u32,
  172|         lod: u8,
  173|         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
  174|     ) -> ChunkPayload {
  175|         self.fallback
  176|             .load_with_reality(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, reality)
  177|     }
  178| 
  179|     fn load_with_artifacts(
  180|         &self,
  181|         origin_x: f32,
  182|         origin_z: f32,
  183|         level: u32,
  184|         lod: u8,
  185|         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
  186|         artifacts: RenderArtifactNeeds,
  187|     ) -> ChunkPayload {
  188|         self.fallback
  189|             .load_with_artifacts(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, reality, artifacts)
  190|     }
  191| 
  192|     fn is_async(&self) -> bool {
  193|         true
  194|     }
  195| 
  196|     fn max_concurrent_requests(&self) -> usize {
  197|         self.pool_size()
  198|     }
  199| 
  200|     fn request(&mut self, request: ChunkRequest) {
  201|         // Route by chunk, not round-robin: each worker archives what it
  202|         // generates, so a chunk evicted from the rolling window and later
  203|         // wanted again must come back to the worker already holding it.
  204|         // `next_accepting` still falls through to any healthy worker, so
  205|         // affinity is a preference and never a way to strand a request on a
  206|         // dead worker.
  207|         let preferred = GenerationWorkerRequests::preferred_worker(
  208|             chunk_key(request.origin_x, request.origin_z),
  209|             self.workers.len(),
  210|         );
  211|         let worker_index = self.requests.borrow().next_accepting(preferred);
  212|         let Some(worker_index) = worker_index else {
  213|             // Fatal worker startup/runtime failures must not strand streaming.
  214|             // This path is deliberately exceptional: the healthy path always
  215|             // generates off-thread, while an exhausted pool favors a complete
  216|             // world over a permanently pending chunk.
  217|             if !self.reported_emergency_fallback {
  218|                 web_sys::console::warn_1(
  219|                     &"generation worker pool failed; using same-thread recovery".into(),
  220|                 );
  221|                 self.reported_emergency_fallback = true;
  222|             }
  223|             let payload = self.fallback.load_with_artifacts(
  224|                 request.origin_x,
  225|                 request.origin_z,
  226|                 request.level,
  227|                 request.lod,
  228|                 &request.reality,
  229|                 request.artifacts,
  230|             );
  231|             self.completed
  232|                 .borrow_mut()
  233|                 .push(CompletedChunk { request, payload });
  234|             return;
  235|         };
  236| 
  237|         let message = js_sys::Object::new();
  238|         let set = |k: &str, v: JsValue| {
  239|             let _ = Reflect::set(&message, &k.into(), &v);
  240|         };
  241|         set("type", "gen".into());
  242|         set("requestId", (request.request_id as f64).into());
  243|         set("ox", (request.origin_x as f64).into());
  244|         set("oz", (request.origin_z as f64).into());
  245|         set("level", (request.level as f64).into());
  246|         set("lod", (request.lod as f64).into());
  247|         set("artifacts", (request.artifacts.bits() as f64).into());
  248|         let reality_words = request.reality.to_words();
  249|         let reality = js_sys::Uint32Array::from(reality_words.as_slice());
  250|         set("reality", reality.into());
  251|         let worker = &self.workers[worker_index];
  252|         self.requests
  253|             .borrow_mut()
  254|             .assign(worker_index, request.clone());
  255|         if let Err(error) = worker.post_message(&message) {
  256|             // A synchronous send failure means this worker can no longer be
  257|             // trusted with its already queued requests. Retire all of them;
  258|             // the engine will validate their ids and retry on healthy slots.
  259|             let abandoned = self.requests.borrow_mut().disable_and_drain(worker_index);
  260|             self.failed.borrow_mut().extend(abandoned);
  261|             worker.terminate();
  262|             web_sys::console::warn_2(
  263|                 &"generation worker postMessage failed; disabling worker:".into(),
  264|                 &error,
  265|             );
  266|         }
  267|     }
  268| 
  269|     fn poll_completed(&mut self) -> Vec<CompletedChunk> {
  270|         std::mem::take(&mut *self.completed.borrow_mut())
  271|     }
  272| 
  273|     fn poll_failed_requests(&mut self) -> Vec<ChunkRequest> {
  274|         std::mem::take(&mut *self.failed.borrow_mut())
  275|     }
  276| }
  277| 
  278| enum WorkerReply {
  279|     Completed(CompletedChunk),
  280|     Failed(ChunkRequest),
  281|     Fatal,
  282|     Malformed,
  283| }
  284| 
  285| /// Decodes the deliberately small worker protocol. Malformed replies are a
  286| /// first-class outcome: the worker queue is serial, so the caller can fail its
  287| /// oldest assigned request instead of leaving that chunk pending forever.
  288| fn parse_worker_reply(event: &MessageEvent) -> WorkerReply {
  289|     let data = event.data();
  290|     let message_type = Reflect::get(&data, &"type".into())
  291|         .ok()
  292|         .and_then(|value| value.as_string());
  293|     match message_type.as_deref() {
  294|         Some("done") => parse_request(&data)
  295|             .and_then(|request| {
  296|                 parse_payload(&data).map(|payload| CompletedChunk { request, payload })
  297|             })
  298|             .map(WorkerReply::Completed)
  299|             .unwrap_or(WorkerReply::Malformed),
  300|         Some("failed") => parse_request(&data)
  301|             .map(WorkerReply::Failed)
  302|             .unwrap_or(WorkerReply::Malformed),
  303|         Some("fatal") => WorkerReply::Fatal,
  304|         _ => WorkerReply::Malformed,
  305|     }
  306| }
  307| 
  308| fn parse_request(data: &JsValue) -> Option<ChunkRequest> {
  309|     let field = |name: &str| Reflect::get(data, &name.into()).ok();
  310|     Some(ChunkRequest {
  311|         request_id: exact_u32(field("requestId")?)?,
  312|         origin_x: finite_f32(field("ox")?)?,
  313|         origin_z: finite_f32(field("oz")?)?,
  314|         level: exact_u32(field("level")?)?,
  315|         lod: u8::try_from(exact_u32(field("lod")?)?).ok()?,
  316|         artifacts: RenderArtifactNeeds::from_bits(
  317|             u8::try_from(exact_u32(field("artifacts")?)?).ok()?,
  318|         )?,
  319|         reality: {
  320|             let encoded = field("reality")?;
  321|             let words = encoded.dyn_into::<js_sys::Uint32Array>().ok()?.to_vec();
  322|             RealitySnapshot::from_words(&words).ok()?
  323|         },
  324|     })
  325| }
  326| 
  327| fn parse_payload(data: &JsValue) -> Option<ChunkPayload> {
  328|     let buffer: ArrayBuffer = Reflect::get(data, &"buf".into()).ok()?.dyn_into().ok()?;
  329|     let bytes = Uint8Array::new(&buffer).to_vec();
  330|     decode_chunk_payload(&bytes)
  331| }
  332| 
  333| fn exact_u32(value: JsValue) -> Option<u32> {
  334|     let number = value.as_f64()?;
  335|     (number.is_finite() && number.fract() == 0.0 && (0.0..=f64::from(u32::MAX)).contains(&number))
  336|         .then_some(number as u32)
  337| }
  338| 
  339| fn finite_f32(value: JsValue) -> Option<f32> {
  340|     let number = value.as_f64()?;
  341|     let narrowed = number as f32;
  342|     (number.is_finite() && narrowed.is_finite()).then_some(narrowed)
  343| }

===== wasm_frontend/src/drivers/generation_worker_requests.rs (254 lines) =====
    1| //! Exact in-flight request bookkeeping for the generation-worker pool.
    2| //!
    3| //! Browser callbacks can arrive after a worker has failed or after the engine
    4| //! has already retried a chunk. This small ledger gives every callback one
    5| //! deterministic operation: finish the exact request it echoes, fail the
    6| //! oldest request after a malformed reply, or drain a failed worker.
    7| 
    8| use std::collections::VecDeque;
    9| 
   10| use crate::application::ports::ChunkRequest;
   11| use crate::application::streaming::ChunkKey;
   12| 
   13| #[derive(Debug)]
   14| struct WorkerRequests {
   15|     accepting_work: bool,
   16|     in_flight: VecDeque<ChunkRequest>,
   17| }
   18| 
   19| /// Per-worker request ownership. Request identity is always checked through
   20| /// [`ChunkRequest::is_same_request`], never by chunk coordinates alone.
   21| #[derive(Debug)]
   22| pub(crate) struct GenerationWorkerRequests {
   23|     workers: Vec<WorkerRequests>,
   24| }
   25| 
   26| impl GenerationWorkerRequests {
   27|     pub(crate) fn new(worker_count: usize) -> Self {
   28|         assert!(
   29|             worker_count > 0,
   30|             "a worker ledger needs at least one worker"
   31|         );
   32|         Self {
   33|             workers: (0..worker_count)
   34|                 .map(|_| WorkerRequests {
   35|                     accepting_work: true,
   36|                     in_flight: VecDeque::new(),
   37|                 })
   38|                 .collect(),
   39|         }
   40|     }
   41| 
   42|     /// Which worker owns a chunk.
   43|     ///
   44|     /// Deliberately not round-robin. Each worker keeps its own archive of
   45|     /// what it has generated, and an archive only pays off if the chunk comes
   46|     /// back to the worker holding it — round-robin would scatter a chunk
   47|     /// across the pool and turn a 0.46 ms read into a 42 ms regeneration on
   48|     /// (n-1)/n of re-requests.
   49|     ///
   50|     /// Hashing the coordinates rather than slicing the world into contiguous
   51|     /// blocks is what keeps the pool balanced: a player standing anywhere has
   52|     /// their surrounding chunks spread evenly across workers, where a
   53|     /// block-per-worker split would leave one worker generating everything
   54|     /// while the rest idled.
   55|     pub(crate) fn preferred_worker(chunk: ChunkKey, worker_count: usize) -> usize {
   56|         if worker_count <= 1 {
   57|             return 0;
   58|         }
   59|         let mut h: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
   60|         for word in [chunk.0 as u64, chunk.1 as u64] {
   61|             for byte in word.to_le_bytes() {
   62|                 h ^= byte as u64;
   63|                 h = h.wrapping_mul(0x1000_0000_01b3);
   64|             }
   65|         }
   66|         (h % worker_count as u64) as usize
   67|     }
   68| 
   69|     /// Finds the next healthy worker, wrapping once from `start`.
   70|     pub(crate) fn next_accepting(&self, start: usize) -> Option<usize> {
   71|         (0..self.workers.len())
   72|             .map(|offset| (start + offset) % self.workers.len())
   73|             .find(|&index| self.workers[index].accepting_work)
   74|     }
   75| 
   76|     pub(crate) fn assign(&mut self, worker_index: usize, request: ChunkRequest) {
   77|         let worker = &mut self.workers[worker_index];
   78|         debug_assert!(worker.accepting_work);
   79|         worker.in_flight.push_back(request);
   80|     }
   81| 
   82|     /// Retires only the exact request echoed by a well-formed worker reply.
   83|     /// Unknown and stale replies leave all current work untouched.
   84|     pub(crate) fn finish_exact(&mut self, worker_index: usize, echoed: &ChunkRequest) -> bool {
   85|         self.take_exact(worker_index, echoed).is_some()
   86|     }
   87| 
   88|     /// Retires an exact request reported as failed by the worker protocol.
   89|     pub(crate) fn fail_exact(
   90|         &mut self,
   91|         worker_index: usize,
   92|         echoed: &ChunkRequest,
   93|     ) -> Option<ChunkRequest> {
   94|         self.take_exact(worker_index, echoed)
   95|     }
   96| 
   97|     /// A worker processes its queue serially, so a malformed response belongs
   98|     /// to its oldest outstanding request even when its envelope cannot be
   99|     /// decoded far enough to recover an id.
  100|     pub(crate) fn fail_oldest(&mut self, worker_index: usize) -> Option<ChunkRequest> {
  101|         self.workers[worker_index].in_flight.pop_front()
  102|     }
  103| 
  104|     /// Stops scheduling to a broken worker and returns all work the engine
  105|     /// must retry. Calling this more than once is harmless.
  106|     pub(crate) fn disable_and_drain(&mut self, worker_index: usize) -> Vec<ChunkRequest> {
  107|         let worker = &mut self.workers[worker_index];
  108|         worker.accepting_work = false;
  109|         worker.in_flight.drain(..).collect()
  110|     }
  111| 
  112|     fn take_exact(&mut self, worker_index: usize, echoed: &ChunkRequest) -> Option<ChunkRequest> {
  113|         let queue = &mut self.workers[worker_index].in_flight;
  114|         let position = queue
  115|             .iter()
  116|             .position(|request| request.is_same_request(echoed))?;
  117|         queue.remove(position)
  118|     }
  119| }

  130|         // coming back into range must be routed to the worker that already
  131|         // has it, or the archive never hits.
  132|         for count in [1usize, 2, 3, 4, 8, 32] {

  135|                 assert_eq!(
  136|                     first,
  137|                     GenerationWorkerRequests::preferred_worker(chunk, count),

  140|                 assert!(first < count, "worker {first} is outside a pool of {count}");
  141|             }

  149|         // idled, which is worse than round-robin.

    1| //! Native desktop build of Vackrooms: a winit window on wgpu's Vulkan
    2| //! backend, driving the same `Engine`, `LocalChunkSource`, and production
    3| //! pipelines the browser uses. No browser, no WebGPU support required.
    4| //!
    5| //! ```sh
    6| //! cargo run -p wasm_frontend --bin play --release
    7| //! cargo run -p wasm_frontend --bin play --release -- --renderer=raymarch --seed=7
    8| //! ```
    9| //!
   10| //! Flags: `--renderer=surface|splat|raymarch|cpu` (default surface),
   11| //! `--preset=compat|full` (default compat: culling optimizations on, the
   12| //! expensive effect passes — shadows, ambient occlusion, deferred — off,
   13| //! because this build exists to test weak/varied hardware), `--quality=low|high`,
   14| //! `--seed=N`. Controls: WASD + mouse (click to capture, Esc releases),
   15| //! F flashlight, G flare, R drink, T eat.
   16| //!
   17| //! This file is the native twin of `drivers/webgpu/renderer.rs` +
   18| //! `drivers/browser.rs`: those are wasm-only (web-sys types in their
   19| //! signatures), so the window/present plumbing is mirrored here while every
   20| //! pipeline, the engine, and generation stay shared.

   52| /// Every start explores a fresh world; `--seed=N` reproduces one. The
   53| /// std hasher is randomly keyed per process, which is all the entropy a
   54| /// world seed needs without pulling in a rand dependency.
   55| fn random_seed() -> u32 {
   56|     use std::hash::{BuildHasher, Hasher};
   57|     std::collections::hash_map::RandomState::new()
   58|         .build_hasher()
   59|         .finish() as u32

   69| /// The compatibility preset every run starts from: all load-*reducing*
   70| /// switches stay on, all load-*adding* effect passes stay off. `--preset=full`
   71| /// restores the browser's default switchboard for parity testing.
   72| fn compat_toggles() -> RenderToggles {
   73|     RenderToggles {
   74|         shadow_pass: false,
   75|         ambient_occlusion: false,
   76|         deferred_shading: false,
   77|         flashlight_occlusion: false,
   78|         ..RenderToggles::default()
   79|     }

   82| fn parse_options() -> Options {
   83|     let mut options = Options {
   84|         renderer: RendererKind::Surface,
   85|         quality: GpuQualityProfile::default(),
   86|         seed: random_seed(),
   87|         toggles: compat_toggles(),
   88|     };
   89|     for argument in std::env::args().skip(1) {
   90|         if let Some(value) = argument.strip_prefix("--renderer=") {
   91|             options.renderer = value.parse().unwrap_or_else(|_| {
   92|                 panic!("unknown renderer {value:?}; use surface|splat|raymarch|cpu")
   93|             });
   94|         } else if let Some(value) = argument.strip_prefix("--preset=") {
   95|             options.toggles = match value {
   96|                 "compat" => compat_toggles(),
   97|                 "full" => RenderToggles::default(),
   98|                 other => panic!("unknown preset {other:?}; use compat|full"),
   99|             };
  100|         } else if let Some(value) = argument.strip_prefix("--quality=") {
  101|             options.quality = value
  102|                 .parse()
  103|                 .unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!("unknown quality {value:?}; use low|high"));
  104|         } else if let Some(value) = argument.strip_prefix("--seed=") {
  105|             options.seed = value
  106|                 .parse()
  107|                 .unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!("seed must be a number, got {value:?}"));
  108|         } else {
  109|             panic!(
  110|                 "unknown flag {argument:?}; supported: --renderer= --preset= --quality= --seed="
  111|             );
  112|         }
  113|     }
  114|     options
  115| }

  253|     fn window_event(&mut self, event_loop: &ActiveEventLoop, _id: WindowId, event: WindowEvent) {
  254|         let Some(state) = &mut self.state else {
  255|             return;
  256|         };
  257|         match event {
  258|             WindowEvent::CloseRequested => event_loop.exit(),
  259|             WindowEvent::Resized(size) => {
  260|                 state.renderer.resize(size.width, size.height);
  261|             }
  262|             WindowEvent::MouseInput {
  263|                 state: ElementState::Pressed,
  264|                 button: MouseButton::Left,
  265|                 ..
  266|             } => {
  267|                 if !state.input.captured {
  268|                     let grabbed = state
  269|                         .window
