    1| //! Prepare the immutable fixture list consumed by a render frame.
    2| //!
    3| //! Chunk payloads overlap on purpose, so the same ceiling panel can arrive
    4| //! from several neighboring halos. Selection belongs here, before any GPU
    5| //! driver: all renderers must see the same deduplicated physical scene.
    6| 
    7| use std::collections::HashMap;
    8| 
    9| use crate::application::ports::LightSource;
   10| 
   11| /// Collects every finite, enabled fixture and orders it by conservative
   12| /// contribution at `camera_position`.
   13| ///
   14| /// The ordering is not a budget: no fixture is discarded. It keeps the hero
   15| /// shadow choice stable and makes output independent of hash-map/chunk arrival
   16| /// order. Projected emitter area and authored intensity raise importance while
   17| /// squared distance lowers it.
   18| pub fn select_scene_lights<'a>(
   19|     lights: impl Iterator<Item = &'a LightSource>,
   20|     camera_position: [f32; 3],
   21| ) -> Vec<LightSource> {
   22|     let mut unique = HashMap::<u64, LightSource>::new();
   23|     for light in lights.copied() {
   24|         if light.enabled && valid(&light) {
   25|             unique.entry(light.id).or_insert(light);
   26|         }
   27|     }
   28| 
   29|     let mut ranked: Vec<(LightSource, f32)> = unique
   30|         .into_values()
   31|         .map(|light| {
   32|             let delta = [
   33|                 light.position[0] - camera_position[0],
   34|                 light.position[1] - camera_position[1],
   35|                 light.position[2] - camera_position[2],
   36|             ];
   37|             let distance_squared = delta.into_iter().map(|v| v * v).sum::<f32>();
   38|             let area = (4.0 * light.half_size[0] * light.half_size[1]).max(0.01);
   39|             let importance = light.intensity * area / (distance_squared + area);
   40|             (light, importance)
   41|         })
   42|         .collect();
   43|     ranked.sort_by(|(a, a_score), (b, b_score)| {
   44|         b_score.total_cmp(a_score).then_with(|| a.id.cmp(&b.id))
   45|     });
   46| 
   47|     ranked.into_iter().map(|(light, _)| light).collect()
   48| }
   49| 
   50| fn valid(light: &LightSource) -> bool {
   51|     light.position.into_iter().all(f32::is_finite)
   52|         && light.color.into_iter().all(f32::is_finite)
   53|         && light
   54|             .half_size
   55|             .into_iter()
   56|             .all(|v| v.is_finite() && v >= 0.0)
   57|         && light.radius.is_finite()
   58|         && light.radius > 0.0
   59|         && light.intensity.is_finite()
   60|         && light.intensity > 0.0
   61| }

===== static/worker.js (106 lines) =====
    1| // Generation worker: a second instance of the same wasm module, producing
    2| // renderer-selected chunk artifacts off the main thread. The handler is
    3| // registered synchronously at module scope so no message can be lost while
    4| // the wasm module is still instantiating; work is serialized through a
    5| // promise chain.
    6| //
    7| // Protocol (main -> worker):
    8| //   { type: "init", query, seed }        one-time generator setup
    9| //   { type: "gen", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality }
   10| //                   one chunk order; artifacts is a u8 bitfield and reality
   11| //                   is Uint32Array
   12| // (worker -> main):
   13| //   { type: "done", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality, ms, buf }
   14| //                                   buf transferred, encoded by chunk_codec
   15| //   { type: "failed", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality, message }
   16| //                                   one request failed and may be retried
   17| //   { type: "fatal", message }      worker initialization failed
   18| import init, { worker_init, worker_generate } from "./pkg/wasm_frontend.js";
   19| 
   20| let wasmReady = null;
   21| function ensureWasm() {
   22|   if (!wasmReady) wasmReady = init();
   23|   return wasmReady;
   24| }
   25| 
   26| let queue = Promise.resolve();
   27| 
   28| function errorMessage(error) {
   29|   if (error instanceof Error) return error.message;
   30|   return String(error);
   31| }
   32| 
   33| function reportFailure(message, error) {
   34|   const description = errorMessage(error);
   35|   console.error("[WORKER] generation failure:", description);
   36|   try {
   37|     if (message?.type === "gen") {
   38|       postMessage({
   39|         type: "failed",
   40|         requestId: message.requestId,

   46|         reality: new Uint32Array(message.reality),
   47|         message: description,
   48|       });
   49|     } else {
   50|       postMessage({ type: "fatal", message: description });
   51|     }
   52|   } catch (reportError) {
   53|     // The browser's Worker error event is the final recovery path when even
   54|     // the structured failure message cannot be cloned or delivered.
   55|     console.error("[WORKER] could not report generation failure:", reportError);
   56|   }
   57| }
   58| 
   59| async function processMessage(message) {
   60|   await ensureWasm();
   61|   if (message.type === "init") {
   62|     worker_init(message.query, message.seed >>> 0);
   63|     return;
   64|   }
   65|   if (message.type !== "gen") return;
   66| 
   67|   const t0 = performance.now();
   68|   const reality = new Uint32Array(message.reality);
   69|   const bytes = worker_generate(
   70|     message.requestId >>> 0,
   71|     message.ox,
   72|     message.oz,
   73|     message.level,
   74|     message.lod,
   75|     message.artifacts >>> 0,
   76|     reality
   77|   );
   78|   const ms = performance.now() - t0;
   79|   console.debug(
   80|     `[WORKER] chunk (${message.ox}, ${message.oz}) lod ${message.lod} generated in ${ms.toFixed(1)} ms`
   81|   );
   82|   postMessage(
   83|     {
   84|       type: "done",
   85|       requestId: message.requestId,
   86|       ox: message.ox,
   87|       oz: message.oz,
   88|       level: message.level,
   89|       lod: message.lod,
   90|       artifacts: message.artifacts,
   91|       reality,
   92|       ms,
   93|       buf: bytes.buffer,
   94|     },
   95|     [bytes.buffer]
   96|   );
   97| }
   98| 
   99| onmessage = (event) => {
  100|   const message = event.data;
  101|   // Catch each queue item independently. A failed request must not leave the
  102|   // promise chain rejected, which would silently skip every later request.
  103|   queue = queue
  104|     .then(() => processMessage(message))
  105|     .catch((error) => reportFailure(message, error));

worker.js analysis:

1. **Unbounded queue**: `queue = queue.then(...)` — messages posted to the worker are queued in the JS promise chain unboundedly. The main thread assigns work only to workers that are "accepting" (in_flight queue in GenerationWorkerRequests), and streaming is bounded by max_concurrent_requests... but requests can be assigned to a worker whose promise chain already has many pending messages? Let's think: main thread's `request()` → `next_accepting(preferred)` picks the first worker with accepting_work=true. `accepting_work` only becomes false on disable_and_drain (worker failure). So all workers always accept work regardless of how many messages are queued in their promise chain. The engine bounds total in-flight requests by max_concurrent_requests() = pool_size. So at most pool_size outstanding requests total → each worker ≤ 1 pending... wait, is that so? The engine's streaming drives `request()` up to max_concurrent_requests concurrently. If the engine only issues requests when in-flight count < max_concurrent_requests, then each worker has at most 1 in-flight request at a time. But note the request → post_message → worker processes serially. If the engine issues a new request before the previous completes, the worker gets 2 messages queued. Given the engine's bookkeeping, requests are issued as completions come in... Actually the engine keeps at most max_concurrent_requests in flight, so with pool_size workers, at most pool_size messages outstanding — the worker promise chain queue length ≤ 1 per worker (since a worker completes before... no — the main thread can issue a new request to the same worker before the previous completes if other workers are also busy? If all pool_size slots are in flight, and one completes, the engine issues exactly one new request, possibly to the same worker that just completed. So queue depth ≤ 1. OK, but the worker-side promise chain is unbounded in principle — if the main thread ever posts faster (e.g., the fallback path or a burst after failure), messages queue up with no cap. The in_flight VecDeque in GenerationWorkerRequests is also unbounded (push_back with no cap). If the engine bugged or called request() more than max_concurrent_requests, it would grow without bound. Also: a worker that is slow (each chunk takes 42ms) — the engine keeps issuing requests as completions arrive, so ≤ 1 outstanding per worker on average. So bounded in practice by the engine's credit system. Medium/Low finding: no explicit backpressure at the driver boundary; worker promise chain unbounded if the engine's credit accounting ever diverges.

2. **Message ordering / lost replies**: worker serializes via promise chain — replies are posted in the same order as messages processed (order preserved per worker). The exact-match validation in finish_exact handles staleness. But there's a subtle race: **reality cloning**. `const reality = new Uint32Array(message.reality);` — the worker copies the reality words; main thread's `request()` builds `reality` from `request.reality.to_words()` — a fresh Uint32Array per message, no transfer, so no race there.

3. **The transfer** `[bytes.buffer]` transfers the buffer. decode on main via parse_payload → Uint8Array::new(&buffer).to_vec() — copies. Fine.

4. **Failure path**: `reportFailure` catches exceptions during `processMessage` — including a failure of `postMessage` itself? If `postMessage({type:"done"...})` throws (e.g., buffer transfer error), the catch calls `reportFailure(message, error)` — which tries to post a "failed" reply with `reality: new Uint32Array(message.reality)` — that works. OK.

5. **Race between worker replies and rAF**: main thread message events and rAF are both on the JS event loop; poll_completed is called during engine.tick inside rAF. Since JS is single-threaded, no data race; ordering is by event loop. Stale data handled by request id validation in engine.

6. **Fatal handling**: `WorkerReply::Fatal` → disable_and_drain + terminate. But a fatal message could also be followed by worker error event → disable_and_drain called twice — harmless (documented). But note: after `terminate()`, a `done` message already queued in the event loop may still be delivered? Per spec, terminate discards queued tasks. The `finished` handler uses worker_index captured by closure — after terminate, any queued message events are dropped, so fine.

7. **Missing: no timeout/hang detection**: a worker that hangs (infinite loop in wasm) never replies; the request stays in in_flight forever; the engine never fails it; streaming stalls on that chunk forever. There's no watchdog. That's a real robustness gap: "lost replies" — a hung worker permanently occupies its slot and its chunk never resolves. Also `max_concurrent_requests` = pool_size means if one worker hangs, capacity drops. Severity Medium (hang detection missing).

8. **Worker spawn**: `Worker::new_with_options` — synchronous spawn, error → Err → fallback to same-thread. OK.

9. **postMessage ordering with init**: init is posted after handlers are set — fine. But note `worker_index` captured in closures by value — each closure has its own index. Good.

10. **reported_emergency_fallback** — only warns once, but keeps falling back on every request while pool is exhausted — sync generation on main thread per request → main-thread jank. Acceptable given it's the fallback.

Now, one more subtle issue in worker_source.rs: In the `request()` method, `assign` is called BEFORE `post_message`. If post_message fails → disable_and_drain drains the assigned request — good. But if post_message succeeds, the request is in in_flight. If the worker dies without replying and without error event (e.g., terminated by browser), the request stays forever. Again no timeout.

Another subtle issue: `next_accepting` is called on `self.requests.borrow()` then `assign` on `borrow_mut()` — two separate borrows, no interleaving issue (single-threaded).

**Potential race on `WorkerReply::Completed` vs engine re-request**: `finish_exact` returns true only for the exact request; if the request was already failed and re-issued with a new id, the stale reply is dropped. Good.

Now lib.rs — the atomics + spawn_local + settings crossing JS boundary.

Notes so far:
- `cluster_scene_lights.rs`: `append_lights_reaching_bounds` is O(L) per call — L = lights in scene. Called per chunk → O(C × L) per frame potentially. Need to see callers. `LightSelectionCache` — HashMap keyed by chunk key, values Vec<u64> of selected ids. `previous_ids.contains()` — Vec contains is O(top_k), fine. But the cache has unbounded growth: entries never evicted — chunk keys accumulate forever as player walks. Unbounded growth finding.
- `lights.rs select_lights`: O(N log N) sort per frame over all fixture lights — fine if N small.
- `upload_scene_lights.rs`: `last_lights == lights` comparison O(L) per frame — fine. Upload O(L). Note `staging.resize` reallocates each time the count changes. OK.

===== wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/trace_voxel_scene/construct_camera_ray.rs (12 lines) =====
    1| //! Construct one normalized world-space camera ray from the fullscreen UV.
    2| 
    3| pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
    4| vec3 constructCameraRay() {
    5|     vec2 ndc = vUv * 2.0 - 1.0;
    6|     return normalize(
    7|         uCamRight * (ndc.x * uAspect * uFovTan)
    8|         + uCamUp * (ndc.y * uFovTan)
    9|         + uCamForward
   10|     );
   11| }
   12| "#;

Big finding in the GLSL raymarcher: `shade_voxel_hit.rs` — for each hit, loops over `lightCount` lights of the receiver chunk and for each light calls `evaluateVisibleSceneLight` which for rectangle lights runs 4 Gauss samples, each calling `directSampleIsVisible` which loops over ALL `uNumChunks` chunks, and for each chunk runs a full `traceChunk` (up to 768 steps). So per-pixel worst case: 1 primary trace (768 steps) + L × 4 × C × 768 steps. With L up to maybe dozens and C=25: 25 chunks × 768 steps × 4 samples × L lights = massive per-pixel cost. That's the biggest algorithmic issue in the shader: O(P · C · L · S) per frame where P = pixels, C = chunk count (≤25), L = lights in receiver chunk, S = trace steps (≤768). Plus primary trace O(P · C · S).

Also `directSampleIsVisible` is called even for the 4 Gauss samples of a rectangle light — worst case 4× per light. And there's no early exit or caching of visibility per (surface, light). It also doesn't limit light count per chunk: `uChunkLightCounts[receiverChunkIndex]` — with the scene light texture, a chunk's light count could be large (e.g., 40+ in tests). For each of those it loops over all 25 chunks. That's the "nested loops over lights/chunks" the parent flagged.

Also `collectOrderedChunkIntervals` is insertion sort O(C²) but C=25, negligible.

`traceChunkDda` loop bound is 768 steps — worst case per chunk per ray; in `selectNearestVoxelHit` it traces every chunk interval (up to 25) without early exit on hit unless front-to-back. So worst case 25 × 768 = 19,200 steps per pixel primary. Plus shadow: L × 4 × 25 × 768.

Also `lookupVoxelLeaf` — restarts at root each step: depth up to 10 levels, each an atlas fetch. Fine (documented choice), O(depth) per lookup with 1 texel fetch per level.

----- lines 7278-7401 -----
Key finding in surface_webgl/draw.rs:

1. `prepare_visible_draws` (lines 262-312): for each visible mesh (V), calls `append_lights_reaching_bounds` which iterates over ALL frame lights (L). So O(V × L) per frame. V is up to resident chunks (~25), L is the full scene light list (could be hundreds). This is a real per-frame CPU cost: for each chunk, scanning all lights. Fix: precompute per-chunk light lists, or use a spatial hash/grid of lights, or compute once per frame per chunk (the same computation is repeated every frame — no caching by chunk). Actually wait — is there a cache? `LightSelectionCache` in cluster_scene_lights.rs exists but is it used here? Not in this file. Let me grep for `select_lights_with_hysteresis` usage.

2. `hero_local_index` check at line 299-303: `hero_id == Some(clustered[lights.first as usize].id)` — fine O(1).

3. Shadow pass iterates all meshes O(M) per frame — fine.

4. `draw_mesh` binds per mesh: ~10 uniform calls + texture bind per draw — acceptable for ~25 draws.

Note there's an important bug-ish thing: `renderer.timer.begin(&self.gl, false)` — timer disabled always (line 127: `self.timer.begin(&self.gl, false)` — hardcoded false!). So GPU timer never starts for surface renderer. `timer.poll` is called but begin is passed false, meaning pending query never created; stats gpu_ms always 0.0. Actually poll would collect nothing. So `GpuFrameTimer` for surface is dead code — telemetry shows GPU 0.00ms always. That's a Medium finding (the toggle `rt_timer`/RenderToggles::gpu_timer is documented but begin is hardcoded false). Let me check other drivers to see if they pass the toggle.

The prior analysis already confirmed a lot. Now let me read the sections around line 12369 (raymarch per-pixel), 12847 (render_options.x), 15294-15300 (SurfacePipeline draw), 16896-16907 (WebGPU vs WebGL2 budgets), and 19673-19708 (SceneLightTexture + top findings), and the very end of the log.
----- lines 12360-12400 -----

1. `raymarch_analytic_direct` (lines 649-668): loops over `frame.render_options.x` = lights.len() — the full frame light count (all lights in the frame, from `collect_frame_lights`). For each light, `evaluate_visible_scene_light` → if direct visibility enabled (shadow_pass + profile) → `finite_segment_visible` → loop over up to 25 chunks, each with `trace_visibility_chunk_skipping_empty_leaves` up to 4096 steps each but with a global remaining budget of 4096 (DIRECT_VISIBILITY_TRACE_BUDGET). So per light per pixel: up to 4096 steps × per chunk loop. With L lights: worst case L × 4096 × (chunk count) steps per pixel — that's enormous: 60 lights × 4096 = 245k iterations per pixel. Actually the remaining_steps budget is per `finite_segment_visible` call, not per pixel: each light gets a fresh 4096 budget. So worst-case per pixel: L × 4096 lookup_leaf calls (each up to 11 atlas fetches). That's the worst algorithmic hotspot: O(P × L × B) with B = 4096, L = number of lights. There's an early-out: `if !has_positive_rgb(unoccluded) continue;` before the visibility trace — so only lights that actually contribute get traced. Still, in a lit corridor with dozens of lights this is the dominant cost.

Note also that light count is `frame.render_options.x` — the FULL frame light list (all resident lights, not just receiver chunk lights). In the GLSL version, shading loops only over the receiver chunk's light range (uChunkLightFirst/Counts); in the WGSL version it loops over ALL frame lights (no per-chunk light ranges). That's an important difference: the WGSL raymarcher loops over every light in the frame at each hit pixel, whereas the GLSL one loops only over the receiver chunk's clustered lights. So this is O(P·L) shading per pixel where L = total scene lights — significant. `frame.render_options.x` is `lights.len()` set in GpuFrameUniforms::from_frame. Let me confirm in gpu_types.rs.

2. `surface_radiance` (else branch, no direct visibility): loops over lights too (render_options.x).

3. Primary loop: `chunk_count` up to 25, each `trace_chunk` up to 4096 steps (budget from `frame.render_options.w` = maximum_trace_steps). With front-to-back and clipping to nearest distance. Worst case O(25 × 4096).

So overall per pixel worst case: primary O(C·S) + shading O(L·(C·B)) — the shading is the killer. GPU parallelization is inherent (fragment shader), so the "hot loop" concern is about per-fragment work.

Also `lookup_leaf` does an 11-level dependent fetch chain per step with no caching — each step re-walks from root (stateless, documented tradeoff). For DDA with 4096 steps... 4096 × 11 = 45k dependent storage loads per ray. That's the empty-space-skip mitigation; fine.

Interesting: WebGPU SurfacePipeline draw — `draw: [0, light_count, 0, 0]` — light_first=0, light_count=ALL frame lights for every chunk. So the WebGPU surface fragment shader loops over ALL lights for every fragment (raster_surface_radiance with light_first=0, light_count=frame light count). In contrast, WebGL2 surface uses per-chunk clustered ranges. So the WebGPU surface path does O(P × L) per frame with L = all frame lights (unclustered). That's another finding: WebGPU raster paths don't use per-chunk light clustering at all; every fragment evaluates every light (rectangular lights = 4 Gauss samples each). This is a real regression vs the WebGL2 path.

Also note draw_shadow_pass draws EVERY resident chunk into the shadow map with no culling — matches WebGL (documented) but shadow pass cost.

- Frame scene_lights can be 100+ fixtures; capped at MAX_ANALYTIC_SCENE_LIGHTS_PER_FRAME = 48 in the copy handed to renderer (per the comment — need to confirm where the cap is applied — in engine prepare_frame_lighting presumably; that's out of scope but the cap exists).
- WebGL2 raster drivers (surface/splat/surfel) select top-16 (MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS=16) camera-ranked lights for the uniform arrays — bounded 16.
- WebGPU raster drivers use the whole frame list (up to 48) with no clustering and no ranking. Every vertex of every face evaluates up to 48 lights × 4 Gauss samples.

Wait, actually for WebGPU surface: `draw: [0, light_count, 0, 0]` where light_count = lights.len() passed to pipeline.draw — which is `collect_frame_lights(frame).len()`. So all 48 max. And no distance rejection in shader (evaluate_scene_light computes everything). Actually wait — finite_range_inverse_square returns 0 quickly if d2 >= range2? Let's check: it computes rangeSquared, normalizedSquared, window = max(1 - ns², 0)... it still computes the full formula. There is no `if distanceSquared >= rangeSquared return 0` early-out in evaluate_scene_light — only in the WebGL2 splat shader (`if (d2 >= range2) continue;`). So WebGPU evaluates all lights fully.

So: WebGPU surface/splat fragment+vertex = O(L) per sample with no spatial pruning, L ≤ 48. WebGL2 = O(16) with early range rejection. Both bounded, but WebGPU's is 3× more lights and no early-out. The important nuance: WebGL2 splat has `if (d2 >= range2) continue` per light (early exit), WebGPU has none. And in WebGL2 the vertex shader light loop is 16 fixed, in WebGPU it's the full list.

Hmm, but the bigger problem: 100+ fixture lights, capped at 48 — the WebGPU raster shaders always pay 48 × 4 = 192 quadrature samples per vertex even when the light is across the map. The per-chunk clustering (append_lights_reaching_bounds) exists in WebGL2 but WebGPU doesn't use it at all for raster. This is a solid High finding.

Now, WebGPU raymarch: `raymarch_analytic_direct` loops `frame.render_options.x` lights (up to 48+4 dynamic), each with `finite_segment_visible` (when direct visibility enabled: profile capability && rt shadow_pass default true) — per light up to 4096 steps across 25 chunks. Worst case 52 × 4096 = 213k leaf lookups per pixel. With 1080p ≈ 2M pixels — utterly prohibitive; but real-world: `has_positive_rgb` gates most lights out (only lights near the surface contribute; the light's range check inside point_light_sample_irradiance returns 0 weight → has_positive_rgb false → skip visibility). So effective cost = number of lights within range of the hit point. In a dense corridor, maybe 10-30 lights in range → 30 × 4096 = 123k steps/pixel worst case, average maybe 100-1000 steps per light. Still the dominant cost. It's a genuine High/Critical perf issue — the parent's focus area. It is bounded by DIRECT_VISIBILITY_TRACE_BUDGET per light per pixel.

GLSL raymarch: worse — per light, per Gauss sample (4), per chunk (25) with 768-step loops, no global budget. `directSampleIsVisible` loop over uNumChunks with traceChunk inside (768 steps each). So O(L_c × 4 × C × 768). L_c = chunk light count (could be 40+ in a dense chunk). Unbounded (no cap on lightCount per chunk — the clustered list has no cap; append_lights_reaching_bounds has no slot cap. In the test, 40 lights all reach bounds). This is the worst shader: 40 lights × 4 samples × 25 chunks × 768 = 3M steps per pixel worst case. High/Critical.

Also GLSL raymarch `shade_voxel_hit` uses `uChunkLightCounts[receiverChunkIndex]` — the light count per chunk is derived from `append_lights_reaching_bounds` — no cap. And the scene light texture can be huge (all lights in frame). OK.

   54|         );
   55|     }
   56|     for (int lightIndex = 0; lightIndex < 4; ++lightIndex) {
   57|         if (lightIndex >= uDynamicLightCount) break;
   58|         analyticDirect += evaluateVisiblePointLight(
   59|             worldPosition,
   60|             hit.normal,
   61|             uDynamicPosRadius[lightIndex].xyz,
   62|             uDynamicColorIntensity[lightIndex].rgb,
   63|             uDynamicPosRadius[lightIndex].w,
   64|             uDynamicColorIntensity[lightIndex].a,
   65|             receiverVoxelSize
   66|         );
   67|     }
   68| 
   69|     vec3 radiance = albedo * (
   70|         ambient + analyticDirect
   71|     ) * (1.0 / PI);
   72|     if (uFlashlightEnabled == 1) {
   73|         radiance += albedo * spotBeam(
   74|             uCameraPosition, uCamForward, worldPosition, hit.normal
   75|         );
   76|     }
   77|     return radiance;
   78| }
   79| "#;

    1| //! Occlusion queries from a visible voxel face to analytic emitter samples.
    2| //!
    3| //! The primary-ray hit and every shadow segment use the same chunk slabs,
    4| //! stateless SVO lookup, and selected stepping policy. Rectangle visibility
    5| //! is evaluated at the same four Gauss samples as its irradiance integral;
    6| //! a center-only visibility term would leak around partial blockers.
    7| 
    8| pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
    9| bool directSampleIsVisible(
   10|     vec3 surfacePosition,
   11|     vec3 surfaceNormal,
   12|     vec3 samplePosition,
   13|     float receiverVoxelSize
   14| ) {
   15|     if (uDirectVisibilityEnabled == 0) return true;
   16| 
   17|     float bias = max(receiverVoxelSize * 1e-3, 1e-5);
   18|     vec3 segmentOrigin = surfacePosition + surfaceNormal * bias;
   19|     vec3 segment = samplePosition - segmentOrigin;
   20|     float segmentLength = length(segment);
   21|     if (!(segmentLength > bias * 2.0)) return true;
   22|     vec3 direction = segment / segmentLength;
   23|     float blockerLimit = segmentLength - bias * 2.0;
   24| 
   25|     for (int chunkIndex = 0; chunkIndex < uNumChunks; ++chunkIndex) {
   26|         vec3 localOrigin = segmentOrigin - uChunkOrigins[chunkIndex];
   27|         RayBoxHit box = intersectBox(
   28|             localOrigin,
   29|             direction,
   30|             vec3(0.0),
   31|             vec3(uChunkWorldSizes[chunkIndex])
   32|         );
   33|         if (!box.hit || box.entry >= blockerLimit) continue;
   34|         box.exit = min(box.exit, blockerLimit);
   35|         VoxelHit blocker = traceChunk(
   36|             localOrigin,
   37|             direction,
   38|             uChunkRootIndices[chunkIndex],
   39|             uChunkWorldSizes[chunkIndex],
   40|             uChunkVoxelSizes[chunkIndex],
   41|             uChunkDepths[chunkIndex],
   42|             box
   43|         );
   44|         if (blocker.hit && blocker.distance < blockerLimit) return false;
   45|     }
   46|     return true;
   47| }
   48| 
   49| vec3 evaluateVisiblePointLight(
   50|     vec3 surfacePosition,
   51|     vec3 normal,
   52|     vec3 lightPosition,
   53|     vec3 lightColor,
   54|     float range,
   55|     float intensity,
   56|     float receiverVoxelSize
   57| ) {
   58|     vec3 delta = lightPosition - surfacePosition;
   59|     float distanceSquared = dot(delta, delta);
   60|     vec3 surfaceToLight = delta * inversesqrt(max(distanceSquared, 1e-8));
   61|     float weight = finiteRangeInverseSquare(distanceSquared, range)
   62|         * receiverCosine(normal, surfaceToLight);
   63|     if (!(weight > 0.0)
   64|         || !directSampleIsVisible(
   65|             surfacePosition, normal, lightPosition, receiverVoxelSize
   66|         )) {
   67|         return vec3(0.0);
   68|     }
   69|     return max(lightColor, vec3(0.0)) * max(intensity, 0.0) * weight;
   70| }
   71| 
   72| vec3 evaluateVisibleSceneLight(
   73|     vec3 surfacePosition,
   74|     vec3 normal,
   75|     SceneLight light,
   76|     float receiverVoxelSize
   77| ) {
   78|     if (light.kind == LIGHT_POINT) {
   79|         return evaluateVisiblePointLight(
   80|             surfacePosition, normal, light.position, light.color,
   81|             light.range, light.intensity, receiverVoxelSize
   82|         );
   83|     }
   84| 
   85|     float area = 4.0 * max(light.halfSize.x, 0.0) * max(light.halfSize.y, 0.0);
   86|     if (!(area > 0.0)) return vec3(0.0);
   87|     const float GAUSS = 0.5773502691896258;
   88|     vec2 offsets[4] = vec2[](
   89|         vec2(-GAUSS, -GAUSS), vec2(GAUSS, -GAUSS),
   90|         vec2(-GAUSS,  GAUSS), vec2(GAUSS,  GAUSS)
   91|     );
   92|     float integral = 0.0;
   93|     for (int sampleIndex = 0; sampleIndex < 4; ++sampleIndex) {
   94|         vec2 offset = offsets[sampleIndex] * light.halfSize;
   95|         vec3 samplePosition = light.position + vec3(offset.x, 0.0, offset.y);
   96|         vec3 delta = samplePosition - surfacePosition;
   97|         float distanceSquared = dot(delta, delta);
   98|         vec3 surfaceToLight = delta * inversesqrt(max(distanceSquared, 1e-8));
   99|         float weight = finiteRangeInverseSquare(distanceSquared, light.range)
  100|             * receiverCosine(normal, surfaceToLight)
  101|             * emitterCosine(light.kind, surfaceToLight);
  102|         if (weight > 0.0
  103|             && directSampleIsVisible(
  104|                 surfacePosition, normal, samplePosition, receiverVoxelSize
  105|             )) {
  106|             integral += weight;
  107|         }
  108|     }
  109|     return max(light.color, vec3(0.0)) * max(light.intensity, 0.0)
  110|         * area * (integral * 0.25);
  111| }
  112| "#;
    1| //! Exact ray/box math, diagnostic DDA, and optional empty-leaf stepping.
    2| 
    3| pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
    4| const float TRACE_INFINITY = 1e30;
    5| const float TRACE_MIN_TIE_EPSILON = 1e-7;
    6| 
    7| struct RayBoxHit {
    8|     bool hit;
    9|     float entry;
   10|     float exit;
   11|     vec3 entryNormal;
   12| };
   13| 
   14| struct ChunkInterval {
   15|     int chunkIndex;
   16|     float entry;
   17|     float exit;
   18|     vec3 entryNormal;
   19| };
   20| 
   21| struct VoxelHit {
   22|     bool hit;
   23|     float distance;
   24|     vec3 normal;
   25|     uint material;
   26|     uint color;
   27|     uint lightWord;
   28| };
   29| 
   30| float inverseDirection(float direction) {
   31|     if (abs(direction) < 1e-20) {
   32|         return direction < 0.0 ? -TRACE_INFINITY : TRACE_INFINITY;
   33|     }
   34|     return 1.0 / direction;
   35| }
   36| 
   37| float distanceTieTolerance(float distance) {
   38|     return max(abs(distance) * 1e-6, TRACE_MIN_TIE_EPSILON);
   39| }
   40| 
   41| float traversalSampleBias(float voxelSize) {
   42|     // This moves classification points off an exactly shared plane; it must
   43|     // remain smaller than nearby, genuinely distinct boundary crossings.
   44|     // At the 0.2 m reference grid, 1e-4 skipped a 13 micrometre
   45|     // interval between a wall and ceiling and changed the reported face.
   46|     return max(voxelSize * 1e-5, TRACE_MIN_TIE_EPSILON);
   47| }
   48| 
   49| RayBoxHit intersectBox(vec3 rayOrigin, vec3 rayDirection, vec3 boundsMin, vec3 boundsMax) {
   50|     // Parallel axes are handled explicitly so a boundary value never forms
   51|     // the undefined product 0 * infinity.
   52|     if ((abs(rayDirection.x) < 1e-20 && (rayOrigin.x < boundsMin.x || rayOrigin.x > boundsMax.x))
   53|         || (abs(rayDirection.y) < 1e-20 && (rayOrigin.y < boundsMin.y || rayOrigin.y > boundsMax.y))
   54|         || (abs(rayDirection.z) < 1e-20 && (rayOrigin.z < boundsMin.z || rayOrigin.z > boundsMax.z))) {
   55|         return RayBoxHit(false, 0.0, 0.0, vec3(0.0));
   56|     }
   57| 
   58|     vec3 inverseRay = vec3(
   59|         inverseDirection(rayDirection.x),
   60|         inverseDirection(rayDirection.y),
   61|         inverseDirection(rayDirection.z)
   62|     );
   63|     vec3 first = (boundsMin - rayOrigin) * inverseRay;
   64|     vec3 second = (boundsMax - rayOrigin) * inverseRay;
   65|     vec3 nearTimes = min(first, second);
   66|     vec3 farTimes = max(first, second);
   67|     if (abs(rayDirection.x) < 1e-20) { nearTimes.x = -TRACE_INFINITY; farTimes.x = TRACE_INFINITY; }
   68|     if (abs(rayDirection.y) < 1e-20) { nearTimes.y = -TRACE_INFINITY; farTimes.y = TRACE_INFINITY; }
   69|     if (abs(rayDirection.z) < 1e-20) { nearTimes.z = -TRACE_INFINITY; farTimes.z = TRACE_INFINITY; }
   70| 
   71|     float entry = max(nearTimes.x, max(nearTimes.y, nearTimes.z));
   72|     float exit = min(farTimes.x, min(farTimes.y, farTimes.z));
   73|     if (entry > exit || exit < 0.0) {
   74|         return RayBoxHit(false, entry, exit, vec3(0.0));
   75|     }
   76| 
   77|     vec3 normal;
   78|     if (entry <= 0.0) {
   79|         vec3 absoluteRay = abs(rayDirection);
   80|         if (absoluteRay.x >= absoluteRay.y && absoluteRay.x >= absoluteRay.z) normal = vec3(-sign(rayDirection.x), 0.0, 0.0);
   81|         else if (absoluteRay.y >= absoluteRay.z) normal = vec3(0.0, -sign(rayDirection.y), 0.0);
   82|         else normal = vec3(0.0, 0.0, -sign(rayDirection.z));
   83|     } else if (nearTimes.x >= nearTimes.y && nearTimes.x >= nearTimes.z) {
   84|         normal = vec3(rayDirection.x > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0, 0.0, 0.0);
   85|     } else if (nearTimes.y >= nearTimes.z) {
   86|         normal = vec3(0.0, rayDirection.y > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0, 0.0);
   87|     } else {
   88|         normal = vec3(0.0, 0.0, rayDirection.z > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0);
   89|     }
   90|     return RayBoxHit(true, max(entry, 0.0), exit, normal);
   91| }
   92| 
   93| float exitDistanceFromBox(
   94|     vec3 rayOrigin,
   95|     vec3 rayDirection,
   96|     vec3 boundsMin,
   97|     vec3 boundsMax,
   98|     out vec3 nextNormal
   99| ) {
  100|     vec3 exitTimes = vec3(TRACE_INFINITY);

Verified the GLSL shade_voxel_hit + directSampleIsVisible structure. Now let me look at traceChunk (in intersect_voxel_scene.rs remainder) to confirm the 768-step budget and chunk count limits, and the chunks.rs (shared GLSL) for chunk count constants.
  100|     vec3 exitTimes = vec3(TRACE_INFINITY);
  101|     if (abs(rayDirection.x) >= 1e-20) exitTimes.x = ((rayDirection.x > 0.0 ? boundsMax.x : boundsMin.x) - rayOrigin.x) / rayDirection.x;
  102|     if (abs(rayDirection.y) >= 1e-20) exitTimes.y = ((rayDirection.y > 0.0 ? boundsMax.y : boundsMin.y) - rayOrigin.y) / rayDirection.y;
  103|     if (abs(rayDirection.z) >= 1e-20) exitTimes.z = ((rayDirection.z > 0.0 ? boundsMax.z : boundsMin.z) - rayOrigin.z) / rayDirection.z;
  104| 
  105|     float nearest = min(exitTimes.x, min(exitTimes.y, exitTimes.z));
  106|     // Traversal bias and tie tolerance solve different problems. The former
  107|     // moves a sample into the next cell; using that comparatively large value
  108|     // here incorrectly merges distinct, very close wall/ceiling crossings.
  109|     float tolerance = distanceTieTolerance(nearest);
  110|     // Use the same tolerant X/Y/Z precedence as finest-cell DDA. Without
  111|     // this, a mathematically tied edge ray can acquire a different face
  112|     // normal solely because one path jumped across a larger empty leaf.
  113|     if (abs(exitTimes.x - nearest) <= tolerance) {
  114|         nextNormal = vec3(rayDirection.x > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0, 0.0, 0.0);
  115|         return nearest;
  116|     }
  117|     if (abs(exitTimes.y - nearest) <= tolerance) {
  118|         nextNormal = vec3(0.0, rayDirection.y > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0, 0.0);
  119|         return nearest;
  120|     }
  121|     nextNormal = vec3(0.0, 0.0, rayDirection.z > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0);
  122|     return nearest;
  123| }

  125| VoxelHit traceChunkDda(
  126|     vec3 rayOrigin,
  127|     vec3 rayDirection,
  128|     int rootIndex,
  129|     float worldSize,
  130|     float voxelSize,
  131|     int svoDepth,
  132|     RayBoxHit chunkBox
  133| );
  134| 
  135| VoxelHit traceChunkSkippingEmptyLeaves(
  136|     vec3 rayOrigin,
  137|     vec3 rayDirection,
  138|     int rootIndex,
  139|     float worldSize,
  140|     float voxelSize,
  141|     int svoDepth,
  142|     RayBoxHit chunkBox
  143| ) {
  144|     float distance = chunkBox.entry;
  145|     vec3 normal = chunkBox.entryNormal;
  146|     float sampleBias = traversalSampleBias(voxelSize);
  147|     float refinementEntry = chunkBox.entry;
  148|     vec3 refinementEntryNormal = chunkBox.entryNormal;
  149| 
  150|     for (int stepIndex = 0; stepIndex < 768; ++stepIndex) {
  151|         if (distance > chunkBox.exit) break;
  152|         vec3 samplePoint = rayOrigin + rayDirection * min(distance + sampleBias, chunkBox.exit);
  153|         VoxelLeaf leaf = lookupVoxelLeaf(samplePoint, rootIndex, worldSize, svoDepth);
  154|         if (leaf.material != 0u) {
  155|             // The coarse walk proves emptiness only. Resolve the final
  156|             // voxel-scale crossing with the diagnostic algorithm so both
  157|             // policies produce one canonical distance, material, and normal.
  158|             RayBoxHit refinementBox = RayBoxHit(
  159|                 true, refinementEntry, chunkBox.exit, refinementEntryNormal
  160|             );
  161|             return traceChunkDda(
  162|                 rayOrigin,
  163|                 rayDirection,
  164|                 rootIndex,
  165|                 worldSize,
  166|                 voxelSize,
  167|                 svoDepth,
  168|                 refinementBox
  169|             );
  170|         }
  171| 
  172|         vec3 crossedNormal;
  173|         float nextDistance = exitDistanceFromBox(
  174|             rayOrigin, rayDirection, leaf.boundsMin, leaf.boundsMax, crossedNormal
  175|         );
  176|         if (nextDistance <= distance + sampleBias * 0.25) {
  177|             nextDistance = distance + sampleBias;
  178|         }
  179|         // A normalized ray moves at most one voxel per axis over this short
  180|         // interval. Retaining it lets the exact resolver reconstruct every
  181|         // potentially competing face without replaying the skipped octant.
  182|         refinementEntry = max(distance, nextDistance - voxelSize);
  183|         refinementEntryNormal = normal;
  184|         distance = nextDistance;
  185|         normal = crossedNormal;
  186|     }
  187|     return VoxelHit(false, 0.0, vec3(0.0), 0u, 0u, 0u);
  188| }
  189| 
  190| VoxelHit traceChunkDda(
  191|     vec3 rayOrigin,
  192|     vec3 rayDirection,
  193|     int rootIndex,
  194|     float worldSize,
  195|     float voxelSize,
  196|     int svoDepth,
  197|     RayBoxHit chunkBox
  198| ) {
  199|     float sampleBias = traversalSampleBias(voxelSize);
  200|     float distance = chunkBox.entry;
  201|     vec3 samplePoint = rayOrigin + rayDirection * min(distance + sampleBias, chunkBox.exit);
  202|     vec3 cell = floor(samplePoint / voxelSize);
  203|     vec3 directionStep = sign(rayDirection);
  204|     vec3 normal = chunkBox.entryNormal;
  205| 
  206|     for (int stepIndex = 0; stepIndex < 768; ++stepIndex) {
  207|         if (distance > chunkBox.exit) break;
  208|         samplePoint = rayOrigin + rayDirection * min(distance + sampleBias, chunkBox.exit);
  209|         VoxelLeaf leaf = lookupVoxelLeaf(samplePoint, rootIndex, worldSize, svoDepth);
  210|         if (leaf.material != 0u) {
  211|             return VoxelHit(true, distance, normal, leaf.material, leaf.color, leaf.lightWord);
  212|         }
  213| 
  214|         // Recompute boundary times from the canonical integer cell each step.
  215|         // Repeated `nextTime += deltaTime` accumulates enough rounding error
  216|         // to reverse two distinct wall/ceiling crossings near a long ray.
  217|         vec3 nextBoundary = (cell + max(directionStep, vec3(0.0))) * voxelSize;
  218|         vec3 nextTimes = vec3(TRACE_INFINITY);
  219|         if (abs(rayDirection.x) >= 1e-20) nextTimes.x = (nextBoundary.x - rayOrigin.x) / rayDirection.x;
  220|         if (abs(rayDirection.y) >= 1e-20) nextTimes.y = (nextBoundary.y - rayOrigin.y) / rayDirection.y;
  221|         if (abs(rayDirection.z) >= 1e-20) nextTimes.z = (nextBoundary.z - rayOrigin.z) / rayDirection.z;
  222| 
  223|         float nextDistance = min(nextTimes.x, min(nextTimes.y, nextTimes.z));
  224|         if (nextDistance > chunkBox.exit) break;
  225|         // Step every tied axis so a ray through an edge/corner cannot stall.
  226|         // This is a floating-point equality tolerance, not the sampling bias.
  227|         // Keeping them separate preserves the mathematically nearer face when
  228|         // two boundaries are close but not actually coincident.
  229|         float tieEpsilon = distanceTieTolerance(nextDistance);
  230|         bool crossX = abs(nextTimes.x - nextDistance) <= tieEpsilon;
  231|         bool crossY = abs(nextTimes.y - nextDistance) <= tieEpsilon;
  232|         bool crossZ = abs(nextTimes.z - nextDistance) <= tieEpsilon;
  233|         if (crossX) cell.x += directionStep.x;
  234|         if (crossY) cell.y += directionStep.y;
  235|         if (crossZ) cell.z += directionStep.z;
  236|         if (crossX) normal = vec3(-directionStep.x, 0.0, 0.0);
  237|         else if (crossY) normal = vec3(0.0, -directionStep.y, 0.0);
  238|         else normal = vec3(0.0, 0.0, -directionStep.z);
  239|         distance = nextDistance;
  240|     }
  241|     return VoxelHit(false, 0.0, vec3(0.0), 0u, 0u, 0u);
  242| }
  243| 
  244| VoxelHit traceChunk(
  245|     vec3 rayOrigin,
  246|     vec3 rayDirection,
  247|     int rootIndex,
  248|     float worldSize,
  249|     float voxelSize,
  250|     int svoDepth,
  251|     RayBoxHit chunkBox
  252| ) {
  253|     if (uEmptySpaceSkipEnabled == 1) {
  254|         return traceChunkSkippingEmptyLeaves(
  255|             rayOrigin, rayDirection, rootIndex, worldSize, voxelSize, svoDepth, chunkBox
  256|         );
  257|     }
  258|     return traceChunkDda(
  259|         rayOrigin, rayDirection, rootIndex, worldSize, voxelSize, svoDepth, chunkBox
  260|     );
  261| }

    1| //! Conservative finite-range fixture clustering for a world-space AABB.
    2| //!
    3| //! Both rewritten GPU paths use this exact predicate. It removes work, not
    4| //! light: a fixture is omitted only when no point on its rectangle can be
    5| //! within its compact-support range of any receiver in the bounds.
    6| 
    7| use crate::application::ports::LightSource;
    8| 
    9| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   10| pub struct LightRange {
   11|     pub first: i32,
   12|     pub count: i32,
   13| }
   14| 
   15| pub fn append_lights_reaching_bounds(
   16|     lights: &[LightSource],
   17|     bounds_min: [f32; 3],
   18|     bounds_max: [f32; 3],
   19|     clustered: &mut Vec<LightSource>,
   20| ) -> LightRange {
   21|     let first = clustered.len();
   22|     clustered.extend(
   23|         lights
   24|             .iter()
   25|             .copied()
   26|             .filter(|light| reaches_bounds(light, bounds_min, bounds_max)),
   27|     );
   28|     LightRange {
   29|         first: first.min(i32::MAX as usize) as i32,
   30|         count: clustered.len().saturating_sub(first).min(i32::MAX as usize) as i32,
   31|     }
   32| }
   33| 
   34| fn reaches_bounds(light: &LightSource, bounds_min: [f32; 3], bounds_max: [f32; 3]) -> bool {
   35|     // Expanding X/Z by the emitter half-size converts rectangle-to-box
   36|     // distance into point-to-box distance (the Minkowski-sum construction).
   37|     let expanded_min = [
   38|         bounds_min[0] - light.half_size[0],
   39|         bounds_min[1],
   40|         bounds_min[2] - light.half_size[1],
   41|     ];
   42|     let expanded_max = [
   43|         bounds_max[0] + light.half_size[0],
   44|         bounds_max[1],
   45|         bounds_max[2] + light.half_size[1],
   46|     ];
   47|     let mut distance_squared = 0.0;
   48|     for axis in 0..3 {
   49|         let delta = if light.position[axis] < expanded_min[axis] {
   50|             expanded_min[axis] - light.position[axis]
   51|         } else if light.position[axis] > expanded_max[axis] {
   52|             light.position[axis] - expanded_max[axis]
   53|         } else {
   54|             0.0
   55|         };
   56|         distance_squared += delta * delta;
   57|     }
   58|     distance_squared <= light.radius * light.radius
   59| }
   60| 
   61| /// Persistent cache for per-chunk top-K light selection with hysteresis.
   62| ///
   63| /// # Rationale & Design Pattern (Observer & Strategy Pattern)
   64| /// Prevents light popping across chunk seams when camera movement or floating point sorting
   65| /// slight changes candidate light order. A candidate replaces an existing selected light only
   66| /// if its calculated importance score exceeds the existing light's score by at least 20%.
   67| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
   68| pub struct LightSelectionCache {
   69|     entries: std::collections::HashMap<crate::application::ports::SurfaceChunkKey, Vec<u64>>,
   70| }
   71| 
   72| impl LightSelectionCache {
   73|     pub fn new() -> Self {
   74|         Self {
   75|             entries: std::collections::HashMap::new(),
   76|         }
   77|     }
   78| 
   79|     /// Ranks lights reaching bounds and applies a hysteresis filter against previous frame selection.
   80|     pub fn select_lights_with_hysteresis(
   81|         &mut self,
   82|         key: crate::application::ports::SurfaceChunkKey,
   83|         candidate_lights: &[LightSource],
   84|         bounds_min: [f32; 3],
   85|         bounds_max: [f32; 3],
   86|         top_k: usize,
   87|     ) -> Vec<LightSource> {
   88|         let center = [
   89|             (bounds_min[0] + bounds_max[0]) * 0.5,
   90|             (bounds_min[1] + bounds_max[1]) * 0.5,
   91|             (bounds_min[2] + bounds_max[2]) * 0.5,
   92|         ];
   93| 
   94|         // Rank candidates by estimated irradiance score = intensity / (distance_sq + 1.0)
   95|         let mut scored: Vec<(f32, &LightSource)> = candidate_lights
   96|             .iter()
   97|             .map(|light| {
   98|                 let dx = light.position[0] - center[0];
   99|                 let dy = light.position[1] - center[1];
  100|                 let dz = light.position[2] - center[2];
  101|                 let dist_sq = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz;
  102|                 let score = light.intensity / (dist_sq + 1.0);
  103|                 (score, light)
  104|             })
  105|             .collect();
  106|         scored.sort_by(|a, b| b.0.partial_cmp(&a.0).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
  107| 
  108|         let previous_ids = self.entries.get(&key);
  109|         let mut selected = Vec::with_capacity(top_k.min(scored.len()));
  110| 
  111|         for (score, light) in scored {
  112|             if selected.len() >= top_k {
  113|                 break;
  114|             }
  115|             let is_previously_selected = previous_ids.map_or(false, |ids| ids.contains(&light.id));
  116|             let effective_score = if is_previously_selected {
  117|                 score * 1.20 // 20% hysteresis boost to retain current lights and prevent seam popping
  118|             } else {
  119|                 score
  120|             };
  121|             selected.push((effective_score, light));
  122|         }
  123| 
  124|         selected.sort_by(|a, b| b.0.partial_cmp(&a.0).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
  125|         let result: Vec<LightSource> = selected.into_iter().take(top_k).map(|(_, l)| *l).collect();
  126|         self.entries
  127|             .insert(key, result.iter().map(|l| l.id).collect());
  128|         result
  129|     }
  130| }

    1| //! Per-frame indexed-surface pipeline.
    2| //!
    3| //! The submission order is deliberately visible in [`render_frame`]:
    4| //!
    5| //! 1. clear the target and establish fixed-function state;
    6| //! 2. collect chunks accepted by the optional visibility optimization;
    7| //! 3. select fixture and dynamic lights;
    8| //! 4. optionally render the hero-light shadow map;
    9| //! 5. bind uniforms that are constant for the frame;
   10| //! 6. bind and draw each visible mesh.
   11| //!
   12| //! Each optional branch is labeled with its `rt_*` switch. Disabling an
   13| //! optimization keeps the same pipeline and selects its reference path.
   14|

  115|         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, Gl::LINEAR as i32);

  121|     fn draw(&mut self, frame: &FrameParams, _chunks: &[ChunkDraw]) {
  122|         let toggles = crate::get_render_toggles();
  123| 
  124|         // OPTIMIZATION (rt_timer): asynchronous timing never waits for the
  125|         // GPU. Disabling it prevents new queries while preserving rendering.
  126|         self.timer.poll(&self.gl);
  127|         let timer_started = self.timer.begin(&self.gl, false);
  128| 
  129|         render_frame(self, frame, toggles);
  130|         self.timer.end(&self.gl, timer_started);
  131|     }
  132| }

  134| fn render_frame(renderer: &mut SurfaceRenderer, frame: &FrameParams, toggles: RenderToggles) {
  135|     begin_main_frame(renderer, frame);
  136|     let (mut visible, clustered_lights) =
  137|         prepare_visible_draws(renderer, frame, toggles.distance_cull);
  138|     if renderer
  139|         .scene_lights
  140|         .upload(&renderer.gl, &clustered_lights)
  141|         .is_err()
  142|     {
  143|         for draw in &mut visible {
  144|             draw.lights.count = 0;
  145|             draw.hero_local_index = -1;
  146|         }
  147|     }
  148| 
  149|     let (shadow, shadow_casters, shadow_draw_calls) =
  150|         render_shadow_pass(renderer, frame, toggles.shadow_pass);
  151| 
  152|     bind_frame_uniforms(
  153|         renderer,
  154|         frame,
  155|         &shadow,
  156|         toggles.dither,
  157|         toggles.baked_lighting,
  158|     );
  159|     let (triangles_drawn, main_draw_calls) = draw_visible_meshes(renderer, &visible, &shadow);
  160|     draw_supply_labels(renderer, frame);
  161| 
  162|     renderer.stats = super::SurfaceFrameStats {
  163|         visible_chunks: visible.len(),
  164|         resident_chunks: renderer.meshes.len(),
  165|         draw_calls: shadow_draw_calls + main_draw_calls,
  166|         triangles_drawn,
  167|         shadow_casters,
  168|     };
  169| }

  171| /// Camera-facing product labels over nearby supply pickups. A cutout pass:
  172| /// depth-tested and depth-writing, so it needs no ordering against the
  173| /// opaque world and never x-rays through walls.
  174| fn draw_supply_labels(renderer: &SurfaceRenderer, frame: &FrameParams) {
  175|     use crate::drivers::shaders::supply_labels;
  176| 
  177|     let Some(atlas) = renderer.label_atlas.as_ref() else {
  178|         return;
  179|     };
  180|     if frame.supply_sprites.is_empty() {

  180|     if frame.supply_sprites.is_empty() {
  181|         return;
  182|     }
  183|     let gl = &renderer.gl;
  184|     let uniforms = &renderer.label_uniforms;
  185|     gl.use_program(Some(&renderer.label_program));
  186| 
  187|     let (projection, view) =
  188|         camera_matrices(frame, renderer.width, renderer.height, MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE);
  189|     gl.uniform_matrix4fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.projection.as_ref(), false, &projection);
  190|     gl.uniform_matrix4fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.view.as_ref(), false, &view);
  191| 
  192|     let count = frame.supply_sprites.len().min(supply_labels::MAX_SPRITES);
  193|     let mut sprites = [0.0f32; supply_labels::MAX_SPRITES * 4];
  194|     for (i, sprite) in frame.supply_sprites.iter().take(count).enumerate() {
  195|         sprites[i * 4] = sprite.position[0];
  196|         sprites[i * 4 + 1] = sprite.position[1];
  197|         sprites[i * 4 + 2] = sprite.position[2];
  198|         sprites[i * 4 + 3] = sprite.atlas_row as f32;
  199|     }
  200|     gl.uniform4fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.sprites.as_ref(), &sprites);
  201|     // Cylindrical billboard: turn with the player's yaw, stay upright.
  202|     let right = [frame.yaw.cos(), 0.0, -frame.yaw.sin()];
  203|     gl.uniform3fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.cam_right.as_ref(), &right);
  204|     gl.uniform2f(
  205|         uniforms.half_size.as_ref(),
  206|         supply_labels::HALF_WIDTH,
  207|         supply_labels::HALF_HEIGHT,
  208|     );
  209|     gl.uniform3f(
  210|         uniforms.camera_position.as_ref(),
  211|         frame.camera_pos[0],
  212|         frame.camera_pos[1],
  213|         frame.camera_pos[2],
  214|     );
  215|     let environment = frame.environment;
  216|     gl.uniform3f(
  217|         uniforms.fog_color.as_ref(),
  218|         environment.fog_color[0],
  219|         environment.fog_color[1],
  220|         environment.fog_color[2],
  221|     );
  222|     gl.uniform1f(uniforms.fog_density.as_ref(), environment.fog_density);
  223|     gl.uniform1f(uniforms.fog_start.as_ref(), environment.fog_start);
  224| 
  225|     gl.active_texture(Gl::TEXTURE7);
  226|     gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(atlas));
  227|     gl.uniform1i(uniforms.atlas.as_ref(), 7);
  228| 
  229|     // Both label faces read; the quad expands entirely from gl_VertexID.
  230|     gl.disable(Gl::CULL_FACE);
  231|     gl.bind_vertex_array(None);
  232|     gl.draw_arrays(Gl::TRIANGLES, 0, (count * 6) as i32);
  233|     gl.enable(Gl::CULL_FACE);
  234| }
  235| 
  236| /// Establishes every fixed-function state relied on by either raster pass.
  237| fn begin_main_frame(renderer: &SurfaceRenderer, frame: &FrameParams) {
  238|     let gl = &renderer.gl;
  239|     gl.viewport(0, 0, renderer.width, renderer.height);
  240| 
  241|     // Match unloaded space to the level atmosphere so generated chunk edges
  242|     // disappear into fog rather than exposing the canvas clear color.
  243|     let environment = frame.environment;
  244|     let atmosphere = if environment.outdoor {
  245|         environment.sky_color
  246|     } else {
  247|         environment.fog_color
  248|     };
  249|     let clear = encode_display_color(atmosphere);
  250|     gl.clear_color(clear[0], clear[1], clear[2], 1.0);
  251|     gl.clear_depth(1.0);
  252|     gl.clear(Gl::COLOR_BUFFER_BIT | Gl::DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT);
  253|     gl.enable(Gl::DEPTH_TEST);
  254|     gl.depth_func(Gl::LEQUAL);
  255|     gl.depth_mask(true);
  256|     gl.enable(Gl::CULL_FACE);
  257|     gl.cull_face(Gl::BACK);
  258| }
  259| 
  260| /// OPTIMIZATION (rt_cull): conservative distance and behind-camera sphere
  261| /// rejection. The disabled reference path submits every resident mesh.
  262| fn prepare_visible_draws(
  263|     renderer: &SurfaceRenderer,
  264|     frame: &FrameParams,
  265|     culling_enabled: bool,
  266| ) -> (
  267|     Vec<VisibleDraw>,
  268|     Vec<crate::application::ports::LightSource>,
  269| ) {
  270|     let mut draws = Vec::new();
  271|     let mut clustered = Vec::new();
  272|     let hero_id = frame.active_scene_lights().first().map(|light| light.id);
  273|     let aspect = renderer.width as f32 / (renderer.height.max(1)) as f32;
  274|     let fov_tan = crate::drivers::webgl::fov_tan();
  275|     for (&key, mesh) in &renderer.meshes {
  276|         let visible = {
  277|             if !culling_enabled {
  278|                 true
  279|             } else {
  280|                 let (center, radius) = chunk_bounding_sphere(mesh.origin, mesh.bounds_max);
  281|                 sphere_visible(center, radius, frame, MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE).is_some()
  282|                     && frustum_side_planes_visible(center, radius, frame, fov_tan, aspect)
  283|             }
  284|         };
  285|         if !visible {
  286|             continue;
  287|         }
  288|         let bounds_max = [
  289|             mesh.origin[0] + mesh.bounds_max[0],
  290|             mesh.origin[1] + mesh.bounds_max[1],
  291|             mesh.origin[2] + mesh.bounds_max[2],
  292|         ];
  293|         let lights = append_lights_reaching_bounds(
  294|             frame.active_scene_lights(),
  295|             mesh.origin,
  296|             bounds_max,
  297|             &mut clustered,
  298|         );
  299|         let hero_local_index =
  300|             if lights.count > 0 && hero_id == Some(clustered[lights.first as usize].id) {
  301|                 0
  302|             } else {
  303|                 -1
  304|             };
  305|         draws.push(VisibleDraw {
  306|             key,
  307|             lights,
  308|             hero_local_index,
  309|         });
  310|     }
  311|     (draws, clustered)
  312| }
  313| 
  314| /// FEATURE (rt_shadows): renders every resident greedy mesh into the selected
  315| /// fixture's top-down depth map. Camera culling must not remove an off-screen
  316| /// caster whose shadow lands on a visible receiver. With the feature
  317| /// disabled, the returned state makes the main shader skip shadow sampling.
  318| fn render_shadow_pass(
  319|     renderer: &SurfaceRenderer,
  320|     frame: &FrameParams,
  321|     enabled: bool,
  322| ) -> (ShadowState, u32, u32) {
  323|     let Some(hero) = frame.active_scene_lights().first() else {
  324|         return (ShadowState::default(), 0, 0);
  325|     };
  326|     if !enabled {
  327|         return (ShadowState::default(), 0, 0);
  328|     }
  329| 
  330|     let range = hero.radius;
  331|     let emitter_half_diagonal =
  332|         (hero.half_size[0] * hero.half_size[0] + hero.half_size[1] * hero.half_size[1]).sqrt();
  333|     let ortho_half = range + emitter_half_diagonal;
  334|     let projection = ortho_matrix(
  335|         -ortho_half,
  336|         ortho_half,
  337|         -ortho_half,
  338|         ortho_half,
  339|         0.1,
  340|         range + emitter_half_diagonal,
  341|     );
  342|     let view = look_at_matrix_down(hero.position);
  343|     let light_view_projection = multiply_matrices(&projection, &view);
  344| 
  345|     let gl = &renderer.gl;
  346|     gl.bind_framebuffer(Gl::FRAMEBUFFER, Some(&renderer.shadow.fbo));
  347|     gl.viewport(0, 0, renderer.shadow.size, renderer.shadow.size);
  348|     gl.color_mask(false, false, false, false);
  349|     gl.clear_depth(1.0);
  350|     gl.clear(Gl::DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT);
  351|     gl.use_program(Some(&renderer.shadow_program));
  352|     gl.uniform_matrix4fv_with_f32_array(
  353|         renderer.shadow_uniforms.light_view_proj.as_ref(),
  354|         false,
  355|         &light_view_projection,
  356|     );
  357| 
  358|     let hero_min_x = hero.position[0] - ortho_half;
  359|     let hero_max_x = hero.position[0] + ortho_half;
  360|     let hero_min_z = hero.position[2] - ortho_half;
  361|     let hero_max_z = hero.position[2] + ortho_half;
  362|     let hero_min_y = hero.position[1] - range;
  363|     let hero_max_y = hero.position[1] + 2.0;
  364| 
  365|     let mut casters_count = 0u32;
  366|     let mut draw_calls = 0u32;
  367| 
  368|     for mesh in renderer.meshes.values() {
  369|         let chunk_max_x = mesh.origin[0] + mesh.bounds_max[0];
  370|         let chunk_max_y = mesh.origin[1] + mesh.bounds_max[1];
  371|         let chunk_max_z = mesh.origin[2] + mesh.bounds_max[2];
  372| 
  373|         // Footprint AABB intersection test for hero-light caster culling
  374|         if chunk_max_x < hero_min_x
  375|             || mesh.origin[0] > hero_max_x
  376|             || chunk_max_z < hero_min_z
  377|             || mesh.origin[2] > hero_max_z
  378|             || chunk_max_y < hero_min_y
  379|             || mesh.origin[1] > hero_max_y
  380|         {
  381|             continue;
  382|         }
  383| 
  384|         casters_count += 1;
  385|         draw_calls += 1;
  386| 
  387|         gl.uniform3f(
  388|             renderer.shadow_uniforms.chunk_origin.as_ref(),
  389|             mesh.origin[0],
  390|             mesh.origin[1],
  391|             mesh.origin[2],
  392|         );
  393|         gl.bind_vertex_array(Some(&mesh.vao));
  394|         gl.draw_elements_with_i32(Gl::TRIANGLES, mesh.index_count, Gl::UNSIGNED_INT, 0);
  395|     }
  396| 
  397|     // Restore the default target state required by the already-cleared main
  398|     // pass. Depth/cull state is shared and remains intentionally unchanged.
  399|     gl.bind_framebuffer(Gl::FRAMEBUFFER, None);
  400|     gl.viewport(0, 0, renderer.width, renderer.height);
  401|     gl.color_mask(true, true, true, true);
  402| 
  403|     (
  404|         ShadowState {
  405|             light_index: 0,
  406|             light_view_projection,
  407|         },
  408|         casters_count,
  409|         draw_calls,
  410|     )
  411| }
  412| 
  413| /// Binds state shared by every visible mesh exactly once per frame.
  414| fn bind_frame_uniforms(
  415|     renderer: &SurfaceRenderer,
  416|     frame: &FrameParams,
  417|     shadow: &ShadowState,
  418|     dither_enabled: bool,
  419|     baked_lighting_enabled: bool,
  420| ) {

Confirmed surface_webgl/draw.rs findings:
- `prepare_visible_draws` (262-312): per visible mesh, `append_lights_reaching_bounds` O(L) → O(V×L) per frame. Note `frame.active_scene_lights()` — from prior analysis, the frame's scene_lights is capped at MAX_ANALYTIC_SCENE_LIGHTS_PER_FRAME=48? Wait — but the WebGL2 shaders use MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS=16. Let me check: `lights.rs select_lights` sorts and truncates to 16. But `frame.active_scene_lights()` — that's the frame's full list (capped at 48 by engine). Hmm, actually the engine truncates scene_lights to 48 for the renderer. Then `lights.rs::select_lights` re-sorts/truncates to 16 for uniforms. But `append_lights_reaching_bounds` uses `frame.active_scene_lights()` — the full 48. So O(V × 48) per frame — bounded, but each light does a box-distance test. With V=25 visible chunks → 1200 predicate evaluations/frame. Not huge, but could be cached per-chunk (chunk bounds are static; lights change rarely). Medium finding.

- `hero_local_index` — checks only `clustered[lights.first]` == hero_id; if hero is the 2nd light in the cluster, returns -1, so hero shadow would not be sampled... wait actually it checks if the FIRST clustered light is the hero. If the hero light isn't first, hero_local_index=-1, meaning no shadow sampling for the hero light. Hmm, but is the hero light guaranteed to be first? frame.active_scene_lights() is sorted by importance (nearest first), and append_lights_reaching_bounds preserves order (filter), so if hero is within bounds of the chunk, it stays in order relative to others. But it's not necessarily the FIRST — e.g., a brighter light... Actually select_scene_lights sorts by importance = intensity*area/(dist²+area). The hero light is the most important overall (first of frame list). But when clustered per chunk, the first in the cluster is the most important light that reaches the chunk... The hero is the first in the frame list, so among the lights reaching the chunk, the hero has the highest importance rank overall, but importance depends on the camera distance — a closer light could outrank the hero for this chunk? No: importance is computed from camera position, the same for all chunks. So the ordering in `clustered` is the same as frame list order (filter preserves). So hero is first in cluster if it reaches the chunk. But `hero_local_index` returns 0 (i.e., "the hero light is at local index 0") or -1. Since the first clustered light == hero iff hero reaches, this is correct-ish: index 0. But the shadow shader probably looks up light by index... `uShadowedLightIndex`? In fragment interface: `uniform int uShadowedLightIndex;` Hmm, in compose_surface_lighting they pass the hero local index. This matters for correctness but it's OK if ordering is preserved.

But wait — there's a subtle bug: `append_lights_reaching_bounds` is called per mesh with the SAME frame list, so the clustered list is ordered by frame order. hero_local_index = 0 if clustered[first] == hero. But what if the hero light is not first in the frame list? `frame.active_scene_lights().first()` — the hero is defined as the first (most important). OK consistent.

    1| //! Per-frame light selection — one implementation for the surface and
    2| //! splat renderers, which previously carried diverging copies.
    3| //!
    4| //! Inputs: fixture lights from every visible chunk (deduplicated by id —
    5| //! a fixture near a chunk border is listed by several chunks) plus the
    6| //! frame's dynamic lights (dropped flares). The most important lights fill
    7| //! the bounded shader slots; the most important *fixture* light also
    8| //! wins the hero shadow map (a flare at ankle height would collapse the
    9| //! top-down shadow frustum, so dynamic lights never own it).
   10| //!
   11| //! Importance = radius * sqrt(intensity) / (distance² + 0.1): bigger and
   12| //! brighter lights reach farther, nearby lights dominate.
   13| 
   14| use crate::application::ports::{FrameParams, LightSource, MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS};
   15| 
   16| /// Maximum shader light slots (matches the GLSL uniform arrays).
   17| pub const MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS: usize = crate::application::ports::MAX_SCENE_LIGHTS;
   18| 
   19| /// The frame's selected lights, packed for `uniform[1i|3fv|4fv]` upload.
   20| pub struct SelectedLights {
   21|     pub count: usize,
   22|     pub positions: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
   23|     pub colors: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
   24|     /// Per light: radius, intensity, half_size.x, half_size.y.
   25|     pub params: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 4],
   26|     pub kinds: [i32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS],
   27|     /// Slot index of the shadow-casting hero light, or -1.
   28|     pub hero_slot: i32,
   29|     /// Hero light's position/radius (meaningful when `hero_slot >= 0`).
   30|     pub hero_position: [f32; 3],
   31|     pub hero_radius: f32,
   32| }
   33| 
   34| /// Wraps the frame's dynamic lights as fixture-shaped sources with sentinel
   35| /// ids in the top range, so one selection pass handles both kinds.
   36| pub fn dynamic_light_sources(frame: &FrameParams) -> Vec<LightSource> {
   37|     frame
   38|         .active_dynamic_lights()
   39|         .iter()
   40|         .enumerate()
   41|         .map(|(i, d)| LightSource {
   42|             id: u64::MAX - i as u64,
   43|             position: d.position,
   44|             half_size: [0.25, 0.25],
   45|             color: d.color,
   46|             radius: d.radius,
   47|             intensity: d.intensity,
   48|             kind: crate::application::ports::LightKind::Point,
   49|             flicker_mode: 0,
   50|             enabled: true,
   51|         })
   52|         .collect()
   53| }
   54| 
   55| fn is_dynamic(light: &LightSource) -> bool {
   56|     light.id > u64::MAX - 16
   57| }
   58| 
   59| /// Selects and packs the frame's lights. `fixtures` should already be
   60| /// deduplicated by id (pass a `HashMap`'s values); `dynamic` comes from
   61| /// [`dynamic_light_sources`].
   62| pub fn select_lights<'a>(
   63|     fixtures: impl Iterator<Item = &'a LightSource>,
   64|     dynamic: &'a [LightSource],
   65|     frame: &FrameParams,
   66| ) -> SelectedLights {
   67|     let mut ranked: Vec<(&LightSource, f32)> = fixtures
   68|         .chain(dynamic.iter())
   69|         .map(|light| {
   70|             let dx = light.position[0] - frame.camera_pos[0];
   71|             let dy = light.position[1] - frame.camera_pos[1];
   72|             let dz = light.position[2] - frame.camera_pos[2];
   73|             let dist2 = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz;
   74|             (light, light.radius * light.intensity.sqrt() / (dist2 + 0.1))
   75|         })
   76|         .collect();
   77|     ranked.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
   78| 
   79|     let count = ranked.len().min(MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS);
   80|     let mut selected = SelectedLights {
   81|         count,
   82|         positions: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
   83|         colors: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
   84|         params: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 4],
   85|         kinds: [0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS],
   86|         hero_slot: -1,
   87|         hero_position: [0.0; 3],
   88|         hero_radius: 0.0,
   89|     };
   90|     for (i, (light, _)) in ranked[..count].iter().enumerate() {
   91|         selected.positions[i * 3..i * 3 + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.position);
   92|         selected.colors[i * 3..i * 3 + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.color);
   93|         selected.params[i * 4] = light.radius;
   94|         selected.params[i * 4 + 1] = light.intensity;
   95|         selected.params[i * 4 + 2] = light.half_size[0];
   96|         selected.params[i * 4 + 3] = light.half_size[1];
   97|         selected.kinds[i] = light.kind as i32;
   98|     }
   99| 
  100|     // Hero shadow: the strongest *fixture* light in the selected slots.
  101|     if let Some(slot) = ranked[..count].iter().position(|(l, _)| !is_dynamic(l)) {
  102|         selected.hero_slot = slot as i32;
  103|         selected.hero_position = ranked[slot].0.position;
  104|         selected.hero_radius = ranked[slot].0.radius;
  105|     }
  106|     selected
  107| }
  108| 
  109| /// Flare-core uniforms (`uCoreCount`/`uCores`/`uCoreColors`), independent of
  110| /// the merged light slots so a flare culled from the four shading lights
  111| /// still shows its ember.
  112| pub struct FlareCores {
  113|     pub count: i32,
  114|     /// xyz = position, w = pre-flickered intensity.
  115|     pub pos_intensity: [f32; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS * 4],
  116|     pub colors: [f32; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS * 3],
  117| }
  118| 
  119| pub fn flare_cores(frame: &FrameParams) -> FlareCores {
  120|     let cores = frame.active_dynamic_lights();
  121|     let mut packed = FlareCores {
  122|         count: cores.len() as i32,
  123|         pos_intensity: [0.0; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS * 4],
  124|         colors: [0.0; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS * 3],
  125|     };
  126|     for (i, c) in cores.iter().enumerate() {
  127|         packed.pos_intensity[i * 4..i * 4 + 3].copy_from_slice(&c.position);
  128|         packed.pos_intensity[i * 4 + 3] = c.intensity;
  129|         packed.colors[i * 3..i * 3 + 3].copy_from_slice(&c.color);
  130|     }
  131|     packed
  132| }
    1| //! Asynchronous GPU frame timing via `EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2`.
    2| //!
    3| //! One query is in flight at a time; results are polled (never blocked on)
    4| //! at the top of the next frames, so the HUD's GPU number lags a frame or
    5| //! two but the pipeline never stalls. Toggleable (`RenderToggles::gpu_timer`)
    6| //! because some drivers serialize on timer queries.
    7| 
    8| use js_sys::Object;
    9| use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlQuery};
   10| 
   11| /// Extension constants absent from WebGL2 core.
   12| const TIME_ELAPSED_EXT: u32 = 0x88BF;
   13| const GPU_DISJOINT_EXT: u32 = 0x8FBB;
   14| 
   15| pub struct GpuFrameTimer {
   16|     extension: Option<Object>,
   17|     pending: Option<WebGlQuery>,
   18|     last_ms: Option<f32>,
   19| }
   20| 
   21| impl GpuFrameTimer {
   22|     /// Probes for the extension; a `None` extension makes every method a
   23|     /// no-op so callers never branch on support.
   24|     pub fn new(gl: &Gl) -> Self {
   25|         Self {
   26|             extension: gl
   27|                 .get_extension("EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2")
   28|                 .ok()
   29|                 .flatten(),
   30|             pending: None,
   31|             last_ms: None,
   32|         }
   33|     }
   34| 
   35|     pub fn last_ms(&self) -> Option<f32> {
   36|         self.last_ms
   37|     }
   38| 
   39|     /// Collects a finished query, if any. Disjoint intervals (GPU clock
   40|     /// disturbance) discard the sample.
   41|     pub fn poll(&mut self, gl: &Gl) {
   42|         let Some(query) = self.pending.as_ref() else {
   43|             return;
   44|         };
   45|         let available = gl
   46|             .get_query_parameter(query, Gl::QUERY_RESULT_AVAILABLE)
   47|             .as_bool()
   48|             .unwrap_or(false);
   49|         let disjoint = self.extension.is_some()
   50|             && gl
   51|                 .get_parameter(GPU_DISJOINT_EXT)
   52|                 .ok()
   53|                 .and_then(|value| value.as_bool())
   54|                 .unwrap_or(false);
   55|         if !available && !disjoint {
   56|             return;
   57|         }
   58|         let query = self.pending.take().expect("pending timer exists");
   59|         if available && !disjoint {
   60|             self.last_ms = gl
   61|                 .get_query_parameter(&query, Gl::QUERY_RESULT)
   62|                 .as_f64()
   63|                 .map(|nanos| (nanos as f32) * 1.0e-6);
   64|         }
   65|         gl.delete_query(Some(&query));
   66|     }
   67| 
   68|     /// Starts timing this frame. Returns whether a query was issued (pass
   69|     /// it to [`Self::end`]). `enabled` comes from the toggle switchboard.
   70|     pub fn begin(&mut self, gl: &Gl, enabled: bool) -> bool {
   71|         if !enabled {
   72|             // The HUD must not present an old sample as current after timing
   73|             // has been switched off. An in-flight query is still collected
   74|             // by `poll` and then discarded from view on this frame.
   75|             self.last_ms = None;
   76|             return false;
   77|         }
   78|         if self.extension.is_none() || self.pending.is_some() {
   79|             return false;
   80|         }
   81|         let Some(query) = gl.create_query() else {
   82|             return false;
   83|         };
   84|         gl.begin_query(TIME_ELAPSED_EXT, &query);
   85|         self.pending = Some(query);
   86|         true
   87|     }
   88| 
   89|     pub fn end(&self, gl: &Gl, started: bool) {
   90|         if started {
   91|             gl.end_query(TIME_ELAPSED_EXT);
   92|         }
   93|     }
   94| }

Confirmed:
- `lights.rs::select_lights` — O(N log N) per frame over all fixture+dynamic lights (up to 48 fixtures + 4 dynamic); sorts then truncates to 16 slots. Fine, bounded.
- `timer.rs` — begin() supports an `enabled` flag but all 4 drivers hardcode `false`. GPU timing dead. Also note: `begin` sets `last_ms = None` when disabled — and `poll` never runs because pending is None... anyway. Medium finding: telemetry dead.

  117|     pub fn upload(&mut self, device: &wgpu::Device, chunks: &[SurfaceChunk<'_>]) {
  118|         for &chunk in chunks {
  119|             self.chunks.remove(&chunk.key);
  120|             if chunk.mesh.vertices.is_empty() || chunk.mesh.indices.is_empty() {
  121|                 continue;
  122|             }
  123|             let vertices: Vec<_> = chunk
  124|                 .mesh
  125|                 .vertices
  126|                 .iter()
  127|                 .map(GpuPackedSurfaceVertex::from)
  128|                 .collect();
  129|             let vertex_buffer = device.create_buffer_init(&wgpu::util::BufferInitDescriptor {
  130|                 label: Some("webgpu.surface.vertices"),
  131|                 contents: bytemuck::cast_slice(&vertices),
  132|                 usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::STORAGE,
  133|             });
  134|             let index_buffer = device.create_buffer_init(&wgpu::util::BufferInitDescriptor {
  135|                 label: Some("webgpu.surface.indices"),
  136|                 contents: bytemuck::cast_slice(&chunk.mesh.indices),
  137|                 usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::INDEX,
  138|             });
  139|             let uniform_buffer = device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
  140|                 label: Some("webgpu.surface.chunk-uniforms"),
  141|                 size: size_of::<GpuChunkUniforms>() as u64,
  142|                 usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::UNIFORM | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
  143|                 mapped_at_creation: false,
  144|             });
  145|             let bind_group = device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
  146|                 label: Some("webgpu.surface.chunk-bind-group"),
  147|                 layout: &self.chunk_layout,
  148|                 entries: &[
  149|                     wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
  150|                         binding: 0,
  151|                         resource: uniform_buffer.as_entire_binding(),
  152|                     },
  153|                     wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
  154|                         binding: 1,
  155|                         resource: vertex_buffer.as_entire_binding(),
  156|                     },
  157|                 ],
  158|             });
  159|             self.chunks.insert(
  160|                 chunk.key,
  161|                 SurfaceChunkGpu {
  162|                     vertices: vertex_buffer,
  163|                     indices: index_buffer,
  164|                     uniforms: uniform_buffer,
  165|                     bind_group,
  166|                     index_count: chunk.mesh.indices.len().min(u32::MAX as usize) as u32,
  167|                     origin: chunk.origin,
  168|                     bounds_max: chunk.mesh.bounds.max,
  169|                     voxel_size: chunk.mesh.voxel_scale,
  170|                 },
  171|             );
  172|         }
  173|     }
