  241|                 view: depth,
  242|                 depth_ops: Some(wgpu::Operations {
  243|                     load: wgpu::LoadOp::Clear(1.0),
  244|                     store: wgpu::StoreOp::Store,
  245|                 }),
  246|                 stencil_ops: None,
  247|             }),
  248|             ..Default::default()
  249|         });
  250|         pass.set_pipeline(&self.pipeline);
  251|         pass.set_bind_group(0, frame_resources.bind_group(), &[]);
  252|         pass.set_bind_group(2, self.shadow.receiver_bind_group(), &[]);
  253|         for chunk in self.chunks.values() {
  254|             if toggles.distance_cull {
  255|                 let (center, radius) = bounds_sphere(chunk.origin, chunk.bounds_max);
  256|                 if !sphere_is_visible(center, radius, frame, self.max_draw_distance)
  257|                     || !frustum_side_planes_visible(center, radius, frame, fov_tan, aspect)
  258|                 {
  259|                     continue;
  260|                 }
  261|             }
  262|             // Keep the storage buffer alive and make its ownership explicit,
  263|             // even though vertex pulling references it through the bind group.
  264|             let _keep_alive = &chunk.vertices;
  265|             pass.set_bind_group(1, &chunk.bind_group, &[]);
  266|             pass.set_index_buffer(chunk.indices.slice(..), wgpu::IndexFormat::Uint32);
  267|             pass.draw_indexed(0..chunk.index_count, 0, 0..1);
  268|         }
  269|     }
  270| 
  271|     /// Every resident indexed surface casts. Camera visibility cannot reject
  272|     /// an off-screen object whose shadow reaches an on-screen receiver.
  273|     fn draw_shadow_pass(&self, encoder: &mut wgpu::CommandEncoder) {
  274|         let mut pass = encoder.begin_render_pass(&wgpu::RenderPassDescriptor {
  275|             label: Some("webgpu.surface.hero-shadow-pass"),
  276|             color_attachments: &[],
  277|             depth_stencil_attachment: Some(wgpu::RenderPassDepthStencilAttachment {
  278|                 view: self.shadow.view(),
  279|                 depth_ops: Some(wgpu::Operations {
  280|                     load: wgpu::LoadOp::Clear(1.0),
  281|                     store: wgpu::StoreOp::Store,
  282|                 }),
  283|                 stencil_ops: None,
  284|             }),
  285|             ..Default::default()
  286|         });

  288|         pass.set_bind_group(0, self.shadow.caster_bind_group(), &[]);
  289|         for chunk in self.chunks.values() {

  295|     }

Confirmed WebGPU SurfacePipeline:
- `draw: [0, light_count, 0, 0]` at line 208 — every chunk's uniform says light_first=0, light_count=ALL frame lights. No clustering. Every fragment of every chunk loops over all lights.
- Also interesting: **per-frame `queue.write_buffer` for EVERY chunk uniform** (line 210) — one write per resident chunk per frame, plus one bind group per chunk. That's fine for ~25 chunks.
- Shadow pass draws ALL resident chunks (no AABB culling vs hero light range, unlike the WebGL2 version which has the AABB test at surface_webgl/draw.rs:368-382). Actually WebGPU `draw_shadow_pass` (273-295) has NO culling at all. WebGL2 has AABB culling. Minor perf finding: WebGPU shadow pass renders every resident mesh regardless of hero-light footprint.    22| /// The high byte of a packed material visual stores authored emission over
   23| /// the current domain range of `0..=10`. The low 24 bits remain the canonical
   24| /// `0xRRGGBB` palette entry, so raster shaders never maintain a second palette.
   25| const PACKED_EMISSION_UNITS_PER_RADIANCE: f32 = u8::MAX as f32 / 10.0;
   26| 
   27| fn pack_material_visual(material: u8) -> u32 {
   28|     let color = material_visual(material).color & 0x00ff_ffff;
   29|     let emission = material_emission_strength(material).unwrap_or_default();
   30|     let quantized_emission = (emission * PACKED_EMISSION_UNITS_PER_RADIANCE)
   31|         .round()
   32|         .clamp(0.0, f32::from(u8::MAX)) as u32;
   33|     color | (quantized_emission << 24)
   34| }

  528| 
  529| fn finite_segment_visible(
  530|     receiver_world: vec3<f32>,
  531|     receiver_normal: vec3<f32>,
  532|     receiver_voxel_size: f32,
  533|     endpoint_world: vec3<f32>,
  534| ) -> bool {
  535|     let endpoint_bias = direct_visibility_bias(receiver_voxel_size);
  536|     let biased_origin = receiver_world + receiver_normal * endpoint_bias;
  537|     let segment = endpoint_world - biased_origin;
  538|     let endpoint_distance = length(segment);
  539|     if endpoint_distance <= endpoint_bias * 2.0 {
  540|         return true;
  541|     }
  542|     let ray_direction = segment / endpoint_distance;
  543|     // Do not classify the light fixture's own endpoint as an occluder.
  544|     let maximum_distance = endpoint_distance - endpoint_bias;
  545|     var remaining_steps = DIRECT_VISIBILITY_TRACE_BUDGET;
  546|     let chunk_count = min(ray_scene.chunk_count, 25u);
  547| 
  548|     for (var index = 0u; index < chunk_count; index += 1u) {
  549|         if remaining_steps == 0u {
  550|             return false;
  551|         }
  552|         let chunk = ray_chunks[index];
  553|         let local_origin = biased_origin - chunk.origin_world_size.xyz;
  554|         let slab = box_intersection(
  555|             local_origin,
  556|             ray_direction,
  557|             vec3<f32>(0.0),
  558|             vec3<f32>(chunk.origin_world_size.w)
  559|         );
  560|         let finite_exit = min(slab.exit, maximum_distance);
  561|         if !slab.hit || finite_exit <= slab.entry {
  562|             continue;
  563|         }
  564|         let interval = BoxHit(true, slab.entry, finite_exit, slab.normal);
  565|         let trace = trace_visibility_chunk_skipping_empty_leaves(
  566|             local_origin,
  567|             ray_direction,
  568|             chunk,
  569|             interval,
  570|             remaining_steps
  571|         );
  572|         remaining_steps -= min(trace.steps, remaining_steps);
  573|         if trace.blocked {
  574|             return false;
  575|         }
  576|     }
  577|     return true;
  578| }
  579| 
  580| fn has_positive_rgb(value: vec3<f32>) -> bool {
  581|     return max(value.x, max(value.y, value.z)) > 0.0;
  582| }
  583| 
  584| fn rectangle_visibility_sample_count() -> u32 {
  585|     return select(1u, 4u, ray_scene._reserved.x == 4u);
  586| }
  587| 
  588| fn evaluate_visible_scene_light(
  589|     world: vec3<f32>,
  590|     normal: vec3<f32>,
  591|     receiver_voxel_size: f32,
  592|     light: GpuLight,
  593| ) -> vec3<f32> {
  594|     let kind = u32(max(light.half_size_kind.z, 0.0) + 0.5);
  595|     if kind == LIGHT_POINT {
  596|         let endpoint = light.position_radius.xyz;
  597|         let unoccluded = point_light_sample_irradiance(world, normal, light, endpoint);
  598|         if !has_positive_rgb(unoccluded) {
  599|             return vec3<f32>(0.0);
  600|         }
  601|         if finite_segment_visible(world, normal, receiver_voxel_size, endpoint) {
  602|             return unoccluded;
  603|         }
  604|         return vec3<f32>(0.0);
  605|     }
  606| 
  607|     if rectangle_visibility_sample_count() == 4u {
  608|         var visible_integral = 0.0;
  609|         for (var sample_index = 0u; sample_index < 4u; sample_index += 1u) {
  610|             let endpoint = rectangle_gauss_sample_position(light, sample_index);
  611|             let sample_weight = rectangle_light_sample_weight(
  612|                 world,
  613|                 normal,
  614|                 light,
  615|                 kind,
  616|                 endpoint
  617|             );
  618|             let sample_irradiance = rectangle_light_irradiance_from_integral(
  619|                 light,
  620|                 sample_weight
  621|             );
  622|             if !has_positive_rgb(sample_irradiance) {
  623|                 continue;
  624|             }
  625|             if finite_segment_visible(world, normal, receiver_voxel_size, endpoint) {
  626|                 visible_integral += sample_weight;
  627|             }
  628|         }
  629|         return rectangle_light_irradiance_from_integral(light, visible_integral);
  630|     }
  631| 
  632|     // Low quality retains the existing four-point unoccluded quadrature and
  633|     // gates its integral with one finite segment to the rectangle center.
  634|     let unoccluded = evaluate_rectangle_light(world, normal, light, kind);
  635|     if !has_positive_rgb(unoccluded) {
  636|         return vec3<f32>(0.0);
  637|     }
  638|     if finite_segment_visible(
  639|         world,
  640|         normal,
  641|         receiver_voxel_size,
  642|         light.position_radius.xyz
  643|     ) {
  644|         return unoccluded;
  645|     }
  646|     return vec3<f32>(0.0);
  647| }
  648| 
  649| fn raymarch_analytic_direct(
  650|     world: vec3<f32>,
  651|     normal: vec3<f32>,
  652|     receiver_voxel_size: f32,
  653| ) -> vec3<f32> {
  654|     var analytic_direct = vec3<f32>(0.0);
  655|     for (var index = 0u; index < frame.render_options.x; index += 1u) {
  656|         let light = lights[index];
  657|         if light.half_size_kind.w < 0.5 {
  658|             continue;
  659|         }
  660|         analytic_direct += evaluate_visible_scene_light(
  661|             world,
  662|             normal,
  663|             receiver_voxel_size,
  664|             light
  665|         );
  666|     }
  667|     return analytic_direct;
  668| }
  669| 
  670| fn camera_ray(pixel: vec2<f32>) -> vec3<f32> {
  671|     let viewport = max(frame.viewport_fov_start.xy, vec2<f32>(1.0));
  672|     let normalized = pixel / viewport;
  673|     let aspect = viewport.x / viewport.y;
  674|     let screen = vec2<f32>(
  675|         (normalized.x * 2.0 - 1.0) * aspect,
  676|         1.0 - normalized.y * 2.0
  677|     ) * frame.viewport_fov_start.z;
  678|     return normalize(
  679|         frame.camera_forward.xyz
  680|         + frame.camera_right.xyz * screen.x
  681|         + frame.camera_up.xyz * screen.y
  682|     );
  683| }
  684| 
  685| @fragment
  686| fn raymarch_fragment(@builtin(position) pixel: vec4<f32>) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
  687|     let direction = camera_ray(pixel.xy);
  688|     var nearest = VoxelHit(false, 1e30, vec3<f32>(0.0), 0u, 0u, 0u, 0.0);
  689|     var nearest_source_index = 0xffffffffu;
  690|     let chunk_count = min(ray_scene.chunk_count, 25u);
  691|     for (var index = 0u; index < chunk_count; index += 1u) {
  692|         let chunk = ray_chunks[index];
  693|         let local_origin = frame.camera_position.xyz - chunk.origin_world_size.xyz;
  694|         let interval = box_intersection(
  695|             local_origin,
  696|             direction,
  697|             vec3<f32>(0.0),
  698|             vec3<f32>(chunk.origin_world_size.w)
  699|         );
  700|         if !interval.hit || interval.entry > nearest.distance { continue; }

   23| impl BrowserGpuContext {
   24|     pub async fn new(canvas: &HtmlCanvasElement) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
   25|         let instance = wgpu::Instance::new(wgpu::InstanceDescriptor {
   26|             backends: wgpu::Backends::BROWSER_WEBGPU,
   27|             ..wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::new_without_display_handle()
   28|         });
   29|         let surface = instance
   30|             .create_surface(wgpu::SurfaceTarget::Canvas(canvas.clone()))
   31|             .map_err(js_error)?;
   32|         // Browser WebGPU does not expose wgpu's native forced-fallback flag.
   33|         // Make one standards-based request and let backend selection recover
   34|         // to WebGL when the browser reports no adapter.
   35|         let adapter = instance
   36|             .request_adapter(&wgpu::RequestAdapterOptions {
   37|                 power_preference: wgpu::PowerPreference::None,
   38|                 compatible_surface: Some(&surface),
   39|                 force_fallback_adapter: false,
   40|                 apply_limit_buckets: true,
   41|             })
   42|             .await
   43|             .map_err(|error| js_error(format!("no WebGPU adapter: {error}")))?;
   44|         let adapter_info = adapter.get_info();
   45|         // Never request more than the adapter reports: desktop-default
   46|         // limits make `requestDevice` reject outright on mobile GPUs. Any
   47|         // pipeline that truly needs more than the clamped budget fails with
   48|         // a specific validation error instead.
   49|         let required_limits = wgpu::Limits::default().or_worse_values_from(&adapter.limits());
   50|         let (device, queue) = adapter
   51|             .request_device(&wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {
   52|                 label: Some("vackrooms-webgpu-device"),
   53|                 required_features: wgpu::Features::empty(),
   54|                 required_limits,
   55|                 experimental_features: wgpu::ExperimentalFeatures::disabled(),
   56|                 memory_hints: wgpu::MemoryHints::MemoryUsage,
   57|                 trace: wgpu::Trace::Off,
   58|             })
   59|             .await
   60|             .map_err(js_error)?;
   61|         let device_lost = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
   62|         device.set_device_lost_callback({
   63|             let device_lost = Arc::clone(&device_lost);
   64|             move |reason, message| {
   65|                 device_lost.store(true, Ordering::Release);
   66|                 web_sys::console::error_1(
   67|                     &format!("WebGPU device lost ({reason:?}): {message}").into(),
   68|                 );
   69|             }
   70|         });
   71|         device.on_uncaptured_error(Arc::new(|error| {
   72|             web_sys::console::error_1(&format!("Uncaptured WebGPU error: {error}").into());
   73|         }));
   74| 
   75|         let capabilities = surface.get_capabilities(&adapter);
   76|         let format = capabilities
   77|             .formats
   78|             .iter()
   79|             .copied()
   80|             .find(|format| !format.is_srgb())
   81|             .ok_or_else(|| {
   82|                 JsValue::from_str(
   83|                     "WebGPU surface exposes no linear color format; Vackrooms encodes display color in WGSL",
   84|                 )
   85|             })?;
   86|         let present_mode = capabilities
   87|             .present_modes
   88|             .iter()
   89|             .copied()
   90|             .find(|mode| *mode == wgpu::PresentMode::AutoVsync)
   91|             .or_else(|| capabilities.present_modes.first().copied())
   92|             .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("WebGPU surface exposes no present modes"))?;
   93|         let config = wgpu::SurfaceConfiguration {
   94|             usage: wgpu::TextureUsages::RENDER_ATTACHMENT,
   95|             format,
   96|             color_space: wgpu::SurfaceColorSpace::Auto,
   97|             width: canvas.width().max(1),
   98|             height: canvas.height().max(1),
   99|             desired_maximum_frame_latency: 2,
  100|             present_mode,
  101|             alpha_mode: wgpu::CompositeAlphaMode::Auto,
  102|             view_formats: vec![],
  103|         };
  104|         surface.configure(&device, &config);
  105| 
  106|         Ok(Self {
  107|             _instance: instance,
  108|             surface,
  109|             adapter_info,
  110|             device,
  111|             queue,
  112|             config,
  113|             device_lost,
  114|         })

   72|     pub fn write(
   73|         &mut self,
   74|         device: &wgpu::Device,
   75|         queue: &wgpu::Queue,
   76|         frame: &GpuFrameUniforms,
   77|         lights: &[GpuLight],
   78|     ) {
   79|         if lights.len().max(1) > self.light_capacity {
   80|             self.light_capacity = lights.len().max(1).next_power_of_two();
   81|             self.light_buffer = create_light_buffer(device, self.light_capacity);
   82|             self.bind_group =
   83|                 create_bind_group(device, &self.layout, &self.frame_buffer, &self.light_buffer);
   84|         }
   85|         queue.write_buffer(&self.frame_buffer, 0, bytemuck::bytes_of(frame));
   86|         if lights.is_empty() {
   87|             queue.write_buffer(
   88|                 &self.light_buffer,
   89|                 0,
   90|                 bytemuck::bytes_of(&GpuLight::zeroed()),
   91|             );
   92|         } else {
   93|             queue.write_buffer(&self.light_buffer, 0, bytemuck::cast_slice(lights));
   94|         }
   95|     }

Good — lib.rs atomics confirmed:
- All statics use Relaxed ordering, single atomic word each — that's fine for single-value flags (each is a self-contained u32/bool). The settings structs are stored as independent atomics — there's a potential torn-snapshot issue: `get_cpu_settings` reads 7 different atomics independently; a JS UI call between reads could leave a mixed snapshot (e.g., scale from new settings, lod from old). In practice these are changed by the settings menu between frames; the mixed snapshot is transient and validated. Low severity.
- `RENDER_TOGGLE_BITS` initial u32::MAX as sentinel; `set_render_toggle` reads-modifies-writes — two JS calls could race but JS is single-threaded; Relaxed fine on wasm32 (single-threaded main thread; workers don't read these).
- Actually on wasm32 with threads disabled (single-threaded), all these atomics are effectively just globals. Fine.

Good — worker entry confirmed. Note: `worker_generate` panics (expect) if called before init, or on invalid artifacts — a panic in wasm aborts the worker → the `fatal` path via error event... actually a Rust panic in wasm32-wasi/unknown aborts, triggering worker `onerror` → `disable_and_drain`. So a malformed message from the main thread could kill a worker — but main thread is the only sender and it always sends valid artifacts. OK.

Also note: worker-side generation is fully synchronous in `worker_generate` — blocks the worker thread (that's the point). The main-thread fallback `LocalChunkSource` — same-thread generation.

worker.js confirmed verbatim. Key concurrency observations for worker.js:

1. **Unbounded promise chain queue** (lines 26, 99-106): `queue = queue.then(...)` grows without any cap. In practice the engine's credit system (max_concurrent_requests = pool_size) bounds outstanding requests, so each worker has at most ~1 queued message... Actually let me think again: is there a path where main thread posts more than 1 message per worker before completion? The engine keeps at most pool_size in-flight; when a worker completes one, the engine issues one more — possibly to the same worker. So queue depth per worker stays ≤ 1... but wait: if the worker finishes quickly and replies, the main thread's in-flight count drops and a new request is issued. Since messages to the same worker can arrive before the worker's previous completion is processed... The worker processes messages serially, so max 1 in the promise chain at a time per worker if the engine only keeps pool_size total in flight. However, `reported_emergency_fallback` path pushes into completed directly — no worker message. Also `request()` can be called multiple times per engine tick (batch of new chunks in range) — the engine's `max_concurrent_requests()` gates total outstanding. But `GenerationWorkerRequests::assign` has NO capacity check — the driver trusts the engine's credit. If the engine ever issues more than pool_size outstanding (e.g., a burst when multiple chunk requests are pending simultaneously: streaming may request up to max_concurrent_requests at once — let me check the engine's streaming to see if requests are issued in batches. In application/streaming.rs — out of my scope, but the prior analysis said engine bounds by max_concurrent_requests. Let me quickly check streaming.rs to confirm credit accounting.

2. **No timeout/hang detection**: if `worker_generate` hangs (infinite loop), the worker never replies, request stays in in_flight forever, and since the engine's credit is pool_size, the whole streaming stalls (all slots could be occupied by hung requests — at most pool_size hung requests → world never completes). There's no watchdog. High-ish (robustness, not perf).

3. **Panic in worker_generate** (e.g., `expect("worker_generate called before worker_init")` at lib.rs:1173, or `expect("invalid artifact bits")` at 1166): a Rust panic in wasm32 aborts the instance and fires the worker's `error` event → error_handler → disable_and_drain → requests failed → engine retries. Good recovery. But the error event may NOT fire in all browsers for wasm aborts... generally it does fire onerror. OK.

4. **`reality: new Uint32Array(message.reality)`** — copies. `worker_generate` receives Vec<u32> — wasm-bindgen converts from the Uint32Array — another copy. Fine.

5. **Fatal reply before init completes**: `processMessage` awaits `ensureWasm()`; the init message is processed first (queue order preserved), so init happens before gen. But: the main thread posts `init` at WorkerChunkSource::new (worker_source.rs:136) and can post `gen` messages before the wasm module finished initializing — handled by the queue chain. Good.

6. **`message.artifacts >>> 0`** etc — fine.

7. One subtle issue: **`queue` promise chain and the transferred buffer** — `bytes.buffer` transferred at line 95; then `reportFailure` may postMessage `message.reality` — but `reality` was NOT transferred, only copied. Fine.

8. **Lost replies on worker termination**: main thread `worker.terminate()` at worker_source.rs:109/128/261 — any replies already in the event queue are dropped; the in-flight ledger for that worker is drained at the same time (disable_and_drain). Consistent.

9. **Race between Fatal reply and error event**: both call disable_and_drain (idempotent) and terminate (idempotent). Fine.

10. **The `ms` field and console.debug per chunk** — console.debug at line 79-81 per chunk could be a perf cost on large streams (dev only? No — console.debug is emitted in production too unless stripped). Minor.

Important discovery! The engine's `issue_requests` credit accounting at engine.rs:923-987:

`max_pending = source.max_concurrent_requests().max(max_loads_per_tick * 2).max(4)` — so `max_pending` can EXCEED `max_concurrent_requests` (pool_size) when `max_loads_per_tick * 2 > pool_size`. E.g., if max_loads_per_tick is 4 (default?), then max_pending ≥ 8 even with 4 workers. This means the driver can receive MORE concurrent requests than the pool has workers — `next_accepting` always returns a worker (any accepting worker), so requests pile into a single worker's in_flight queue and the worker's JS promise chain. The `in_flight` VecDeque is unbounded, and worker.js's `queue` promise chain is unbounded. So messages DO queue per worker beyond 1. That's the "unbounded queue with no backpressure" finding — real, though bounded in practice by pending.len() ≤ max_pending (which is a few dozen). The deeper issue: the driver-side `GenerationWorkerRequests.in_flight` VecDeque grows without bound if the engine ever issues beyond the pool; and there's no per-worker queue cap. Also with `max_pending` up to 2×max_loads_per_tick, and the worker being slow (42ms/chunk), latency for later requests in a worker's queue grows.

Also note `issue_requests` per frame loops over `desired_visual` (all missing chunks in footprint, up to ~100?) calling `self.pending.contains_key` for each → O(F × pending) — application layer, not my scope. But `pending.len()` etc. — out of scope.

Another subtle thing in issue_requests: it's called every frame; for each missing chunk it does `self.store.contains(key) && !self.pending.contains_key(&key)` — O(1) hashmaps. Fine.

Now — the more important driver-side concurrency issue: **when a request is assigned to a worker and that worker has a long queue, the chunk latency is serialized; but there's no rebalancing**. Affinity routing + `next_accepting` (first healthy worker from preferred) means under load, a burst of new chunks hashed to the same worker queue up there even when other workers are idle. E.g., player standing still: the same 4 workers... it's hashed so new chunks spread. When the player moves into a new area, the new chunks hash across workers. But the same worker gets re-requests for its affinity chunks. OK.

More important: **the engine can stall forever on a hung worker** (no watchdog). And **when a worker is terminated, its queued-but-unassigned messages in the JS queue are lost, but the ledger drains them — consistent. However: messages posted but not yet assigned?** No — assign happens before post_message; drain covers all assigned. Between `post_message` success and the reply, if the worker dies with an error event, disable_and_drain retires everything. Consistent. Good design.

One real subtle issue in worker_source.rs: the `request()` fallback path (when next_accepting returns None) pushes `CompletedChunk` directly — but the engine's `pending` map still holds the request key... that's fine, poll_completed returns it and install_completed validates.

Another subtle issue: **request_id** — the driver assigns `request.request_id` from the engine's counter (ChunkRequest). The engine's `install_completed` rejects stale results by id. Let me quickly confirm the request id uniqueness — `make_request` presumably uses a monotonically increasing id. Out of scope.

Also, `fail_oldest` for malformed replies: if a worker's reply is malformed (e.g., JSON parse fails), the OLDEST request is failed. But with a multi-message queue, the malformed reply may correspond to a LATER request (e.g., reply for request 2 arrives malformed while request 1 is still pending — then failing request 1 is wrong, it will be regenerated needlessly; but request 2 remains pending forever!). Wait — malformed reply means the worker's serial queue advanced past the malformed message, meaning the worker processed that message... The reply protocol: each message produces exactly one reply. If the reply for request 2 is malformed, the worker already moved on to request 3. Failing the oldest (request 1) when the malformed reply was for request 2 means request 2 is never completed nor failed → the chunk stays pending forever → the engine never retries it (it's in `self.pending`). Actually the engine's pending map keeps it; issue_requests only issues for chunks NOT in pending. So chunk 2 would be stuck forever unless the player moves away (pending.retain drops out-of-footprint entries). That's a **lost-reply edge case**: a malformed reply fails the WRONG request (oldest), leaving the actual request stuck. The comment in generation_worker_requests.rs:97-99 claims "a malformed response belongs to its oldest outstanding request" — true only if replies arrive in order (they do, per-worker serial queue) AND each message yields exactly one reply. If the worker processed messages 1..3 and the reply for 3 is malformed but replies for 1,2 were lost (e.g., transfer failure)... edge case. Realistically: replies are serial per worker, so if reply 2 is malformed, reply 1 was already delivered (in order). So the oldest outstanding at the time the malformed reply arrives IS the one that produced it — assuming exactly-once replies. But consider: worker crashes AFTER processing message 2 (generating successfully) but before posting; error event drains both 1 and 2. Fine.

What if the reply for message 2 arrives malformed while message 1's reply is also malformed? Both fail oldest → message 1's reply malformed → fail request 1 (oldest) — but the malformed reply might be for request 2 if reply 1 was never generated... can't happen: replies are generated in order.

BUT there is a genuine bug case: **`worker_generate` returning data that fails `decode_chunk_payload`** → Malformed → fail_oldest. If the worker queue has requests 1 and 2, and the reply for request 1 fails decode, fail_oldest fails request 1 — correct. Then request 2's reply arrives — finish_exact(request 2) — correct. OK, the "oldest" heuristic is right under serial, exactly-once-reply assumptions.

The REAL issue: **a malformed `done` reply for a request that was already retried** — no wait, stale replies are dropped by finish_exact.

OK. Let me also verify `ChunkRequest.is_same_request` includes reality (prior analysis showed ports.rs:626-632: request_id, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality — yes).

    1| //! Complete analytic-fixture upload shared by the surface and raymarch paths.
    2| //!
    3| //! A texture is used instead of fragment-uniform arrays for two reasons: the
    4| //! physical scene is not silently truncated to a camera-ranked slot budget,
    5| //! and the large raymarch chunk table no longer competes with lights for the
    6| //! WebGL minimum uniform-vector allowance. Each light occupies three RGBA32F
    7| //! texels in the layout decoded by `shaders/sample_scene_lights.rs`.
    8| 
    9| use wasm_bindgen::JsValue;
   10| use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlTexture};
   11| 
   12| use crate::application::ports::LightSource;
   13| 
   14| const PREFERRED_ROW_TEXELS: i32 = 1024;
   15| const TEXELS_PER_LIGHT: usize = 3;
   16| 
   17| pub struct SceneLightTexture {
   18|     texture: WebGlTexture,
   19|     width: i32,
   20|     maximum_size: i32,
   21|     staging: Vec<f32>,
   22|     last_lights: Vec<LightSource>,
   23|     uploaded: bool,
   24| }
   25| 
   26| impl SceneLightTexture {
   27|     pub fn create(gl: &Gl) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
   28|         let texture = gl
   29|             .create_texture()
   30|             .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("failed to create scene-light texture"))?;
   31|         let maximum_size = gl
   32|             .get_parameter(Gl::MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE)?
   33|             .as_f64()
   34|             .unwrap_or(0.0) as i32;
   35|         if maximum_size < 1 {
   36|             return Err(JsValue::from_str("WebGL reported no 2-D texture capacity"));
   37|         }
   38|         let width = PREFERRED_ROW_TEXELS.min(maximum_size);
   39|         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&texture));
   40|         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
   41|         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
   42|         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_S, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
   43|         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_T, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
   44|         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, None);
   45|         Ok(Self {
   46|             texture,
   47|             width,
   48|             maximum_size,
   49|             staging: Vec::new(),
   50|             last_lights: Vec::new(),
   51|             uploaded: false,
   52|         })
   53|     }
   54| 
   55|     /// Replaces the immutable frame snapshot and returns its exact light count.
   56|     pub fn upload(&mut self, gl: &Gl, lights: &[LightSource]) -> Result<i32, JsValue> {
   57|         if self.uploaded && self.last_lights == lights {
   58|             return Ok(lights.len().min(i32::MAX as usize) as i32);
   59|         }
   60|         let texel_count = lights.len().max(1) * TEXELS_PER_LIGHT;
   61|         let rows = (texel_count as i32 + self.width - 1) / self.width;
   62|         if rows > self.maximum_size || lights.len() > i32::MAX as usize {
   63|             return Err(JsValue::from_str(
   64|                 "resident fixture list exceeds the WebGL scene-light texture",
   65|             ));
   66|         }
   67| 
   68|         self.staging.clear();
   69|         self.staging
   70|             .resize(self.width as usize * rows as usize * 4, 0.0);
   71|         for (index, light) in lights.iter().enumerate() {
   72|             let offset = index * TEXELS_PER_LIGHT * 4;
   73|             self.staging[offset..offset + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.position);
   74|             self.staging[offset + 3] = light.kind as u8 as f32;
   75|             self.staging[offset + 4..offset + 7].copy_from_slice(&light.color);
   76|             self.staging[offset + 7] = light.intensity;
   77|             self.staging[offset + 8] = light.radius;
   78|             self.staging[offset + 9] = light.half_size[0];
   79|             self.staging[offset + 10] = light.half_size[1];
   80|         }
   81| 
   82|         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&self.texture));
   83|         gl.pixel_storei(Gl::UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, 4);
   84|         let view = js_sys::Float32Array::from(self.staging.as_slice());
   85|         gl.tex_image_2d_with_i32_and_i32_and_i32_and_format_and_type_and_opt_array_buffer_view(
   86|             Gl::TEXTURE_2D,
   87|             0,
   88|             Gl::RGBA32F as i32,
   89|             self.width,
   90|             rows,
   91|             0,
   92|             Gl::RGBA,
   93|             Gl::FLOAT,
   94|             Some(&view),
   95|         )?;
   96|         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, None);
   97|         self.last_lights.clear();
   98|         self.last_lights.extend_from_slice(lights);
   99|         self.uploaded = true;
  100|         Ok(lights.len() as i32)
  101|     }
  102| 
  103|     pub fn bind(&self, gl: &Gl) {
  104|         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&self.texture));
  105|     }
  106| 
  107|     pub fn width(&self) -> i32 {
  108|         self.width
  109|     }
  110| }
    1| //! Conservative visibility tests shared by the raster drivers.
    2| 
    3| use crate::application::ports::FrameParams;
    4| 
    5| /// Shared raster far plane and conservative culling boundary (world units).
    6| /// Beer--Lambert fog never becomes exactly opaque, so projection and culling
    7| /// must use the identical distance rather than hiding a ten-unit mismatch.
    8| pub const MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE: f32 = 110.0;
    9| 
   10| /// Sphere visibility: inside the draw distance and not entirely behind the
   11| /// camera plane. Returns the squared distance for near-to-far sorting, or
   12| /// `None` when culled. Deliberately conservative (no side-plane frustum
   13| /// test): a false "visible" costs a few draws, a false cull costs a hole
   14| /// in the world.
   15| pub fn sphere_visible(
   16|     center: [f32; 3],
   17|     radius: f32,
   18|     frame: &FrameParams,
   19|     max_draw_distance: f32,
   20| ) -> Option<f32> {
   21|     let to = [
   22|         center[0] - frame.camera_pos[0],
   23|         center[1] - frame.camera_pos[1],
   24|         center[2] - frame.camera_pos[2],
   25|     ];
   26|     let distance2 = to[0] * to[0] + to[1] * to[1] + to[2] * to[2];
   27|     // Cull only when the *whole sphere* lies beyond the distance boundary.
   28|     // Testing the center against `max_draw_distance` cuts chunks/cells that
   29|     // still intersect the visible volume and creates a hard pop at the fog
   30|     // edge.
   31|     let farthest_visible_center = max_draw_distance + radius;
   32|     if distance2 > farthest_visible_center * farthest_visible_center {
   33|         return None;
   34|     }
   35|     let (sp, cp) = frame.pitch.sin_cos();
   36|     let (sy, cy) = frame.yaw.sin_cos();
   37|     let forward = [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy];
   38|     let dot = to[0] * forward[0] + to[1] * forward[1] + to[2] * forward[2];
   39|     if dot >= -radius {
   40|         Some(distance2)
   41|     } else {
   42|         None
   43|     }
   44| }
   45| 
   46| /// Center + bounding-sphere radius of a chunk from its origin and local
   47| /// bounds-max — the shape both mesh and splat chunk records share.
   48| pub fn chunk_bounding_sphere(origin: [f32; 3], bounds_max: [f32; 3]) -> ([f32; 3], f32) {
   49|     let center = [
   50|         origin[0] + bounds_max[0] * 0.5,
   51|         origin[1] + bounds_max[1] * 0.5,
   52|         origin[2] + bounds_max[2] * 0.5,
   53|     ];
   54|     let radius = (bounds_max[0] * bounds_max[0]
   55|         + bounds_max[1] * bounds_max[1]
   56|         + bounds_max[2] * bounds_max[2])
   57|         .sqrt()
   58|         * 0.5;
   59|     (center, radius)
   60| }
   61| 
   62| /// Conservative AABB vs. Frustum test with safety inflation margin (0.5 voxel).
   63| ///
   64| /// # Rationale
   65| /// Prevents false culls on side view boundaries while rejecting chunks strictly outside
   66| /// the extended camera view cone.
   67| pub fn aabb_frustum_visible(
   68|     origin: [f32; 3],
   69|     bounds_max: [f32; 3],
   70|     frame: &FrameParams,
   71|     margin: f32,
   72| ) -> bool {
   73|     let (center, radius) = chunk_bounding_sphere(origin, bounds_max);
   74|     let inflated_radius = radius + margin;
   75|     sphere_visible(center, inflated_radius, frame, MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE).is_some()
   76| }
   77| 
   78| /// Signed world-space distance from a sphere center to one side plane of the
   79| /// perspective frustum, positive meaning inside. `axis` is `right` or `up`;
   80| /// `tan_half` is the tangent of that axis's half-angle (horizontal uses

Confirmed upload_scene_lights.rs: `self.last_lights == lights` — full O(L) comparison per frame; `staging.resize(width*rows*4)` reallocates each time the count changes — only when light list changes. Fine. Note the texture upload happens per frame only when light list changed. Good design.

Now, `visibility.rs` — `sphere_visible`, `chunk_bounding_sphere`, `aabb_frustum_visible`, `frustum_side_planes_visible` — all O(1). Fine.

    1| //! Per-frame raymarch submission.
    2| //!
    3| //! Each helper uploads one coherent piece of frame state. The final
    4| //! [`RendererPort::draw`] reads as the pipeline order: timer, target, program,
    5| //! camera, lighting, chunks, atlas, fullscreen draw.
    6| 
    7| use web_sys::WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl;
    8| 
    9| use crate::application::atlas::MAX_CHUNKS;
   10| use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, FrameParams, RendererPort};
   11| use crate::application::rendering::encode_display_color;
   12| use crate::drivers::gl::cluster_scene_lights::{LightRange, append_lights_reaching_bounds};
   13| use crate::drivers::gl::upload_scene_lights::SceneLightTexture;
   14| 
   15| use super::{Uniforms, WebGl2Renderer, fov_tan};
   16| 
   17| /// Reused uniform arrays. Their capacity is fixed at construction so steady
   18| /// frame submission performs no heap allocations.
   19| pub(super) struct ChunkUniformBuffers {
   20|     origins: Vec<f32>,
   21|     roots: Vec<i32>,
   22|     sizes: Vec<f32>,
   23|     voxel_sizes: Vec<f32>,
   24|     depths: Vec<i32>,
   25|     light_first: Vec<i32>,
   26|     light_counts: Vec<i32>,
   27| }
   28| 
   29| impl ChunkUniformBuffers {
   30|     pub(super) fn with_capacity(chunks: usize) -> Self {
   31|         Self {
   32|             origins: Vec::with_capacity(chunks * 3),
   33|             roots: Vec::with_capacity(chunks),
   34|             sizes: Vec::with_capacity(chunks),
   35|             voxel_sizes: Vec::with_capacity(chunks),
   36|             depths: Vec::with_capacity(chunks),
   37|             light_first: Vec::with_capacity(chunks),
   38|             light_counts: Vec::with_capacity(chunks),
   39|         }
   40|     }
   41| }
   42| 
   43| #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
   44| struct CameraBasis {
   45|     right: [f32; 3],
   46|     up: [f32; 3],
   47|     forward: [f32; 3],
   48| }
   49| 
   50| fn camera_basis(frame: &FrameParams) -> CameraBasis {
   51|     let (sin_pitch, cos_pitch) = frame.pitch.sin_cos();
   52|     let (sin_yaw, cos_yaw) = frame.yaw.sin_cos();
   53|     CameraBasis {
   54|         right: [cos_yaw, 0.0, -sin_yaw],
   55|         up: [sin_pitch * sin_yaw, cos_pitch, sin_pitch * cos_yaw],
   56|         forward: [-cos_pitch * sin_yaw, sin_pitch, -cos_pitch * cos_yaw],
   57|     }
   58| }
   59| 
   60| fn clear_target(gl: &Gl, frame: &FrameParams, width: i32, height: i32) {
   61|     gl.viewport(0, 0, width, height);
   62|     let environment = frame.environment;
   63|     let atmosphere = if environment.outdoor {
   64|         environment.sky_color
   65|     } else {
   66|         environment.fog_color
   67|     };
   68|     let clear = encode_display_color(atmosphere);
   69|     gl.clear_color(clear[0], clear[1], clear[2], 1.0);
   70|     gl.clear(Gl::COLOR_BUFFER_BIT);
   71| }
   72| 
   73| fn upload_camera(gl: &Gl, uniforms: &Uniforms, frame: &FrameParams, width: i32, height: i32) {
   74|     gl.uniform3f(
   75|         uniforms.camera_position.as_ref(),
   76|         frame.camera_pos[0],
   77|         frame.camera_pos[1],
   78|         frame.camera_pos[2],
   79|     );
   80|     let basis = camera_basis(frame);
   81|     gl.uniform3fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.cam_right.as_ref(), &basis.right);
   82|     gl.uniform3fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.cam_up.as_ref(), &basis.up);
   83|     gl.uniform3fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.cam_forward.as_ref(), &basis.forward);
   84|     gl.uniform1f(
   85|         uniforms.aspect.as_ref(),
   86|         width as f32 / height.max(1) as f32,
   87|     );
   88|     gl.uniform1f(uniforms.fov_tan.as_ref(), fov_tan());
   89| }
   90| 
   91| fn upload_environment(gl: &Gl, uniforms: &Uniforms, frame: &FrameParams) {
   92|     let environment = frame.environment;
   93|     gl.uniform1i(
   94|         uniforms.outdoor.as_ref(),
   95|         if environment.outdoor { 1 } else { 0 },
   96|     );
   97|     gl.uniform3fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.sky_color.as_ref(), &environment.sky_color);
   98|     gl.uniform3fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.fog_color.as_ref(), &environment.fog_color);
   99|     gl.uniform1f(uniforms.ambient_scale.as_ref(), environment.ambient_scale);
  100|     gl.uniform1f(uniforms.fog_density.as_ref(), environment.fog_density);
  101|     gl.uniform1f(uniforms.fog_start.as_ref(), environment.fog_start);
  102| }
  103| 
  104| fn bind_scene_lights(gl: &Gl, uniforms: &Uniforms, texture: &SceneLightTexture) {
  105|     gl.active_texture(Gl::TEXTURE1);
  106|     texture.bind(gl);
  107|     gl.uniform1i(uniforms.scene_light_texture.as_ref(), 1);
  108|     gl.uniform1i(uniforms.scene_light_texture_width.as_ref(), texture.width());
  109| }

  111| fn cluster_scene_lights(
  112|     frame: &FrameParams,
  113|     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
  114| ) -> (Vec<crate::application::ports::LightSource>, Vec<LightRange>) {
  115|     let mut clustered = Vec::new();
  116|     let ranges = chunks
  117|         .iter()
  118|         .take(MAX_CHUNKS)
  119|         .map(|chunk| {
  120|             let bounds_max = [
  121|                 chunk.origin[0] + chunk.world_size,
  122|                 chunk.origin[1] + chunk.world_size,
  123|                 chunk.origin[2] + chunk.world_size,
  124|             ];
  125|             append_lights_reaching_bounds(
  126|                 frame.active_scene_lights(),
  127|                 chunk.origin,
  128|                 bounds_max,
  129|                 &mut clustered,
  130|             )
  131|         })
  132|         .collect();
  133|     (clustered, ranges)
  134| }
  135| 
  136| fn upload_dynamic_lights(gl: &Gl, uniforms: &Uniforms, frame: &FrameParams) {
  137|     let lights = frame.active_dynamic_lights();
  138|     let mut position_radius = [0.0f32; 16];
  139|     let mut color_intensity = [0.0f32; 16];
  140|     for (index, light) in lights.iter().enumerate() {
  141|         let offset = index * 4;
  142|         position_radius[offset..offset + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.position);
  143|         position_radius[offset + 3] = light.radius;
  144|         color_intensity[offset..offset + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.color);
  145|         color_intensity[offset + 3] = light.intensity;
  146|     }
  147|     gl.uniform1i(uniforms.dynamic_light_count.as_ref(), lights.len() as i32);
  148|     gl.uniform4fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.dynamic_pos_radius.as_ref(), &position_radius);
  149|     gl.uniform4fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.dynamic_color_intensity.as_ref(), &color_intensity);
  150| }
  151| 
  152| fn upload_chunks(
  153|     gl: &Gl,
  154|     uniforms: &Uniforms,
  155|     buffers: &mut ChunkUniformBuffers,
  156|     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
  157|     light_ranges: &[LightRange],
  158| ) {
  159|     let chunks = &chunks[..chunks.len().min(MAX_CHUNKS)];
  160|     gl.uniform1i(uniforms.num_chunks.as_ref(), chunks.len() as i32);
  161|     if chunks.is_empty() {
  162|         return;
  163|     }
  164| 
  165|     buffers.origins.clear();
  166|     buffers.roots.clear();
  167|     buffers.sizes.clear();
  168|     buffers.voxel_sizes.clear();
  169|     buffers.depths.clear();
  170|     buffers.light_first.clear();
  171|     buffers.light_counts.clear();
  172|     for (index, chunk) in chunks.iter().enumerate() {
  173|         buffers.origins.extend_from_slice(&chunk.origin);
  174|         buffers.roots.push(chunk.root_index);
  175|         buffers.sizes.push(chunk.world_size);
  176|         buffers.voxel_sizes.push(chunk.voxel_size);
  177|         buffers.depths.push(chunk.svo_depth as i32);
  178|         let range = light_ranges
  179|             .get(index)
  180|             .copied()
  181|             .unwrap_or(LightRange { first: 0, count: 0 });
  182|         buffers.light_first.push(range.first);
  183|         buffers.light_counts.push(range.count);
  184|     }
  185|     gl.uniform3fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.chunk_origins.as_ref(), &buffers.origins);
  186|     gl.uniform1iv_with_i32_array(uniforms.chunk_root_indices.as_ref(), &buffers.roots);
  187|     gl.uniform1fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.chunk_world_sizes.as_ref(), &buffers.sizes);
  188|     gl.uniform1fv_with_f32_array(uniforms.chunk_voxel_sizes.as_ref(), &buffers.voxel_sizes);
  189|     gl.uniform1iv_with_i32_array(uniforms.chunk_depths.as_ref(), &buffers.depths);
  190|     gl.uniform1iv_with_i32_array(uniforms.chunk_light_first.as_ref(), &buffers.light_first);
  191|     gl.uniform1iv_with_i32_array(uniforms.chunk_light_counts.as_ref(), &buffers.light_counts);
  192| }
  193| 
  194| impl RendererPort for WebGl2Renderer {
  195|     fn upload_atlas(&mut self, texels: &[u32]) {
  196|         self.atlas.replace(&self.gl, texels);
  197|     }
  198| 
  199|     fn upload_atlas_rows(&mut self, first_row: u32, texels: &[u32]) -> bool {
  200|         self.atlas.update_rows(&self.gl, first_row, texels)
  201|     }
  202| 
  203|     fn upload_brick_voxels(&mut self, words: &[u32]) {
  204|         self.bricks.replace(&self.gl, words);
  205|     }
  206| 
  207|     fn upload_brick_voxels_rows(&mut self, first_row: u32, words: &[u32]) -> bool {
  208|         self.bricks.update_rows(&self.gl, first_row, words)
  209|     }
  210| 
  211|     fn draw(&mut self, frame: &FrameParams, chunks: &[ChunkDraw]) {
  212|         let toggles = crate::get_render_toggles();
  213|         self.timer.poll(&self.gl);
  214|         let timer_started = self.timer.begin(&self.gl, false);
  215|         let (clustered_lights, mut light_ranges) = cluster_scene_lights(frame, chunks);
  216|         if self
  217|             .scene_lights
  218|             .upload(&self.gl, &clustered_lights)
  219|             .is_err()
  220|         {
  221|             for range in &mut light_ranges {
  222|                 range.count = 0;
  223|             }
  224|         }
  225| 
  226|         {
  227|             let gl = &self.gl;
  228|             clear_target(gl, frame, self.width, self.height);
  229|             gl.use_program(Some(&self.program));
  230|             upload_camera(gl, &self.uniforms, frame, self.width, self.height);
  231|             gl.uniform1i(
  232|                 self.uniforms.flashlight.as_ref(),
  233|                 if frame.flashlight { 1 } else { 0 },
  234|             );
  235|             gl.uniform1i(
  236|                 self.uniforms.front_to_back.as_ref(),
  237|                 if toggles.front_to_back { 1 } else { 0 },
  238|             );
  239|             gl.uniform1i(
  240|                 self.uniforms.empty_space_skip.as_ref(),
  241|                 if toggles.empty_space_skip { 1 } else { 0 },
  242|             );
  243|             gl.uniform1i(
  244|                 self.uniforms.direct_visibility.as_ref(),
  245|                 if toggles.shadow_pass { 1 } else { 0 },
  246|             );
  247|             // OPTIMIZATION (rt_dither): optional noise hides color banding.
  248|             gl.uniform1i(
  249|                 self.uniforms.dither.as_ref(),
  250|                 if toggles.dither { 1 } else { 0 },
  251|             );
  252|             upload_environment(gl, &self.uniforms, frame);
  253|             bind_scene_lights(gl, &self.uniforms, &self.scene_lights);
  254|             upload_dynamic_lights(gl, &self.uniforms, frame);
  255|             upload_chunks(
  256|                 gl,
  257|                 &self.uniforms,
  258|                 &mut self.chunk_uniforms,
  259|                 chunks,
  260|                 &light_ranges,
  261|             );
  262| 
  263|             gl.active_texture(Gl::TEXTURE0);
  264|             self.atlas.bind(gl);
  265|             gl.uniform1i(self.uniforms.node_texture.as_ref(), 0);
  266|             gl.active_texture(Gl::TEXTURE2);
  267|             self.bricks.bind(gl);
  268|             gl.uniform1i(self.uniforms.brick_texture.as_ref(), 2);
  269|             gl.bind_vertex_array(Some(&self.quad.vao));
  270|             gl.draw_arrays(Gl::TRIANGLES, 0, 6);
  271|             gl.bind_vertex_array(None);
  272|         }
  273| 
  274|         self.timer.end(&self.gl, timer_started);
  275|     }
  276| }

    1| //! Shared GLSL chunks — snippets spliced into more than one shader so the
    2| //! engine has exactly one definition of each cross-cutting effect.
    3| //!
    4| //! Shader sources are assembled at startup by `format!` concatenation (a
    5| //! few string copies once per program link — nothing per frame). Each chunk
    6| //! is a self-contained set of GLSL functions/consts with no `uniform`
    7| //! declarations, so any stage can include it.
    8| 
    9| use std::fmt::Write;
   10| 
   11| use vackrooms::adapters::material_palette::MATERIAL_VISUALS;
   12| 
   13| /// The flashlight spotlight cone — **GLSL mirror of the single spec in
   14| /// `adapters::cpu_splatter::flashlight`** (inner/outer angle, finite-range
   15| /// inverse-square transport, lamp offset, and tint). A tuning change there
   16| /// must be mirrored here.
   17| ///
   18| /// Shape: smoothstep between an inner cone (full strength, 11°) and an
   19| /// outer cone (zero, 24°) around the camera forward axis. Transport uses a
   20| /// compact-support inverse-square law and a strict Lambert receiver cosine.
   21| pub const SPOT_CONE_GLSL: &str = r#"
   22| // --- flashlight cone (spec: adapters/cpu_splatter/flashlight.rs) ---
   23| const float SPOT_INNER_COS = 0.9816272; // cos(11 deg)
   24| const float SPOT_OUTER_COS = 0.9135455; // cos(24 deg)
   25| const float SPOT_RANGE_END = 14.0;
   26| const float SPOT_INTENSITY = 32.0;
   27| const float SPOT_MIN_DISTANCE = 0.25;
   28| const float SPOT_INV_PI = 0.3183098861837907;
   29| const vec3  SPOT_TINT = vec3(1.0, 0.91, 0.72);
   30| 
   31| // The hand-held lamp sits slightly forward of and below the eye.
   32| vec3 spotLampPos(vec3 camPos, vec3 camForward) {
   33|     return camPos + camForward * 0.18 - vec3(0.0, 0.10, 0.0);
   34| }
   35| 
   36| // Angular falloff: 1 inside the inner cone, 0 outside the outer.
   37| float spotCone(vec3 beam, vec3 camForward) {
   38|     return smoothstep(SPOT_OUTER_COS, SPOT_INNER_COS, dot(beam, camForward));
   39| }
   40| 
   41| // Finite-range inverse-square transport. The compact window and its first
   42| // derivative both reach zero at RANGE_END, so the beam has no hard rim.
   43| float spotAttenuation(float dist) {
   44|     if (!(dist >= 0.0) || dist >= SPOT_RANGE_END) return 0.0;
   45|     float normalizedSquared = (dist * dist) / (SPOT_RANGE_END * SPOT_RANGE_END);
   46|     float window = max(1.0 - normalizedSquared * normalizedSquared, 0.0);
   47|     float minimumSquared = SPOT_MIN_DISTANCE * SPOT_MIN_DISTANCE;
   48|     return (window * window) / max(dist * dist, minimumSquared);
   49| }
   50| 
   51| // Lambertian reflected-radiance factor at a surface point with normal N.
   52| // The CPU contract evaluates irradiance first and multiplies albedo / PI;
   53| // folding 1/PI here preserves that exact composition at GPU call sites.
   54| vec3 spotBeam(vec3 camPos, vec3 camForward, vec3 surfacePos, vec3 N) {
   55|     vec3 lamp = spotLampPos(camPos, camForward);
   56|     vec3 toSurf = surfacePos - lamp;
   57|     float dist = length(toSurf);
   58|     vec3 beam = toSurf / max(dist, 1e-4);
   59|     float cone = spotCone(beam, camForward);
   60|     float attenuation = spotAttenuation(dist);
   61|     float facing = max(-dot(beam, N), 0.0);
   62|     return SPOT_TINT * (SPOT_INTENSITY * SPOT_INV_PI * cone * attenuation * facing);
   63| }
   64| "#;
   65| 
   66| /// Builds the palette lookup shared by both WebGL rasterizers. Shader source
   67| /// is assembled once at startup, so deriving it here removes a hand-maintained
   68| /// GLSL mirror without adding frame-time work.
   69| pub fn material_color_glsl() -> String {
   70|     let mut source = String::from("vec3 materialColor(float material) {\n");
   71|     for (material, visual) in MATERIAL_VISUALS.iter().enumerate() {
   72|         let red = (visual.color >> 16) & 0xff;
   73|         let green = (visual.color >> 8) & 0xff;
   74|         let blue = visual.color & 0xff;
   75|         writeln!(
   76|             source,
   77|             "    if (material < {:.1}) return vec3({red}.0, {green}.0, {blue}.0) / 255.0;",
   78|             material as f32 + 0.5,
   79|         )
   80|         .expect("writing to a String cannot fail");
   81|     }
   82|     source.push_str("    return vec3(0.0);\n}\n");
   83|     source
   84| }

  161|         let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&path);

    1| //! Intersect the camera ray with resident chunks and optionally order entries.
    2| 
    3| pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
    4| int collectOrderedChunkIntervals(
    5|     vec3 rayDirection,
    6|     out ChunkInterval intervals[25]
    7| ) {
    8|     int intervalCount = 0;
    9|     for (int chunkIndex = 0; chunkIndex < uNumChunks; ++chunkIndex) {
   10|         vec3 localOrigin = uCameraPosition - uChunkOrigins[chunkIndex];
   11|         RayBoxHit box = intersectBox(
   12|             localOrigin,
   13|             rayDirection,
   14|             vec3(0.0),
   15|             vec3(uChunkWorldSizes[chunkIndex])
   16|         );
   17|         if (!box.hit) continue;
   18| 
   19|         int insertion = intervalCount;
   20|         if (uFrontToBackEnabled == 1) {
   21|             while (insertion > 0 && intervals[insertion - 1].entry > box.entry) {
   22|                 intervals[insertion] = intervals[insertion - 1];
   23|                 insertion--;
   24|             }
   25|         }
   26|         intervals[insertion] = ChunkInterval(
   27|             chunkIndex, box.entry, box.exit, box.entryNormal
   28|         );
   29|         intervalCount++;
   30|     }
   31|     return intervalCount;
   32| }

    1| //! Trace every candidate chunk interval and retain the nearest solid voxel.
    2| 
    3| pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
    4| VoxelHit selectNearestVoxelHit(
    5|     vec3 rayDirection,
    6|     ChunkInterval intervals[25],
    7|     int intervalCount,
    8|     out int closestChunkIndex
    9| ) {
   10|     VoxelHit closest = VoxelHit(
   11|         false, TRACE_INFINITY, vec3(0.0), 0u, 0u, 0u
   12|     );
   13|     closestChunkIndex = -1;
   14|     for (int intervalIndex = 0; intervalIndex < intervalCount; ++intervalIndex) {
   15|         ChunkInterval interval = intervals[intervalIndex];
   16|         // Sorted traversal may stop only after every remaining AABB begins
   17|         // beyond the nearest solid hit. Breaking after the first hit is wrong
   18|         // because power-of-two padded chunk boxes overlap.
   19|         if (uFrontToBackEnabled == 1 && interval.entry >= closest.distance) break;
   20| 
   21|         int chunkIndex = interval.chunkIndex;
   22|         vec3 localOrigin = uCameraPosition - uChunkOrigins[chunkIndex];
   23|         RayBoxHit box = RayBoxHit(
   24|             true, interval.entry, interval.exit, interval.entryNormal
   25|         );
   26|         VoxelHit candidate = traceChunk(
   27|             localOrigin,
   28|             rayDirection,
   29|             uChunkRootIndices[chunkIndex],
   30|             uChunkWorldSizes[chunkIndex],
   31|             uChunkVoxelSizes[chunkIndex],
   32|             uChunkDepths[chunkIndex],
   33|             box
   34|         );
   35|         if (candidate.hit && candidate.distance < closest.distance) {
   36|             closest = candidate;
   37|             closestChunkIndex = chunkIndex;
   38|         }
   39|     }
   40|     return closest;
   41| }

Confirmed. Now the WebGPU config.rs — raymarch profile (chunk counts, steps, direct visibility default). And evaluate_scene_lighting.rs (surface GLSL light loop). And sample_scene_lights.rs.
    1| //! Direct-light equations shared by the surface and voxel-hit shaders.
    2| //!
    3| //! Rectangular emitters use deterministic 2×2 Gauss quadrature over their
    4| //! physical area. Point lights use the same finite-range inverse-square law
    5| //! without the area integral. This is intentionally compact and diagnosable;
    6| //! shadow visibility is an explicit input owned by the caller.
    7| 
    8| pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
    9| const float PI = 3.14159265358979323846;
   10| const int LIGHT_POINT = 0;
   11| const int LIGHT_CEILING_PANEL = 1;
   12| const int LIGHT_STRIP = 2;
   13| const int LIGHT_EMERGENCY = 3;
   14| 
   15| float finiteRangeInverseSquare(float distanceSquared, float range) {
   16|     if (!(range > 0.0) || !(distanceSquared >= 0.0)) return 0.0;
   17|     float rangeSquared = range * range;
   18|     float normalizedSquared = distanceSquared / rangeSquared;
   19|     float window = max(1.0 - normalizedSquared * normalizedSquared, 0.0);
   20|     return (window * window) / max(distanceSquared, 0.04);
   21| }
   22| 
   23| float receiverCosine(vec3 normal, vec3 surfaceToLight) {
   24|     return max(dot(normal, surfaceToLight), 0.0);
   25| }
   26| 
   27| float emitterCosine(int kind, vec3 surfaceToLight) {
   28|     if (kind == LIGHT_POINT) return 1.0;
   29|     // Rectangular fixtures lie in XZ and point down. `surfaceToLight.y` is
   30|     // positive exactly when the receiver is in their emitting hemisphere.
   31|     return max(surfaceToLight.y, 0.0);
   32| }
   33| 
   34| vec3 evaluatePointLight(
   35|     vec3 surfacePosition,
   36|     vec3 normal,
   37|     vec3 lightPosition,
   38|     vec3 lightColor,
   39|     float range,
   40|     float intensity
   41| ) {
   42|     vec3 delta = lightPosition - surfacePosition;
   43|     float distanceSquared = dot(delta, delta);
   44|     vec3 surfaceToLight = delta * inversesqrt(max(distanceSquared, 1e-8));
   45|     float geometry = receiverCosine(normal, surfaceToLight);
   46|     return max(lightColor, vec3(0.0)) * max(intensity, 0.0)
   47|         * finiteRangeInverseSquare(distanceSquared, range) * geometry;
   48| }
   49| 
   50| vec3 evaluateRectangleLight(
   51|     vec3 surfacePosition,
   52|     vec3 normal,
   53|     vec3 lightPosition,
   54|     vec2 halfSize,
   55|     vec3 lightColor,
   56|     float range,
   57|     float intensity,
   58|     int kind
   59| ) {
   60|     const float GAUSS = 0.5773502691896258;
   61|     vec2 offsets[4] = vec2[](
   62|         vec2(-GAUSS, -GAUSS), vec2(GAUSS, -GAUSS),
   63|         vec2(-GAUSS,  GAUSS), vec2(GAUSS,  GAUSS)
   64|     );
   65|     vec3 integral = vec3(0.0);
   66|     for (int sampleIndex = 0; sampleIndex < 4; ++sampleIndex) {
   67|         vec2 offset = offsets[sampleIndex] * halfSize;
   68|         vec3 samplePosition = lightPosition + vec3(offset.x, 0.0, offset.y);
   69|         vec3 delta = samplePosition - surfacePosition;
   70|         float distanceSquared = dot(delta, delta);
   71|         vec3 surfaceToLight = delta * inversesqrt(max(distanceSquared, 1e-8));
   72|         float geometry = receiverCosine(normal, surfaceToLight)
   73|             * emitterCosine(kind, surfaceToLight);
   74|         integral += finiteRangeInverseSquare(distanceSquared, range) * geometry;
   75|     }
   76|     float area = 4.0 * max(halfSize.x, 0.0) * max(halfSize.y, 0.0);
   77|     if (!(area > 0.0)) return vec3(0.0);
   78|     return max(lightColor, vec3(0.0)) * max(intensity, 0.0)
   79|         * area * (integral * 0.25);
   80| }
   81| 
   82| vec3 evaluateSceneLight(
   83|     vec3 surfacePosition,
   84|     vec3 normal,
   85|     vec3 lightPosition,
   86|     vec2 halfSize,
   87|     vec3 lightColor,
   88|     float range,
   89|     float intensity,
   90|     int kind
   91| ) {
   92|     if (kind == LIGHT_POINT) {
   93|         return evaluatePointLight(
   94|             surfacePosition, normal, lightPosition, lightColor, range, intensity
   95|         );
   96|     }
   97|     return evaluateRectangleLight(
   98|         surfacePosition, normal, lightPosition, halfSize,
   99|         lightColor, range, intensity, kind
  100|     );
  101| }

Confirmed the GLSL surface path evaluates 4 Gauss samples per rectangle light per fragment. And the WebGL2 surface fragment shader loops over the clustered range (uLightFirst/uLightCount) — the clustering bounds it, but with no cap on count per chunk (per the test: 40 lights reaching a chunk = 40×4=160 evaluations per fragment). But real-world: MAX_SCENE_LIGHTS=16 fixtures in frame for WebGL2 raster (select_lights truncates to 16), so the cluster can't exceed 16 per chunk for raster. For raymarch WebGL2, the clustered list has no cap (all frame lights ≤ 48).

Wait — MAX_SCENE_LIGHTS = 16 is for the uniform arrays (lights.rs MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS). But the scene light TEXTURE for raymarch has no cap (up to 48 per frame). For the surface/splat WebGL2 raster drivers: do they use select_lights (16 slots) or the scene light texture? Let me check splat_webgl/draw.rs and surfel_webgl/draw.rs and surface_webgl's shader usage. The surface GLSL fragment interface (render_world_surfaces/mod.rs) has both `uLightCount/uLightFirst + uSceneLightTexture` (clustered texture range) AND uDynamicPosRadius[4]. The upload path: `renderer.scene_lights.upload(&renderer.gl, &clustered_lights)` — the clustered lights (from append_lights_reaching_bounds over frame.active_scene_lights, up to 48) are uploaded to the texture, and per-chunk ranges index into it. So WebGL2 surface: fragment loops over the chunk's clustered lights from the texture, up to 48 per chunk worst case (a big cluster). OK so it's O(P × L_c × 4) with L_c = per-chunk cluster size.
